Having removed the two blades of *barhis* grass and having taken up the [sacrificial cake], he rises with the formula: "For heaven thee! For the intermediate region thee! For the earth thee! He goes out by the eastern door with the formula: "O Indra, strike away the mind of him who hates us; strike away him who seeks to overcome us; strike away him who acts as our enemy."

Having approached, he offers [the oblation] into the *āhavanīya* fire while the sacrificer maintains contact [with him], saying: "For breath thee! For out-breath thee! For diffused breath thee! For the existent thee! For the non-existent thee! For the waters thee, for the plants thee! For all beings thee! From whom [proceed] creatures that are unimpaired."

The reading of the MSS of the *BaudhŚS.*, namely M, J, and the *Mantramālā*, is the same as that of BI. The spelling *-kkh-* appears to occur after a vowel due to orthographic convention; cf. Goto, 126, n. 143. [TSw: *akhidrā*; TSgols: *akkhidrā*; BI: *askhidrā*] "They were born without flaw. To that Prajāpati, the all-encompassing, the luminous, I offer you, the luminous one, Svāhā! (7.4:205.2). Then he pours its rinsing water inside the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
"One should give either an excellent cow or an excellent bull," so said Baudhāyana; "twelve heifers," says Āñjīgavi;
"a bull," says Kātya.
"It is 'the jeweled earring'," says Rāthītara.

(7.5:205.6) Then, having brought down these [grains] for the Hotṛ’s cup between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he places them upon the skin. (7.5:205.7) While those grains are being moistened (*nigrābhyā*), he causes the sacrificer to recite, beginning with: "You are the *nigrābhyā*s; heard by the gods, satisfy my life-span," and continuing until: "May my groups not thirst."

Having handed those over to the sacrificer, he then takes up whichever of these pressing-stones is like a living creature, saying: "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee."

Having taken it up, he consecrates it with: "Thou art a pressing-stone, performing the sacrifice for the gods; make this sacrifice profound. With thy highest rim, [press] for Indra the well-pressed Soma, full of honey, full of milk, winning rain."

Then, having leaned him forward and loosened him, he measures out the *upāṃśusavana* stone over the King Soma with the formula: "For Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra; for Indra, the overcomer of Vṛtra; for Indra, the slayer of adversaries; for Indra, accompanied by the Ādityas; for Indra, accompanied by the Viśve Devas"—thus five times with the *yajus* and five times silently.
Measuring ten times, he measures out half the quantity for the King Soma.
Then, having tied the remaining King Soma with a turban and brought it between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he places it in the interior (*nīḍa*).

Then he pours the measured King Soma together with the waters from the *hotṛ*’s cup, [reciting]: "You are invigorating, overcomers of Vṛtra; you are the wives of immortality who delight in bounty. O goddesses, establish this sacrifice among the gods. Being invited, drink of the Soma! Being invited, let the Soma drink of you!"

(7.5:206.2) Then he mixes it together with [the formula]: "O Soma, whatever light of yours is in heaven, whatever on earth, and whatever in the broad intermediate space—with that, grant wide wealth to this sacrificer! Speak in favor of the giver! (7.5:206.4) He touches the two pressing-boards across the skin with [the formula]: "O two Dhiṣaṇās, being firm, be firm; bestow strength; bestow strength upon me! May I not harm you; may you not harm me."

Then he causes [the sacrificer] to recite the *vṛddhi* verses: "O well-born ones, I have increased you with my mind; O you who are born of the *ṛta*, may we be your fortune (*bhaga*). O divine plants, in harmony with Indra, may you consent to the pressing of the Soma.
(7.5:206.9) The Pratiprasthātṛ holds six stalks in his left hand from the King [Soma] that has been fully satiated. Then, with that same hand, he takes up the Upāṃśu cup.
(7.5:206.10) Then he presses the consecrated King Soma eight times first.

(7.5:206.11) When the *aṃśu* stalk has fallen, he makes [the sacrificer] recite: "May it not depart from me, together with offspring, together with the increase of wealth; do not destroy my sensory power and my vigor.
(7.5:206.13) Then he gathers [the juice] with his joined palms silently.
The Pratiprasthātṛ places [the vessel] between;
the Adhvaryu pours [the soma] with the first two shoots, saying: "Flow pure for Vācaspati, O racer! Thereupon, these two shoots are joined together.
In the same manner, he presses the king [Soma] for a second time eleven times after it has been thus approached.
Here, he does not make [the sacrificer] recite when a shoot falls out;
likewise, he strikes [the Soma] with his joined palms silently.
The Pratiprasthātṛ places [the vessel] between;
the Adhvaryu pours [the Soma] with the two middle shoots, saying: "The bull [is purified] by the two shoots of the bull, cleansed by the hands.
Thus he accompanies these two shoots.
In the same manner, he presses the king [Soma] for the third time twelve times when it has been approached. He does not cause [the sacrificer] to recite here when a shoot has fallen out.
In the same manner, he strikes [the Soma] with his joined palms, but silently.
The Pratiprasthātṛ places [the filter] between.
The Adhvaryu pours [the soma] through the two final stalks with the formula: "O god, you are the purifier of the gods; for those whose portion you are, for them I take you.
He then touches these two stalks.
(7.5:207.2) Then, having wiped this Upāṃśusavana stone with the fringed filter, he places it on the eastern half of the mound, facing south.
(7.5:207.3) Then he takes the cup from the Pratiprasthātṛ, saying, "Thou art self-consecrated," and covers the cup.
(7.5:207.4) Then he looks at it, saying: "Make our nourishments honey-sweet.
(7.5:207.5) Then he wipes it upwards, saying: "For all thy powers, celestial and terrestrial.
(7.5:207.6) Then, taking it up, he rises, saying: "May the mind take hold of thee."
He comes, saying, "Follow the wide mid-region.

Having arrived, while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, he offers an oblation into the Āhavanīya fire, saying, "Svāhā! To thee, O well-born one, for Sūrya, svāhā! Having offered, he breathes out after [the offering].
He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art *bhūḥ*, the best of rays, the protector of breath; protect my breath.
Then, having wiped him downward, he wipes the middle enclosing-stick with his hand turned toward the west and downward, saying: "For the gods who drink the rays of light, thee!
Then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the cup into the Āgrayaṇa vessel, saying: "This is thy womb."
Then he throws the *aṃśu* stalk into this *upāṃśupātra* cup.
Then he places it to the south, touching it with the *upāṃśusavana* stone, saying, "For out-breath (*prāṇa*), thee!
He then touches the *upāṃśusavana* stone in response, saying, "For diffused breath (*vyāna*), thee!"

While the Adhvaryu is busy there, the Pratiprasthātṛ inserts two stalks at a time into the King Soma, saying: "O Soma, that which is thy invincible, watchful name—for that [name] of thine, O Soma, to Soma, svāhā! Thus he says: "That which is thine, O Soma," "that which is thine, O Soma.
Then, about to press the juice, they sit down all around the King Soma;
the Adhvaryu sits behind him, facing eastward.
The sacrificer follows his right arm;
the Pratiprasthātṛ stands to the south;
the Āgnīdhra stands to the north.
Between the Pratiprasthātṛ and the Āgnīdhra, he who is the fourth presses [the Soma].
Then he says to the Unnetṛ: "Bring it! Pour it in!
The Unnetṛ pours from the Ādhavanīya vessel with a ladle.
In the upper half of the *hotṛ*’s cup, they cause the stalks (*aṃśu*) to overflow [with water], saying: "May those quarters—east, west, north, and south—run toward you; O Mother, flow down!
This is the *nigrābha*.
They then cause [the soma] to swell.
They drive away [the dregs];
they press [the soma];
they go to the *nigrābha* water.
They cause [the Soma] to swell; they remove [the dregs];
they press it.
They proceed to the *nigrābha* water;
they cause it to swell and they distribute it.
They press [the Soma];
they do not go to the fourth *nigrābha* call.
Then, having gathered it well-prepared into the gathering-vessel, he hands it over to the *unnetṛ*.
The Unnetṛ pours it into the Ādhavanīya vessel. In this very manner the second round is completed;
likewise the third.
(7.6:208.10) Having wrapped the *ṛjīṣa* around with the fringe of the *daśāpavitra*, he hands it to the *unnetṛ*.
(7.6:208.11) The *unnetṛ*, having rinsed it in the *ādhavanīya* jar and squeezed it out, brings it down between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and places it upon the hide.
(7.6:208.12) Having arranged the pressing-stones facing it, he distributes this *ṛjīṣa* into four portions from the mouths of the stones.
Then either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, having crept behind the axle of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, places the *droṇakalaśa* facing eastward upon the pressing stones.
Upon it they spread out the *daśāpavitra* filter with its fringes pointing northward.
When this has been done, they await the rising of the sun.

When the sun has risen, he draws the Antaryāma cup from the King who is being purified, [saying]: "Thou art taken with a support; O Maghavan, restrain within, protect the Soma, ward off [evil] from wealth, and sacrifice for the sake of nourishments. I place thee between heaven and earth, between the wide mid-region, in harmony with the gods, both lower and higher; O Maghavan, rejoice in the Antaryāma! With the words, "Thou art made ready by thyself," he sets down the cup.
(7.6:209.1) Then he gazes at it, saying: "Make our nourishments honey-sweet.
(7.6:209.2) Then he wipes it upwards, saying: "For all thy powers, celestial and terrestrial.
(7.6:209.3) Then, taking it up, he stands up, saying: "May the mind attend thee."
He comes, saying, "Follow along the wide mid-region.
Having arrived, while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, he offers an oblation in the Āhavanīya fire, saying, "Svāhā! To thee, O well-born one, for Sūrya, svāhā!
Having offered, he breathes out after [the smoke].
He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art the yoke-pole, the best of the reins; thou art the out-breath and the in-breath. Protect my out-breath.

Then, having wiped it upwards, he wipes it across the middle enclosing-stick with his hand turned upwards and facing eastward, saying: "For the gods who drink the rays, thee! Then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the draught into the Āgrayaṇa vessel, saying: "This is thy womb."

(7.6:209.9) Then he places it down to the north, touching it with the Upāṃśusavana stone, [saying]: "For out-breathing thee! (7.6:209.10) [Saying]: "For diffused breathing thee! he touches the Upāṃśusavana stone in response.
(7.6:209.11) Then he says to the Unnetṛ: "Bring [the water] continuously and without negligence; I shall draw the Upāṃśu cups."
(7.6:209.12) Then he takes the cup for Indra and Vāyu.
(7.6:209.12) This cup has a rim and a neck-ring;

(7.6:209.13) with it he draws from the King who is being purified, reciting: "O Vāyu, come hither, you who drink the pure! Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Vāyu."

(7.6:209.15) Then, having moved it away, he draws it again, reciting: "O Indra and Vāyu, these [somas] are pressed. Having run through the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra and Vāyu," (7.6:209.17) and having wiped it around, he sets it down with: "This is thy womb; for the two who are in harmony, I take thee.
(7.6:209.17) Then he takes the cup of Mitra and Varuṇa.
This [procedure] is like that for the *pilakā* cup.

With this, he draws from the King who is being purified, reciting: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, this [is for you]... Having recited thus, and saying, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Mitra and Varuṇa," he places two blades of *barhis* grass between [the vessel and the milk] and mixes it with milk.
Having extracted the two blades of *barhis* grass and wiped [the cup] with the *daśāpavitra* strainer, he sets it down, saying: "This is your womb; for the two seekers of Truth (*ṛtāyu*), you!
Then, passing over the *āśvina* cup, he takes up the *śukra* cup;
this latter is made of *bilva* or *palāśa* wood and is smooth.
With that [cup], he draws from the King who is being purified, reciting: "This Vena impels... Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śaṇḍa.
Having wiped it around, he sets it down, saying: "This is thy womb; protect heroism.
Then he takes the Manthin vessel.
This [ladle] is made of *vaikaṅkata* wood and is smooth.
With it he draws [the draught], reciting for the King who is being purified: "Him as of old... and having run through [the rest], "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Marka.
Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the ladle and the vessel], he mixes it with groats.

Having extracted the two blades of *barhis* grass and wiped [the vessel] with the *daśāpavitra* strainer, he sets it down, saying: "This is thy womb; protect the offspring. Then he takes the *āgrayaṇa* vessel. With that, he draws [the portion] from the King who is being purified, reciting: "O gods who are eleven in heaven," and continuing: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the All-gods (*viśve devāḥ*)."
Then he utters the sound "hiṃ" over her three times.

(7.7:210.16) *hiṃ hiṃ hiṃ*. Soma purifies himself; Soma purifies himself; Soma purifies himself. He purifies himself for this sacred power (*brahman*); he purifies himself for this ruling power (*kṣatra*); he purifies himself for this people (*viś*). He purifies himself for food; he purifies himself for strength; he purifies himself for the waters; he purifies himself for the plants; he purifies himself for the trees.

[He recites: "It flows for Heaven and Earth; it flows for well-being; it flows for spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). It flows for this sacrificer who presses [the Soma], for me. Having spoken thus in a low voice (*upāṃśu*), he says aloud: "It flows for preeminence (*jyaiṣṭhya*). Then he addresses it: "Thou art the Āgrayaṇa, the good Āgrayaṇa. Quicken the sacrifice, quicken the lord of the sacrifice. Protect the pressings! May Viṣṇu protect thee; protect the people with thy power (*indriya*). Thus.

Having wiped it around, he sets it down with: "This is thy womb; for the Viśve Devas thee. From this point onward, he draws the cups accompanied by a supporting verse: "The thirty and three who are in groups, breaking asunder...
So says the Brāhmaṇa: "One should draw [the cup] with a verse containing the word 'broken' against one who is hostile."
Then he takes the Ukthya vessel.

With it he draws from the King who is being purified: "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra, the mighty, the vigorous, the seeker of hymns (ukthāyu), I take thee, who art dear to him, as that great vigor of thine, O Indra.
Having wiped it around, he sets it down: "This is thy womb; for Indra, the seeker of hymns, thee!"
(7.7:211.9) Then he takes up the *dhruvā* vessel.
(7.7:211.10) He says: "Those who entered by the eastern door, let them go out toward the east; those [who entered] by the western door, let them go toward the west; may I not pass around you."

Having passed around behind the pressers and the Soma-pressers, he receives [the vessel] from the north, reciting: "The head of heaven, the messenger of earth... Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Agni Vaiśvānara. Then he consecrates it with: "Thou art firm, a firm dwelling, the firmest of the firm, the most immovable of the immovable."

Then, having carried it back in the same manner as it was brought, he places it on the ground where it has not been strewn, in front of the support of the northern *havirdhāna* cart, with the formula: "This is thy womb; for Agni Vaiśvānara, thee!
With this, he deposits the King [Soma] using the *dhruva* cup.

Then, having thrown the *pariplu* ladle into the *droṇakalaśa* which is more than half-full, he consecrates the drops with the formulas: "The drop has fallen," "Thy drop that fell," "The drop that fell," and "Thy drop that fell."
Then he says to the Unnetṛ: "Make the *pūtabhṛt* vessel non-empty; I shall draw the cups for the Pavamāna.
Having heard this, the Unnetṛ spreads the filter over the opening of the *pūtabhṛt* and pours in two or three ladlings of the King [Soma].
Then, while the *pūtabhṛt* is not emptied, he draws the cups for the Pavamāna. He touches the *droṇakalaśa* with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati, thee!"
(7.7:212.5) "For Indra thee!"—with these words [he pours] into the *ādhavanīya* vessel;
(7.7:212.6) "For all the gods thee!"—with these words [he pours] into the *pūtabhṛt* vessel.
Then he says, "O *unnetṛ*, cause the King [Soma] to flow from the *pūtabhṛt* toward the east; having wiped the *ādhavanīya* with the fringes, turn it upside down."
He does so.
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he creeps out; as he creeps out, the Udgātṛ takes hold of him from behind.
The Prastotṛ [should touch] the Udgātṛ;
the Pratihartṛ [should touch] the Prastotṛ; and the sacrificer [should touch] the Pratihartṛ.
The Brahman, the sacrificer,
and the Pratiprasthātṛ as the seventh creep forward; while they have taken hold of one another, he offers a spoonful in the Āhavanīya fire.

"May Agni protect us at the morning pressing—Vaiśvānara, great by his majesty, the source of all well-being; may he, the purifier, bestow wealth upon us. May we be long-lived, sharing in the draught, Svāhā! With this verse the two Adhvaryus offer the oblation.
The others offer according to their respective Vedas.
Then they proceed toward the north, moving toward the Pavamāna.

(7.8:212.16) The Adhvaryu, bowing low, creeps forward first, shaking the two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), [reciting]: "May Speech go in front, going straight to the gods, bestowing glory upon me, vital breaths in the cattle, and offspring upon me and the sacrificer.
(7.8:212.18) Then they sit down in their respective places in the *āstāva*.

(7.8:212.19) Then he hands the two blades of sacrificial grass to either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, [with the formula]: "Thou art the under-layer for the Ṛc and the Sāman, for the procreation of the pair," or silently.

Then he mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the *hiṅ*-singer; Agni is the *prastotṛ*; Prajāpati is the *sāman*; Bṛhaspati is the *udgātṛ*; the Viśve Devas are the *upagātṛ*s; the Maruts are the *pratihartṛ*s; Indra is the *nidhana*. May those gods, the sustainers of breath, bestow breath upon me!
Om! Sing! This *bahiṣpavamāna* chant consists of nine verses.
When the fifth [verse] has been chanted forth, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art a falcon, having the Gāyatrī metre; I take hold of thee; carry me safely across.

At this point, he recites the Daśahotṛ formula. When the Sāman has been chanted out, he issues the command: "O Āgnīdh, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; adorn the sacrificial cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, let the animal victim be near at hand."
The two of them perform according to the direction.
Then, having touched water, he says, "Come, O sacrificer!
Having caused him to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he pays homage to the entire King Soma with the verse: "O Viṣṇu, you are our nearest [kinsman]."
Then he takes the cup for the Aśvins.
It is this very [cup] which has two corners.

Into it he draws [the Soma] from the *droṇakalaśa* with the dipping-spoon, reciting: "The whip which is yours... and so on, followed by: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Aśvins."
Having wiped [the ladle], he sets it down with the words: "This is your womb; for the two Mādhvīs, you!
Then, having touched water, he says: "Come, O sacrificer!

Having run to the Āhavanīya fire and taken four portions of ghee into the offering-ladle, and having mentally recited the Saptahotṛ formula, he offers it into the Āhavanīya while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, saying: "Svāhā!"
Then he proceeds with the *avakāśa* offerings using this section: "He encompasses Agni; he encompasses Indra.
Then he takes nine portions into the *pracaraṇī* ladle.
Then the Āgnīdhra priest distributes the embers from the Āgnīdhrīya hearth onto the other hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*) in successive order.
Then, sitting in front and facing west, he sprinkles the distributed *dhiṣṇiya* hearths with the same formulas as those used for their original placement.
If he offers oblations according to the order of their placement, he finally offers at the *Āgnīdhra* hearth with the verse, "Seven are yours...
(*sapta te*). If, however, he offers with "Svāhā! Svāhā!", he finally offers at the *Āgnīdhrīya* hearth simply with "Svāhā! for the sake of maintaining the orientation toward the north.

(7.8:214.3) Then he places the *pracaraṇī* ladle on the front corner (*cubuka*) of the northern *havirdhāna* cart. (7.8:214.4) Then, along the path of visibility, he spreads the *pṛṣṭhyā* grass-line continuously from the *gārhapatya* fire to the *āhavanīya* fire.
Then the Adhvaryu, with a cord in his hand, approaches the sacrificial post.
Having shifted the previous cord upward, while winding [the new cord] at the height of the navel, he says: "Recite for the post being encircled!
Having set aside the sacrificial post provided with a wooden chip (svaru), he dedicates the animal victim to Agni.
The ritual procedure up to the *pravara* is the same;
he chooses the *hotṛ* in the established manner.

Then he causes [the *āgnīdhra*] to announce: "O, cause to hear! Let there be a hearing! The two Aśvins are the *adhvaryus* by virtue of their *adhvaryu*-office; I and so-and-so are the human [officiants]."
He pronounces the name of the Pratiprasthātṛ.

Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause [the Hotṛ] to hear! "Let it be heard! "Mitra and Varuṇa are the Praśāstṛs; from the office of the Praśāstṛ. "So-and-so is the human one," thus he pronounces the name of the Maitrāvaruṇa.

Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Indra is the Brahman priest from among the Brāhmaṇās. "So-and-so is the human [priest]," thus he utters the name of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "The Maruts are the Potṛ priest from among the [Maruts]. "So-and-so is the human [priest]," thus [he says].
He pronounces the name of the Potṛ.
Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O announce! Let there be hearing! From the Neṣṭṛ, O divine ones! [And] "So-and-so is the human one," thus he pronounces the name of the Neṣṭṛ.
(7.9:214.17) Then he causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Agni from the Āgnīdhra fire! "So-and-so is the human [sacrificer].
(7.9:214.18) He pronounces the name of the Āgnīdhra; for each of them, as soon as they have entered upon their duties, he offers the *pravṛtāhuti* oblations.

(7.9:214.19) “May I be beloved of speech; fulfill the hymn with the *ṛc*; may the god Sūrya protect me from the gods”—with these [verses], the two *adhvaryus* offer oblations. (7.9:215.1) The others offer according to their respective Vedas. Then he calls for the *śrauṣaṭ*: “O, cause [them] to hear! “Let there be hearing! “Agni is the leader of the divine clans; the sacrificer, pressing [the soma], is the leader of men. May the household-fire of those two shine without failing for a hundred winters. May you two, as givers of wealth, be united in purpose yet distinct in bodies. Thus [he says].
The ritual procedure for the omentum is the same.
Having performed the offering with the omentum and having thrown the two omentum-spits into the fire, they step out and purify themselves at the *cātvāla* pit.
Then he causes the sacrificer to stand upon the rubbish-heap (*utkara*) facing the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the beaters (*vighana*).

(7.10:215.7) "The wooden sword is well-being, the mallet is well-being; the rib-bone is the altar, the axe is our well-being. You are worthy of sacrifice, you are the performers of sacrifice; do you invite me to this sacrifice! May Heaven and Earth invite me; may the *āstāva*, the *kalaśa* vessel, Soma, and Agni invite me; may the gods and the sacrifice invite me; may the *hotrā* invocations invite me to the invitation!
(7.10:215.10) Then, with the words, "Homage to Agni, the slayer of Makha; may the glory of Makha come to me," he worships the Āhavanīya fire.

"Obeisance to Rudra, the slayer of Makha; having been saluted, protect me!"—thus at the Āgnīdhra fire. "Obeisance to Indra, the slayer of Makha; do not destroy my sensory power and my vigor"—thus at the Hotrīya fire. Then, turning toward the east, he mutters: "You two are firm; you two, being relaxed, are joined together; protect me from distress! May the god Sūrya protect me from celestial distress; Vāyu from the intermediate space; Agni from the earth; Yama from the fathers; Sarasvatī from men."

(7.10:215.16) Then, having turned clockwise, he touches the two eastern doors of the *sadas* with the formula: "O divine doors, do not burn me. (7.10:215.17) Then he enters the *sadas* with the formula: "Homage to the *sadas*, homage to the lord of the *sadas*, homage to the eye of the friends who go before, homage to heaven, homage to earth.

(7.10:215.19) Then, from his seat, he throws away a blade of grass outside the *sadas* with the formula: "O son of a remarried woman, stand aside; sit on the seat of another who is more foolish than we."
He sits down, [reciting]: "May I go from the lowlands and the highlands.
Then he gazes at these [two], [reciting]: "O Heaven and Earth, protect me this day.
Then he looks across toward the southern half, [reciting]: "Come, O Fathers; may I be possessed of fathers through you; may you be possessed of good offspring through me."
(7.10:216.4) Then he looks toward the northern half [of the altar], saying:
"For the sake of being situated toward the north."
Then these two Adhvaryus worship the Āhavanīya fire in this very manner, beginning from the Āhavanīya;
likewise the Āgnīdhrīya; likewise the Hotrīya.
Having thus turned toward the east, they both mutter [the mantra].
Having thus turned clockwise, they touch the two eastern doors of the *sadas*.
In this manner, they enter the *sadas*.
In this manner, they both cast out blades of grass outside the *sadas* from their respective seats. The Adhvaryu sits down leaning against the southern doorpost,
and the Pratiprasthātṛ leans against the northern one.
Thus they look at one another;
thus they gaze upon the southern half and the northern half for the sake of being situated facing north.
Then the *vaṣaṭ*-utterers, starting from the Āhavanīya fire, worship the Āhavanīya in this very manner;
likewise the Āgnīdhrīya.
They pass around it by the north.
In this manner [they perform] for the Hotṛ's cup;
in this manner, having turned toward the east, they mutter [the formulas].
In this manner, having turned clockwise, they touch the two eastern doors of the Sadas.
In this manner they enter the *sadas*.
Having passed along the front of the *dhiṣṇiya*s and around the north of the *dhiṣṇiya* of the Acchāvāka, they thus cast out blades of grass from their seats outside the *sadas*.
In this manner, each sits down behind his own respective *dhiṣṇiya*.
Thus they look;
thus they gaze upon both the southern half and the northern half for the sake of being oriented toward the north.

(7.11:216.17) Then all the Udgātṛs—the Brahman and the Sadasya being among those who do not utter the vaṣaṭ—worship the Āhavanīya fire in this very manner, beginning from the Āhavanīya itself. (7.11:216.19) Likewise [they worship] the Āgnīdhrīya fire.
They pass around it on the north side.
In this manner [they touch] the Hotrīya; in this manner, having turned toward the east, they mutter [the formulas].
In this manner, having turned to the right and having gone around the north of the Sadas, they thus touch the two western doors of the Sadas.
In this manner they enter the *sadas* hall;
in this manner they cast out blades of grass from their seats toward the outside of the *sadas*;
and the *udgātṛ*s sit down around the *audumbarī* post.
To the south, the Brahman and the Sadasya sit facing north;
in this manner they look at one another. In this same way, they gaze across toward the southern half and the northern half.
"For the sake of standing toward the north.
Thus [it is said]. Now follows their movement while standing apart:
those who have no *dhiṣṇiya* altar move between the *dhiṣṇiya* of the Hotṛ and that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
Then those who have their own *dhiṣṇiya* altars go around each of their respective *dhiṣṇiya*s by the north.
When the pressing (*savana*) has concluded, they creep out in the same order as they had crept in.
Having recognized that they have moved forward, the Adhvaryu asks for the *savanīya* sacrificial cakes.
Then this Āgnīdhra, having sat down behind the Gārhapatya fire, spreads out fivefold [the flour] in a vessel;
he sets aside the sacrificial cake in the middle, having spread [the flour] beneath it and poured [ghee] over it.
The parched grains are in the east;
the groats are in the south;
the parched barley flour is in the west.
The *āmikṣā* is placed to the north.

Then, having grasped these [portions] together, having carried them out by the eastern door, having gone around the north of the *sadas*, and having carried them around the north of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, he places them within the altar (*antarvedi*).
Then, spreading a base of ghee in the *juhū* and *upabhṛt* ladles, he says: "Recite for the morning *prātaḥsāvan* offering as the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) are being cut off for Indra."
He cuts off two portions from the sacrificial cake, two from the parched grains,
and two from the flour-mash.
He pours clarified butter over the *parivāpa* twice and over the *āmikṣā* twice.
He anoints [the offering].
Then, for the *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation, he cuts off a portion once from the northern half of each of all [the portions] into the *upabhṛt* ladle;
he pours clarified butter over it twice.
He does not anoint [the offering].
Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the morning *prātaḥsāvan* of the Soma; [offer] the cakes set forth for Indra.
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation.
Then, while pouring together [the oblation], he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni.
Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Agni.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings.

(7.12:218.4) Then, having stepped across toward the north and placed the two *sruva*-ladles in their respective places, and having gathered the *iḍā* in the vessel, he sends the sacrificial cakes westward.
(7.12:218.6) Some follow along, saying, "The cattle are the *iḍā*.
(7.12:218.7) Then, moving eastward, he says: "Recite for Vāyu and for Indra-Vāyu!"

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the *pratinirgrāhya* portion for Indra and Vāyu from the *droṇakalaśa* into the auxiliary cup belonging to the *ādityasthālī* by means of the *pariplu* ladle, [saying]: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art the seat of speech. I take thee for the two guardians of speech, the two guardians of the ritual, the two supervisors over the firmness of this sacrifice.
Having taken the two cups, he steps out.
As soon as he has stepped out, the Adhvaryu takes the two cups.
He hands over the portion to be taken back to the Pratiprasthātṛ standing to the north.
Now, it is indeed said:
"Having taken the cup for Indra and Vāyu, he should perform the Āghāra-libation."

Having taken ghee from the vessel for the clarified butter with the *sruva* ladle and having taken the cup for Indra and Vāyu, he pours the *āghāra* libation, saying: "O gods, may this sacrifice be a peaceful rite (*adhvara*) for our plants, for our cattle, for our people, and for every living being; you are the peaceful rite. Swell, O divine Soma, rich in ghee! Svāhā!
Then he calls for the announcement: "O, cause [the Śrauṣaṭ] to be heard! "Let there be a hearing! "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Vāyu and for Indra-Vāyu!
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, the Adhvaryu offers first.
At the second *vaṣaṭ*-call, both offer together.

Having offered, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "O Indra and Vāyu, lords of splendor, whoever assails us, our rival who overflows [with hostility], here I cast him down lower, so that I may be the highest, O Indra.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the draught from the Adhvaryu’s cup into his own vessel.
The Adhvaryu pours half of both [portions] into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel;
the Pratiprasthātṛ pours that into the Āditya-sthālī with the formula, “For the gods thee!
Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, having handed the vessel to the Hotṛ and moving eastward, says, “Recite for Mitra and Varuṇa!”

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the counter-portion (*pratinirgrāhya*) for Mitrāvaruṇa from the *droṇakalaśa* into the reserve cup (*aupaśaya*) belonging to the *ādityasthālī*, using the dipping-spoon (*pariplu*). [He says: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art seated in the Truth (*ṛtasad*); I take thee for the two protectors of sight, the two protectors of the will, the two supervisors over this firm sacrifice.
Having taken the two cups, he steps out.
As soon as he has stepped out, the Adhvaryu takes the two cups.
He hands over the portion to be taken back (*pratinirgrāhya*) to the Pratiprasthātṛ standing to the north.
Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause [them] to hear! "Let there be a hearing! "Give the command for Mitra and Varuṇa!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, both of them offer together.

Having offered the oblation, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, lords of splendor, whoever seeks to harm us, our rival who drinks [us dry], O lords of beauty—I cast him down beneath my feet, so that I may be preeminent, as Indra is.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the draught from the Adhvaryu’s cup into his own vessel.
The Adhvaryu pours half of both [portions] into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s cup.
The Pratiprasthātṛ pours that into the Āditya-sthālī with the formula: “For the Viśve Devas, thee!
Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, having handed the cup to the Hotṛ, and moving eastward, says: “Recite for the Aśvins!”

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the *pratinirgrāhya* cup for the Aśvins from the *droṇakalaśa* into the reserve cup belonging to the *ādityasthālī*, using the *pariplu* ladle, with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art one who has heard [the call]. I take thee for the two protectors of hearing, the two protectors of the will, the two supervisors of this firm sacrifice. Having taken the two cups, he steps out.
As soon as he has stepped out, the Adhvaryu takes the two cups.
He hands over the *pratinirgrāhya* cup to the Pratiprasthātṛ standing to the north.
Then he calls for the announcement: "O, cause [the Agnīdh] to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Command [the Hotṛ] regarding the Aśvins!
At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, both of them offer together.

Having offered the oblation, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "O Aśvins, lords of splendor, whatever rival of ours assails us or drinks up our strength, here I cast him down beneath me, so that I may be supreme, as Indra is.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the draught from the Adhvaryu’s cup into his own vessel.
The Adhvaryu pours half of both [residues] into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel.
The Pratiprasthātṛ pours it into the Aditya vessel with the formula: "For all the gods, thee!"
If the vessel is indeed more than half-full with these residues, he covers it with this cup.

But if it is not more than half-full, he makes it more than half-full from the *droṇakalaśa* and covers it with that very same cup, saying: "O Viṣṇu of wide stride, this is your Soma; guard it! Let no evil-eyed one look upon it!"

(7.13:220.12) Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, having handed the cup to the Hotṛ and moving eastward, says: "Recite for those being filled! Fill the cups following the Hotṛ’s cup! Make them bright on both sides! O Camasādhvaryu of the Acchāvāka, do not fill yours! O Pratiprasthātṛ, receive [the splinters] with four splinters, both sprinkled and unsprinkled! (7.13:220.16) They act according to these instructions.
(7.13:220.16) They first draw [the Soma] from the *droṇakalaśa*;
then from the *pūtabhṛt*;
then from the *droṇakalaśa*.
These [cups] have bright [contents] on both sides.
They draw the *hotṛ*’s cup first,
and the others as they come.
Having lifted it up, they set it down upon the high altar (*uttaravedi*).
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ sprinkles two of the four wood-shavings; two remain unsprinkled.
Having covered [the vessels] with two sprinkled [strainers], they take hold of them with two unsprinkled ones;
the Adhvaryu takes the *śukra* (pure draught),
and the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the *manthin* (stirred draught).
Taking the two cups, they go out.
The Adhvaryu goes out leaning against the southern doorpost;
the Pratiprasthātṛ [goes out] against the northern one.

Behind the *uttaravedi*, the two of them join the two cups together with the six joining formulas: "Join the life-force; quicken that for me! Join the out-breath; quicken that for me! Join the in-breath; quicken that for me! Join the diffused breath; quicken that for me! Join the eye; quicken that for me! Join the ear; quicken that for me! Having joined them with these six unions, they step apart.

"You are praised, O giver of people; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead you forward. Producing offspring rich in heroes, go around, O *śukra*, with the brilliance of the *śukra*!"—with these words, the *adhvaryu* walks around the northern altar by the south.

"You are praised, O giver of people; may the gods who drink the *manthin* lead you forward. Producing offspring rich in progeny, go around, O *manthin*, with the brilliance of the *manthin*!"—with these words, the *pratiprasthātṛ* walks around the northern altar by the north.
The two of them run toward the *uttaravedi* from the east, facing westward, [saying]: "United with Indra, may we overcome those who attack us, slaying the Vṛtras without resistance.

"O Agni, by that splendor (*tejas*) which is yours, may I become splendid; by that radiance (*varcas*) which is yours, O Agni, may I become radiant; by that heat (*haras*) which is yours, O Agni, may I become hot."

(7.13:221.16) Then, between the sacrificial post and the Āhavanīya fire, they join together two cups [with the formulas]: "You two are life; bestow life upon me! Bestow life upon the sacrifice! Bestow life upon the lord of the sacrifice! You two are breath; bestow breath upon me! Bestow breath upon the sacrifice! Bestow breath upon the lord of the sacrifice! You two are out-breath; bestow out-breath upon me! Bestow out-breath upon the sacrifice! Bestow out-breath upon the lord of the sacrifice! You two are diffused breath..."

"You two are the *stha* [support]; bestow the *vyāna* upon me; bestow the *vyāna* upon the sacrifice; bestow the *vyāna* upon the lord of the sacrifice. You two are the eye; bestow sight upon me; bestow sight upon the sacrifice; bestow sight upon the lord of the sacrifice. You two are the ear; bestow hearing upon me; bestow hearing upon the sacrifice; bestow hearing upon the lord of the sacrifice. Having joined together with these six joints, they step apart.
"O you two gods, Śukra and Manthin, arrange the divine subjects; arrange the human subjects; bestow food and vigor upon us; place vital breaths in the cattle, and progeny in me and the sacrificer.
Having spoken thus, they cast away the two unsprinkled wood-shavings outside the altar.
"Śaṇḍa is cast out along with so-and-so," saying this, the Adhvaryu meditates in his mind upon whomsoever the sacrificer hates.
"Marka has been cast out along with him," [saying this] the Pratiprasthātṛ mentally contemplates whomever the sacrificer hates.
Then, having touched water, they both place two sprinkled fuel-sticks [on the fire].
"This is thy bright fuel-stick; be kindled by it, svāhā!"—thus says the Adhvaryu.
(7.14:222.9) "<This is your fuel-stick for the *manthin* cup; be kindled by it, *svāhā*!"—thus says the *pratiprasthātṛ*.
(7.14:222.10) At this time, the *camasādhvaryu*s lift up the cups.

(7.14:222.11) Then the *adhvaryu*, standing in front facing west, causes [the *āgnīdhra*] to call out: "O, cause [him] to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Prompt [the *hotṛ*] for the Soma-pressings of the morning, belonging to the bright and the *manthin* [cup], dripping with sweetness; for Indra, the Somas are set forth—prompt [the *hotṛ*]! Thus he says.

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, both offer together: "He is the first creator, Viśvakarman; he is the first Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni; he is the first wise Bṛhaspati; to that Indra I offer the pressed [soma], svāhā!
Thus they offer twice—at the *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*.
In the same manner, they offer all the *camasa*s twice each.

Then he issues the command: "Let the cup of the Hotṛ go forward, the cup of the Brahman, the cup of the Udgātṛ, the cup of the Sacrificer, and the cup of the Sadasya; O Camasādhvaryus of the Hotrakas, having drawn [Soma] from the Droṇakalaśa each once, turn back! O Camasādhvaryu of the Hotṛ, stop! Come, O Pratiprasthātṛ, offer the residue of the Manthin in the northern half of the Āhavanīya fire.
They act according to the command.

(7.14:222.21) Then, having turned clockwise, he pours the residue of the draught into the Hotṛ’s cup, either with the formula, “I pour thee, who hast been offered, into that which has been offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men,” or silently. (7.14:223.1) Then the Pratiprasthātṛ offers the residue of the Manthin draught on the northern half of the Āhavanīya fire with the formula: “This is thy portion, O Rudra, which thou didst demand; enjoy it! May we obtain cattle, increase of wealth, heroic power, and well-being lasting for a year—svāhā!”
Then, having touched water, he places the *śukra* cup and the *manthin* cup on the mound (*khara*) in their respective places.
These goblets of the great officiants (*mahartvij*) go forth.
Then the cup-bearers of the *hotraka*s, having drawn [Soma] from the *droṇakalaśa* each once, turn back.
Taking the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup from among them and having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "O *praśāstṛ*, recite the offering-verse (*yaja*).
At the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ* calls, he makes two offerings.

Having performed the joint offerings for the five officiating priests (*hotṛs*) with the calls, "O *brahman*, recite the offering-verse! O *potr̥*, recite the offering-verse! O *neṣṭṛ*, recite the offering-verse! O *agnīdh*, recite the offering-verse!", he turns to the right, hastens back toward the west, and sits down in front of the *hotṛ* with the words, "The *agnīdh* has offered."
"He has performed a blessing," says the Hotṛ, "he who shall cause us to drink King Soma.
Then the Hotṛ takes the cup for Indra and Vāyu; as soon as it is taken, the Adhvaryu takes hold of it from behind.
When the Adhvaryu has taken hold [of him], the Hotṛ, having sought permission (*upahava*), consumes [the portion] as he knows it.
Likewise, when the Hotṛ has taken hold [of him], the Adhvaryu, having sought permission, consumes [it] with the formula: "In me is the Vasu, the Purovasu; Vāk is the protector. Protect my speech.
Then the Hotṛ consumes [his portion].
Then the Adhvaryu hands it over to the Hotṛ; the Hotṛ then places it in its proper place.
Then the Hotṛ takes the Maitrāvaruṇa cup; the Adhvaryu takes hold of it as soon as it has been taken.
When the Adhvaryu has taken hold of it, the Hotṛ, having sought permission, consumes it according to the formula he knows.

When the Hotṛ has thus taken hold [of him], the Adhvaryu, having sought permission (*upahava*), consumes [the portion] with the formula: "May the Vasu, the finder of wealth, the protector of sight, protect my sight.
Then he hands it over to the Hotṛ;
the Hotṛ places it in its proper place.
Then the Hotṛ takes the cup for the Aśvins.
As soon as it has been taken, the Adhvaryu touches it from behind.
When the Adhvaryu has touched it, the Hotṛ, having sought permission, consumes it according to the formula he knows.

When the Hotṛ has thus taken hold [of him], the Adhvaryu, having sought permission (*upahava*), consumes [the portion] with the formula: "In me is the Vasu, the gatherer of wealth, the protector of hearing; protect my hearing!
Regarding this, there is a Brāhmaṇa passage stating: "He consumes the Āśvina cup while moving it around on all sides.
Then he hands it over to the Hotṛ.
Then the Hotṛ sets it down in its proper place.
Then, having touched water, they lift up the *iḍā* for the Hotṛ.
While the *iḍā* is being invoked, they hold up the cups;
when the *iḍā* has been invoked, there remains an unoffered portion for the *agnīdh*.
Then he makes these vessels dedicated to the dual deities non-empty.
He throws a fragment of the sacrificial cake into the cup for Indra and Vāyu;
the curd-mixture into the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa; and the parched grains into the cup for the Aśvins.

Then, having taken hold of these [spoons], having carried them out by the eastern door, and having brought them into the *havirdhāna* shed by the western door, he places them on the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna*.
They remain there until the third pressing. Then he places the sixfold portion in the *āgnīdhra* fire.
They consume [the portions] and perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*).

They consume the cups for which the *iḍā* has been invoked, reciting the long *bhakṣa*-formula: "O food, come; enter me! Having thus recited, they say: "O divine Soma, belonging to the Vasu-group, knower of our thoughts, of the morning pressing, having the *gāyatrī* metre, drunk by Indra, full of sweetness, being invited—I, being invited, consume thee."
Having invited one another, these three consume the *hotṛ*’s cup alone; they consume the other cups according to their respective vessels.
With the words, "Impel [the breath] for me," they touch themselves.
They swell the cups with the mantra, "Swell up; let [the milk] gather unto thee.
The *nārāśaṃsa* goblets, having been swelled, are set down one below the other along the support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the sake of Indra and Agni.
Then this *acchāvāka* sits in front of the *sadas*.
Placing a large piece of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) for him, he says: "O Acchāvāka, speak what you have to say.
When he recognizes the Acchāvāka's [response], "Come hither, O Brahmins, call the Brahmins," then he says: "O Hotṛ, this Acchāvāka here desires an invitation; invite him.
The Hotṛ invites him with a verse.
Then, as they are moving eastward, he says: "Recite for the [Soma] being drawn out! O Camasādhvaryu of the Acchāvāka, draw [the Soma] out; make it bright on both sides. He does so.
Then, having gone east and taken the Acchāvāka’s cup, and having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "O Acchāvāka, recite the offering prayer (*yaja*)."
Having offered at the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he carries away the portion for consumption.
If the Acchāvāka seeks an invitation (*upahava*) from him, he indeed invites him; however, they do not consume it together.
His *nārāśaṃsa* cup, having been made to swell, is set down.
Then he says: "O *acchāvāka*, sit down! O *neṣṭṛ*, lead the wife forward! O *agnīdh*, announce to me that the *acchāvāka* has sat down.
Thereupon this *acchāvāka* sits down behind his own *dhiṣṇiya* hearth.
The Neṣṭṛ brings the wife, taking the *pannejani* waters, with this *nigada*: "Go forth! Come up!

Having caused her to go out by the eastern door and having led her into the *sadas* by the western door, he places the *pannejani* waters behind the Neṣṭṛ’s *dhiṣṇiya*, on a path not used for traffic, on the way to the Sāman, [saying]: "For the Vasus, for the Rudras, for the Ādityas, for the Viśve Devas..."
"From all the gods, I set down for you the foot-washing waters," [he says]. "For the sacrifice, I set down for you the foot-washing waters.
Then the Āgnīdhra says, "The Acchāvāka is seated; the Acchāvāka, having been seated, has caused the foot-washing waters to be placed near him.
At this time, the sacrificer eats portions of the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) in the Āgnīdhra fire-hall.
If there should be food, it should be in the wife’s chamber.
Then they take up the two ṛtu-cups: the Adhvaryu takes the southern one, and the Pratiprasthātṛ the northern one.

The Adhvaryu first draws [the Soma] from the Droṇakalaśa with the Vāyavya cup, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Madhu. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ draws it, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Mādhava."
Taking the two cups, they go out.
The Adhvaryu goes out leaning against the southern doorpost; the Pratiprasthātṛ stops, leaning against the northern doorpost.
Then the Adhvaryu causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Prompt with the season-formula!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation;
the Pratiprasthātṛ steps out.
The Adhvaryu enters; he takes [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śukra.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be a hearing! "Prompt [the Hotṛ] by means of the season!"
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers the oblation;
the Adhvaryu steps out,
and the Pratiprasthātṛ enters.
He draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śuci.
Then the Adhvaryu causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Prompt [the Hotṛ] by means of the season! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.
The Pratiprasthātṛ steps out, the Adhvaryu enters, and he draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Nabhya."
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ calls for the announcement: "O, cause [him] to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Command [the Hotṛ] by means of the season!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering;
the Adhvaryu then steps out.
The Pratiprasthātṛ enters; he takes [the draught] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Nabhasya.
Then the Adhvaryu causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be a hearing! "Prompt for the season!"
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation;
the Pratiprasthātṛ steps out,
while the Adhvaryu enters, turning the vessel upside down.
He draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Īṣa.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ calls for the announcement: "O, announce! Let it be heard! Command with the season!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.
The Adhvaryu steps out;
the Pratiprasthātṛ enters, having turned his vessel upside down. He draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Ūrj."
Then the Adhvaryu calls for the announcement: "O, cause it to be heard! "Let there be hearing! "Command [the Hotṛ] by means of the seasons!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering;
the Pratiprasthātṛ steps out.
The Adhvaryu enters [the Sadas];
he takes [the cup] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the beloved of Sahas.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ calls for the announcement: "O, announce! "Let there be a hearing! "Prompt [the Hotṛ] by means of the seasons!"
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers the oblation;
the Adhvaryu steps out,
while the Pratiprasthātṛ enters.
He draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Sahasya.
Then the Adhvaryu calls for the announcement: "O announce! "Let it be heard! "Command for the Seasons!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation.
The Pratiprasthātṛ steps out, while the Adhvaryu enters, turning his vessel upside down.
He draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Tapas."
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Prompt with the seasons!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering;
the Adhvaryu then steps out.
The Pratiprasthātṛ steps forward, having turned the vessel upside down.
He says to him, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, rest with this vessel.
Then the Adhvaryu causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause [the Agnīdh] to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Command for the season! (ṛtunā preṣya).
"O two Adhvaryus, sacrifice! says the Praśāstṛ. "O Hotṛ, sacrifice this! says the Adhvaryu.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers the oblation.
He approaches the Pratiprasthātṛ who is seated right there.
The Pratiprasthātṛ takes [the draught] first, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Tapasya.
Then the Adhvaryu takes [it], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art the gliding one; I take thee, acceptable to Aṃhaspati."
Taking the two cups, they go out.
The Adhvaryu goes out leaning against the southern doorpost;
the Pratiprasthātṛ [goes out] leaning against the northern one.
At this point, the Pratiprasthātṛ causes [the announcement] to be heard: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "Prompt for the season! Then the Praśāstṛ says, "O Gṛhapati, sacrifice!
and the Gṛhapati says, "O Hotṛ, sacrifice this!"
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, both offer together.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the draught into the Adhvaryu’s cup.
He says to him: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, take the draught for Indra and Agni with this cup."

Then the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the draught for Indra and Agni from the *droṇakalaśa* with the dipping-spoon (*pariplu-pātra*), reciting: "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice! Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra and Agni. Having wiped it around, he sets it down, saying: "This is thy womb; for Indra and Agni, thee!"

Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, causes the Hotṛ to consume this cup with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the Seasons," [and] with "by the Hotṛ, by the Potṛ, by the Neṣṭṛ, by the Āgnīdh, by the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, by the Maitrāvaruṇa.

Then, turning the cup over, the Hotṛ alone consumes it four times with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the Seasons," [and] with "by the Hotṛ, by the Potṛ, by the Neṣṭṛ, by the Acchāvāka. Then, turning the cup over again, the Hotṛ alone consumes it twice with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the Season."
Then he asks the Hotṛ: "Will you recite the *praṇava* in a low voice (*upāṃśu*), or with distinct pauses (*vigrāham*)? Having heard how the Hotṛ replies, he holds the vessel and turns away.
He mutters as much of this *yajus* as can be completed: "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods."
The Hotṛ calls out to him; the Adhvaryu responds;
[the Hotṛ] recites.
He responds: what he recites in a whisper, that he responds to in a whisper;
what he recites aloud, that he responds to aloud.
Having responded to the *uktha*— whether continuously or with pauses— in the established manner, he goes forward and lifts up this cup for Indra and Agni;
they lift up the *nārāśaṃsa* goblets after him.
Then he causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "O reciter of the hymns, sacrifice the Soma!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he offers twice.
In the same manner, they shake the *nārāśaṃsa* cups twice each.
The Nārāśaṃsa cups follow this vessel. The consumption is according to the libation: "Of what has been drunk by Indra and Agni.

Thus the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu together consume this vessel with the formula for what was drunk by Narāśaṃsa: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, belonging to the morning pressing, having the Gāyatrī metre, drunk by the Pitṛs, full of sweetness, and invited—I, being invited, partake."
These three, having invited one another, consume from the *hotṛ*’s cup alone; they consume from their respective cups according to the cup.
With the words, "Impel me," they touch themselves.
They swell the cups with the mantra, "Swell up; let [the milk] gather unto thee.
The *nārāśaṃsa* goblets, having been swelled, are set down below the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the sake of the *vaiśvadeva* draught.

Then, having gone forward to the east while taking up the *śukra* cup, he says: "O *unnetṛ*, when I take this *vaiśvadeva* draught, then cause the King Soma to flow through the *pūtabhṛt* filter toward the north. Having wiped the *droṇakalaśa* with the fringes of the filter, turn it upside down."
He acts accordingly.

With the *śukra* cup, he draws the *vaiśvadeva* draught from the *kalaśa*, reciting: "O protectors, supporters of the people... Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Viśve Devas. Having wiped it around, he sets it down, saying: "This is thy womb; for the Viśve Devas, thee!"
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the chant for the *vaiśvadeva* [laud] for the Hotṛ.
"This is the last [verse]," they announce.
The Adhvaryu turns away from the Hotṛ’s time;
the Hotṛ calls out to him,
and the Adhvaryu responds.
He recites the *śastra*;
he responds with the *pratigara*.
Having responded to the *uktha* in the established manner, he goes forward and lifts up this cup for the Viśve Devās.
The *nārāśaṃsa* cups are lifted up again;
then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause it to be heard! "Let there be a hearing! "O reciter of the *uktha*, offer the oblation of Soma!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering twice.
In the same manner, they shake the Nārāśaṃsa cups twice each.
The Nārāśaṃsas follow this cup.
The consumption [of the Soma] occurs at each pressing with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by all the gods."

The Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu together consume this cup with the formula for what has been drunk by Narāśaṃsa: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, belonging to the morning pressing, having the Gāyatrī metre, drunk by the Fathers, full of sweetness, and invited—I, being invited, partake.
Thus these three, having invited one another, consume the Hotṛ’s cup, and they consume the other cups according to their respective vessels.
With the words, "Impel me," they touch themselves; they do not cause the cups to swell; having consumed the entire contents, they perform the ritual purification.
Then he says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, having cleansed these four cups and this Śukra cup at the Mārjālīya fire, pour them back into the [other] cups.
He does so.
Then, as he goes forward toward the east, he says:
"Fill the cups following the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa; O Unnetṛ, prepare the Soma!
Thus they fill the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa first, and the others as they come.
Having poured it out, they set it down upon the *uttaravedi*. Then he takes the supplementary cup from the *ukthya-sthālī*.

Into that, he draws the third portion of this King [Soma] which is contained in the *ukthya-sthālī*, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, agreeable to the gods, seeking the gods, for the *ukthya*s, seeking the *ukthya*s, for the life of the sacrifice—agreeable to Mitra and Varuṇa, I take thee."
Again, with the formula, "Thou art the oblation," he touches the *ukthya* vessel; having wiped it around, he sets it down with, "This is thy womb; for Mitra and Varuṇa, thee.
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the chant (*stotra*).
They chant for the Maitrāvaruṇa: "This is the last," they say.
From the time of the Maitrāvaruṇa, the Adhvaryu turns away.
The Maitrāvaruṇa calls out to him;
the Adhvaryu responds;
[the Hotṛ] recites.
He responds.
Having responded to the *uktha*, he goes forward and lifts up this cup;
the goblets are lifted up after it.
Then he causes [the Hotṛ] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "O reciter of hymns, sacrifice the Soma-libations!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he makes two offerings;
in the same manner, they offer all the *camasa* cups twice each.

(7.18:231.6) Then, having turned clockwise, he pours the residue of the draught into the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa, either with the formula: "I pour thee, who hast been offered, into that which has been offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men," or silently. (7.18:231.8) Having set down this very vessel right there, they run back toward the west with the portions for consumption. (7.18:231.9) The formula for consumption at each pressing is: "Of what has been drunk by Mitra and Varuṇa."
These three, having invited one another, consume the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa; they consume the other cups according to their respective vessels.
With the words, "Impel [the sacrifice] for me," they touch themselves.
They do not swell the cups;
having consumed the entire contents, they perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*).
Then he says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, proceed with your two cups."
Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ, moving forward toward the east, says:
"Fill the cups following the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; O Unnetṛ, cause the Soma to swell!
Thus they fill the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin first, and the others as they come.
Having poured it out, they set it down upon the *uttaravedi*. Then he takes the supplementary cup belonging to the *ukthya-sthālī*.

Into that, he draws half of this *rājā* (Soma) which remains in the *ukthya-sthālī*, [saying]: "Thou art taken with a support; for the gods thee, the god-loving; for the *ukthyas* thee, the *uktha*-loving; for the life of the sacrifice, for Indra thee, I take thee as one who is dear."
(7.19:231.20) Again, [reciting] "Thou art the oblation," he touches the *ukthya* vessel;
having wiped it around, he sets it down [with the words], "This is thy womb; for Indra thee.
(7.19:231.21) Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the *stotra*.
They chant for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, saying, "This is the last [verse]. At the moment of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's [recitation], the Pratiprasthātṛ turns away.
The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin calls out to him; the Pratiprasthātṛ responds; he recites.
He responds.
Having responded to the *uktha*, he goes forward and lifts up this cup;
the *camasa* cups are lifted up after it.
Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause it to be heard! "Let there be hearing! "O reciter of the hymns, sacrifice the Soma-libations!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he makes two offerings.
In that same manner, they offer all the *camasa* cups twice each.

Then, having turned clockwise, he pours the residue of the draught into the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, either with the formula, "I pour thee, who art offered, into that which is offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men," or silently. Having set down this very vessel right there, they run westward with the portions for consumption. The formula for the consumption at each pressing is: "Of that which has been drunk by Indra."
These three, having invited one another, consume the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; they consume their respective cups according to the order of the cups.
With the words, "Impel for me," they touch themselves.
They do not swell the cups;
having consumed the entire contents, they perform the ritual purification.
Then, as they proceed toward the east, he says:
"Fill the cups following the cup of the Acchāvāka; O Unnetṛ, draw out the entire King Soma; do not leave any remainder; O Pratiprasthātṛ, rest with this cup; come, O Sacrificer!

Having thus caused him to enter the Havirdhāna shed by the eastern door, he then spreads this skin upon the two boards with its neck toward the east and the hair upward, either with the formula "O Sacrifice, be established," or silently.

Having placed the pressing-stones facing him, he brings down the King [Soma] between the two shafts of the southern *havirdhāna* cart with two verses: "For the heart thee! For the mind thee! O King Soma, come, descend! Then they announce him to the *udgātṛ*s;
they perform upon him whatever they know [to be prescribed].
(7.20:232.19) Then, having turned the *adhavanīya* vessel face upwards, he pours half of the *vasatīvarī* waters into it;
(7.20:232.20) half of the *ekadhanā* waters [he pours in as well].
(7.20:232.20) He sets down the *vasatīvarī* waters in front of the axle.
Behind the axle-pole are the ekadhana vessels; they draw the cup of the Acchāvāka first,
and the others as they come.
Having drawn out the King Soma entirely, they set it down upon the high altar (*uttaravedi*).
Then he takes the secondary vessel belonging to the *ukthya-sthālī*.

Into that, he draws all of the King Soma that remains in the *ukthya-sthālī*, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, agreeable to the gods, longing for the gods, for the *ukthya* cups, longing for the *ukthya*s, for the life of the sacrifice, for Indra and Agni."
(7.20:233.4) Here, however, he does not touch the *ukthya* vessel with the formula, "Thou art the oblation.
(7.20:233.5) Having wiped it with the fringes of the cloth, he turns it upside down.
(7.20:233.6) Having wiped it all around, he sets it down with the words: "This is thy womb; for Indra and Agni, thee!"
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the *stotra*.
They chant the *stotra*.
To the *acchāvāka*, they say: "This is the last [verse]."
After the time of the Acchāvāka, the Pratiprasthātṛ turns away from him;
the Acchāvāka calls out to him,
and the Pratiprasthātṛ responds.
He recites the *śastra*;
he responds with the *pratigara*.
Having responded to the *uktha* in the established manner, he goes forward and lifts up this cup.
The cups are lifted up;
then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause it to be heard! "May there be a hearing! "O reciter of the hymn, offer the Soma-libations!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*, he offers twice.
In the same manner, they offer all the *camasa*s twice each.

Then, having turned clockwise, he pours the residue of the draught into the *camasa* of the Acchāvāka, either with the formula, "I pour thee, who art offered, into that which is offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men," or silently.
Having set down this very vessel right there, they run back toward the west with the portions to be consumed.
The consumption at each pressing is performed with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by Indra and Agni.
These three, having invited one another, consume the cup of the Acchāvāka; the others consume their respective cups according to their vessels.
With the words, "Impel me," they touch themselves; they do not swell the cups; having consumed the entire contents, they perform the ritual purification.
Then, having responded to the morning pressing with "O reciter of the *uktha*," he says, "O *praśāstṛ*, give the command! The *praśāstṛ* then says, "Proceed!"
The morning pressing is concluded.

(8.1:234.1) "O divine doors, open yourselves for the midday pressing"—having recognized that they have thus moved forward from this very place, the Adhvaryu, walking eastward, says: "O pressers, come! Summon the Grāvastut! Come, O sacrificer!

(8.1:234.2-3) Having caused him to enter the Havirdhāna shed by the eastern door, and having poured water from the Vasatīvarī waters into the Hotṛ’s cup, he makes the sacrificer recite over those same *nigrābhya* waters as before.
Having handed those over to the sacrificer in that same manner, he takes up another pressing-stone other than the *upāṃśusavana*.
Having rested it facing eastward in that same manner and having loosened the King [Soma], he measures out the King against the pressing-stone, saying: "For Indra thee! For Indra thee!
five times with the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) and five times silently.
Measuring ten times, he measures the King [Soma] in every respect.
Having sprinkled him with water, he hands the turban to the Grāvastut.
Having likewise sprinkled it with water, they carry the garment to the residence of the Adhvaryu.
In the same manner, he pours the measured king [Soma] with the waters from the *hotṛ*’s cup;
in the same manner, he stirs it together; in the same manner, he touches the two boards across the hide.
Likewise, he causes the *vṛddhi* formulas to be recited; here the stalks are not used together; they press only with sounds, saying: "Hither! Hither! Hither!"
They lead that very [horse] with the words: "Hither! Hither! Hither! Hither! Hither! Then they cause it to play about at the *saṃbharaṇīya* [stotra] with the words: "Hither! Hither! Hither!
Then, having well-gathered it, he hands it over to the *unnetṛ* on the *saṃbharaṇī* [vessel].
The Unnetṛ pours it into the Ādhavanīya vessel. In this very manner the second round is completed;
likewise the third.
On the third day of the third [pressing], they proceed with the Bṛhat [Sāman], chanting: "Bṛhat, Bṛhat, Bṛhat!
At the end, having wrapped the *ṛjīṣa* in the *daśāpavitra*, he hands it to the *unnetṛ*.
The *unnetṛ*, having washed it in the *ādhavanīya* jar and squeezed it out, brings it down between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and places it upon the hide.
Having placed those pressing-stones directly in front of him in that same manner, he distributes this *ṛjīṣa* in four parts from the mouths of the stones.
Then either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, having crept behind the axle of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, places the *droṇakalaśa* upon the stones facing eastward.
Having spread over it a *daśāpavitra* filter with its fringes pointing northward in that same manner, he draws the *śukra* and *manthin* cups in the established manner.
Then, with the two Ṛtupātra vessels, he draws two Marutvatīya cups.

With the two verses, "The bull accompanied by the Maruts, the one who has grown strong" and "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here," he then pours the Āgrayaṇa vessel over [the draught] and supports it from below. Having likewise uttered the *abhihiṅkāra* over it three times and wiped it around, he sets it down.
In the same manner, he draws the Ukthya cup.
He concludes the King Soma with the Ukthya.

Then, having thrown the *pariplu* ladle into the upper half of the *droṇakalaśa*, he consecrates the drops with the mantras: "The drop has fallen," "O drop that is thine," "The drop," and "O drop that is thine."
Likewise, he says to the Unnetṛ: "Make the *pūtabhṛt* vessel non-empty; I shall draw the cups of the *pavamāna*.
Having thus made the *pūtabhṛt* non-empty, he draws the cups of the *pavamāna*. He touches the *droṇakalaśa* with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra, thee!
He [touches] the *ādhavanīya* with the formula: "For Indra, thee!"
(8.2:235.19) "For Indra thee!"—with these words [he draws] from the *pūtabhṛt*.

(8.2:235.19) Likewise, he says, "O *unnetṛ*, cause the King [Soma] to flow together toward the *pūtabhṛt* in an easterly direction; having wiped the *ādhavanīya* with the fringes [of the filter], turn it upside down.
He does so.

(8.2:236.1) Having likewise touched water and taken two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he steps out. (8.2:236.2) While they are likewise maintaining contact with him, he offers a spoonful (*sruva-āhuti*) into the Āhavanīya fire.

(8.2:236.3) With the verse, "May all the gods, the Maruts, and Indra not abandon us at this second pressing; may we, long-lived and speaking what is pleasing to them, abide in the favor of the gods, svāhā!"—with this [verse], the two Adhvaryus offer the oblation.
The others offer according to their respective Vedas.
Then, having turned to the right, they proceed toward the *sadas* for the *pavamāna* chant; thus they sit down in the *sadas*, each in his proper place.

Likewise, he gives two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) to either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, saying, "Thou art the under-layer for the *Ṛc* and the *Sāman*, for the procreation of the couple," or he does so silently. Then he mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the maker of the *hiṅ*.
This is the fifteenfold midday *pavamāna* stotra.

When the eighth [offering] has been commenced, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art the fair-winged one, having the *triṣṭubh* as thy metre; I take hold of thee; convey me safely across. At this point, he recites the *Caturhotṛ* formula. When the *sāman* has been chanted, he issues the direction: "O *Āgnīdh*, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; adorn the sacrificial cakes; O *Pratiprasthātṛ*, bring curds for the *dadhigharma*."
The two of them perform according to the direction;
having likewise touched water, he says, "Come, O sacrificer," and having caused him to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he worships the entire King Soma in that manner.
He proceeds in that manner with the *avakāśas*;
likewise, he takes nine portions in the *pracaraṇī* ladle;
and likewise, this *āgnīdhra* priest distributes the embers from the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth onto the other hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*) in successive order.

In the same manner, sitting facing west in front [of the altar], he sprinkles the distributed *dhiṣṇiya* hearths. In the same manner, he places the *pracaraṇī* ladle on the chin of the northern *havirdhāna* cart.
In the same manner, by way of the visible path, he spreads the *pṛṣṭhyā* line continuously from the *gārhapatya* fire to the *āhavanīya* fire.
Then, having sat down between the two *havirdhāna* sheds, he asks for curds for the *dadhigharma*.
When it has been brought, he looks at it, saying: "Thou art the light of Vaiśvānara, the milk of the speckled cow.

Placing two blades of *barhis* grass in between, he takes [the curds] in either a bronze vessel or a wooden cup, saying: "As great as heaven and earth are in their magnitude, and as far as the seven rivers extend—so great, O Indra, is thy draught; with strength, I take thee, the invincible."

Having removed two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he then mixes it [with milk], saying: "May speech and mind mix you; may out-breath and in-breath mix you; may sight and hearing mix you; may skill and strength mix you; may vigor and force mix you; may life-span and old age mix you; may the self and the body mix you. You are cooked, you are made cooked; for the sake of what is cooked, for the sake of those who are cooked, make me cooked."
(8.3:237.12) Then he says, "O Hotṛ, speak what is to be spoken by you.
(8.3:237.12) Then, taking it up and rising, he says, "The oblation is cooked.
(8.3:237.13) Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Recite the offering prayer for the curd-mixture (*dadhigharma*)."

At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers [the oblation] with: "Him whom they call Indra, him whom they call Varuṇa, him whom they call Mitra, and him whom they call Truth; he who is the most divine among the gods, born of ascetic heat (*tapas*)—to him, to them, and to you, *svāhā*!
Having offered at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, he carries away the portion for consumption.

Having sought the invitation from as many officiating priests of the *pravargya* as there are, the sacrificer alone consumes [the portion] directly, [reciting]: "In me be that great power (*indriya*); in me be skill (*dakṣa*), in me be resolve (*kratu*). In me has been placed heroic vigor (*suvīrya*); may the three-fold *gharma* shine upon me."

(8.3:237.19) “With intention, together with the mind; with sovereign power, together with light; with sacrifice, together with milk; with the sacred word (*brahman*), together with splendor; with dominion, together with glory; with truth, together with austerity—may we partake of its milking, may we partake of its favor, may we partake of its consumption. Of that which has been drunk by Indra, which is honey-sweet, and which has been invited, being myself invited, I consume it. Having thus rinsed the vessel, he hands it over.
In the same manner, he requests the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) for the *savana* offerings.
Cutting portions from them in the same manner, he says: "Recite for Indra the sacrificial cakes being cut for the midday pressing.
Having cut from the front half, he cuts from the rear half;
he then pours clarified butter over them.
He anoints [the spoon] in the same manner; for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering in the *upabhṛt* ladle, he cuts portions once each from the northern half of all [the offerings],
and he pours clarified butter over them twice.
He does not anoint [the offering]. Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the sacrificial cakes set forth for Indra at the midday pressing.
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation.
Likewise, while pouring [the butter] together, he says, "Recite for Agni.
Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Prompt for Agni.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings.

(8.3:238.9) Having stepped across toward the north and placed the two *sruva*-ladles in their respective places, and having likewise gathered the *iḍā* in the vessel, he sends forth the sacrificial cakes toward the west.
(8.3:238.11) Some follow along, saying, "The cattle are the *iḍā*.
Then, moving eastward, he says: "Recite for those being lifted up!"

"Fill the cups following the Hotṛ's cup; make them bright on both sides; you, O Camasādhvaryu of the Acchāvāka, also fill your cup; O Pratiprasthātṛ, receive [the offerings] with four wood-shavings, some sprinkled and some unsprinkled.
Thus they act according to the direction. The ritual procedure is the same up to the *āśrāvaṇa* call.
The call for the *āśrāvaṇa* itself passes away.

Then the Adhvaryu, standing in front and facing west, causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause [them] to hear! "Let there be hearing! "For the exclusive portion of the midday pressing, for Indra, the Soma-draughts set forth—rich in *śukra*, rich in *manthin*, dripping with honey—issue the command!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, both of them sacrifice together, saying: "He is the first creator, the maker of all."
At the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, they offer twice;
in the same manner, they offer all the *camasa* cups twice each. Then he issues the direction: "Let the *camasa* of the Hotṛ go forward; let that of the Brahman go forward."
