Having turned clockwise in that manner, he pours the residue of the draught into the Hotṛ’s cup, either with the formula, "I pour thee, who hast been offered, into what has been offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men," or silently.
Likewise, the Pratiprasthātṛ offers the residue of the Manthin draught on the northern half of the Āhavanīya fire.
Having likewise touched water, he places both the Śukra vessel and the Manthin vessel on the mound (khara) in their respective places.
These goblets of the great officiating priests (*mahartvij*) proceed;
likewise, these cup-bearers (*camasādhvaryu*) of the assistant priests (*hotraka*) return after having drawn [Soma] from the *droṇakalaśa* vessel once each.
Having taken up the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa in the same manner, and having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "O *praśāstṛ*, recite the offering prayer (*yaja*)."
"O Brahman, sacrifice! O Potṛ, sacrifice! O Neṣṭṛ, sacrifice! O Acchāvāka, sacrifice! O Agnīdh, sacrifice!

Having thus performed the six *saṃyāja* offerings for the officiants (*ḍhotrāḥ*), he turns to the right, hastens back facing west, and sits down in front of the Hotṛ. "The Agnīdh has sacrificed," [the Hotṛ says];
"He has done what is auspicious," the Hotṛ replies, "he who will cause us to drink King Soma."
(8.4:239.13) Having likewise sipped water, they lift up the *iḍā* for the Hotṛ.
(8.4:239.14) While the *iḍā* is being invoked, they hold the cups close.
(8.4:239.15) Once the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places the sixfold portion (*ṣaḍavatta*) into the Āgnīdhra’s bowl.

They consume [the portions] and perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*). They consume the cups for which the *iḍā* has been invoked, reciting the long consumption formula (*dīrghabhakṣa*) as follows: "O Soma, come, enter me! O divine Soma, belonging to the troop of Rudra, who knowest the mind, of the midday pressing, having the *triṣṭubh* metre, drunk by Indra, full of sweetness, being invited, I, being invited, consume thee."
These three, having invited one another, consume from the *hotṛ*’s cup alone; they consume from their respective cups according to the cup-assignment (*yathācamasa*).
With the words, "Impel [the breath] for me," they touch themselves.
They swell the cups with the mantra, "Swell up; let [the milk] gather unto thee.
The *nārāśaṃsa* goblets, having been swelled, are set down below the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the third *marutvatīya* draught.
At this time, the sacrificer eats portions of the sacrificial cakes in the *āgnīdhra* shed.
If there should be food, it shall be in the wife's chamber for the wife.
(8.5:240.6) Now, when he is about to offer the *dakṣiṇā* oblations, he asks for the vessel of clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*) together with the *sruva*-ladle and the *sruk*-ladle, and a garment.
(8.5:240.7) At the end of this very garment, at the fringe, a piece of gold is tied.
(8.5:240.8) Having taken all this, he says: "Come, O sacrificer!"

Having gone around the north of the Āgnīdhrīya fire, having gone around the north of the Sadas, and having entered the hall by the eastern door, while the participants have taken hold of one another and the fires are covered, he melts clarified butter over the Gārhapatya, purifies it, takes four portions into the ladle, and, holding the end of the garment against the handle of the ladle, he offers on the Gārhapatya with two solar verses: "The rays bear up that god Jātavedas, the Sun, so that everyone may see him; Svāhā!
Thus.

Having taken another fourfold portion, he offers it in the Gārhapatya fire itself with the mantra: "The brilliant face of the gods has risen; the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. It has filled heaven, earth, and the mid-region. Sūrya is the soul of all that moves and stands. Svāhā!"

(8.5:240.16) Then, having run to the Āgnīdhra shed and taken four spoonfuls of clarified butter in the ladle, he holds the end of the garment against the handle of the ladle and offers it in the Āgnīdhra fire with the verse containing the word "lead": "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God who knowest all ways; keep away from us the crooked sin; we offer to thee the most abundant speech of homage, Svāhā! (8.5:240.19) Then, having offered a piece of gold with the words, "Go to heaven, fly to the light," he lifts it up.

The sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*) are released along the southern path: between the *sadas* and the *gārhapatya*, between the *sadas* and the *āgnīdhra*, and between the *cātvāla* and the rubbish-heap (*utkara*).
In this manner the northerners proceed;
having turned them clockwise, he approaches them with the formula: "I approach your form with my form, your vigor with my vigor."
(8.5:241.3) Then he distributes them, saying: "May Tutha, the all-knowing, distribute you upon the highest firmament.

(8.5:241.4) Then he approaches the Sadas, saying: "This gift of yours, O Agni, comes accompanied by Soma; lead it along the path of Mitra. Go forth along the path of Ṛta, O those with radiant dakṣiṇās, leading us to prosperity along the path of the sacrifice."
Then this descendant of Atri sits in front of the *sadas*.

He approaches him [with the thought]: "May I today succeed with a Brahmin who is a seer (*ṛṣi*), a descendant of seers (*ārṣeya*), who has a father and a grandfather, and who is accompanied by a well-bestowed sacrificial fee.
Then, stepping aside from him, he asks: "Who is the descendant of Atri?"
"I am he," the other replies.
Having stepped forward in the same manner for the second time, he asks, "Who is the descendant of Atri?
"I am he," the other replies.
Having stepped forward in the same manner for the third time, he asks: "Who is the descendant of Atri?
The other replies: "It is I.
He places gold into his hand with the words, "O Moon, bestow! as well as whatever else has been prepared.
(8.6:241.13) Then, having hastened to the Āgnīdhra shed, he gives [the gold] with its face toward the Āgnīdhra.
(8.6:241.14) Then, having come to the Sadas, he gives it to the Brahman, to the Hotṛ, and to the Udgātṛ.
(8.6:241.14) Then, having hastened to the Havirdhāna shed, he gives it to the Adhvaryu and to whoever else stands around him.

Then, having come to the *sadas*, he gives [the sacrificial fee] to the *prastotṛ*, the *praśāstṛ*, the *brahmānācchaṃsin*, the *acchāvāka*, the *sadasya*, the *āgnīdhra*, the *potr*, the *neṣṭṛ*, the *grāvastut*, the *unnetṛ*, the *subrahmaṇya*, and finally to the *pratihartṛ*.
To the *prasarpakas* he gives according to what has been agreed upon.
Then he says: "Come, O sacrificer!"

Having run to the Āgnīdhra shed and taken four portions of clarified butter into the offering-spoon, he offers five Vaiśvakarman oblations in the Āgnīdhra fire with the verse: "The seers have struck the lord of the sacrifice with sin.
Then he proceeds across [the altar] with the rites for deliverance (*atīmokṣa*), using these two sections: "With Agni as the god" and "Those gods who are slayers of the sacrifice.
Then he causes the sacrificer, facing eastward, to look [at the sun] with the words: "Behold the heaven; behold the intermediate space."
(8.6:242.4) Then he causes him to sit down in the *sadas* with the words: "Exert yourself together with those in the *sadas*.

(8.6:242.5) Then he points out the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*) with the formula: "Given by us, go among the gods, full of sweetness; enter the giver. Without abandoning us, sit in the world of the doers of good by way of the path of the gods; may that be prepared for us."
Then, as they are proceeding eastward, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Indra accompanied by the Maruts.
Having heard this, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the two cups and steps out.
As soon as he has stepped out, the Adhvaryu takes the two cups.
He hands one [portion] to the Pratiprasthātṛ standing to the north.
Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause it to be heard! "Let there be a hearing! "Command for Indra accompanied by the Maruts!
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, they both offer together.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the remnants of the draught from the Adhvaryu’s cup into his own.
He says to him: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, take the third Marutvatīya draught with this cup."

With that [cup], the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the third Marutvatīya draught from the Droṇakalaśa with the dipping-spoon, reciting: "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, as a bull for the battle... Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra accompanied by the Maruts. Having wiped it around, he sets it down with: "This is thy womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, thee!"

(8.7:242.18) Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened toward the west, causes the Hotṛ to consume this cup with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by Indra accompanied by the Maruts.
(8.7:242.19) Having held the cup, he turns away; as soon as he completes this sacrificial formula, he mutters: "Iḍā, the invoker of the gods.
(8.7:242.20) He continues to mutter for as long as it takes to finish this formula.
The Hotṛ calls out to him; the Adhvaryu responds;
[the Hotṛ] recites.
He responds.
Having responded to the *uktha* in the established manner, he goes forward and lifts up this third Marutvatīya cup; they lift up the Nārāśaṃsa vessels after him.
Then he causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: “O, cause to hear! “Let there be hearing! “O reciter of the hymns, sacrifice the Soma!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he offers twice.
In the same manner, they shake the *nārāśaṃsa* cups twice each.
The Nārāśaṃsa cups follow this vessel. The consumption is according to the occasion of the pressing: "Of that which was drunk by Indra accompanied by the Maruts.

Thus both the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu consume this vessel together. [They consume] the Nārāśaṃsa cups with [the formula for] what was drunk by Narāśaṃsa: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, belonging to the midday pressing, having the Triṣṭubh metre, drunk by the Fathers, full of sweetness, being invited, I, invited, partake."* (*This is an expansion of TS 3.2.5.2.)
Having invited one another, these three consume from the *hotṛ*’s cup alone; they consume from their respective cups according to the cup.
With the words, "Impel [the breath] for me," they touch themselves.
They cause the cups to swell with the mantra, "Swell up; let [the milk] gather unto thee.
The Nārāśaṃsa goblets, having been swelled, are set down below the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the sake of the Mahendra cup.

(8.8:243.14) Then, having gone forward to the east and taking up the *śukra* cup, he says: "O *unnetṛ*, when I take this *māhendra* draught, then cause the King [Soma] to flow through the *pūtabhṛt* filter toward the north; having wiped the *droṇakalaśa* with the fringes of the filter, turn it upside down.
He does so.

With the *śukra* cup, he draws the *māhendra* draught from the *droṇakalaśa*, reciting: "Great is Indra, who by his might... Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Mahendra. Having wiped it around, he sets it down, saying: "This is thy womb; for Mahendra, thee!
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the *stotra*.

They chant for the Mahendra cup. When the *sāman* has been introduced, he issues the direction: "O pressers, press! O *agnīdh*, pour out the milk-mixture; make the mortar resound! O *pratiprasthātṛ*, offer the cake on one potsherd for Varuṇa; take note of the offering for Soma! They act according to these directions.
"To the Hotṛ: 'This is the last,'" they say. After the time of the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu turns away;
the Hotṛ calls out to him.
The Adhvaryu calls back;
[the Hotṛ] recites; [the Adhvaryu] responds.
Having responded to the well-known *uktha*, he goes forward and lifts up this cup for Mahendra.
They lift up the *nārāśaṃsa* goblets in succession.
Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O, cause it to be heard! "Let there be a hearing! "O reciter of the *uktha*, offer the oblation of Soma! Thus.
At the *vaṣaṭ* call and at the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ* call, he offers twice.
In the same manner, they shake the *nārāśaṃsa* cups twice each time.
The *nārāśaṃsa* cups follow this vessel.
The formula for the consumption at each pressing (*anusavanabhakṣa*) is: "Of that which was drunk by Mahendra.

With this, both the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu consume this cup together with the Narāśaṃsa-portion: "O Soma, god, who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, belonging to the midday pressing, having the *triṣṭubh* metre, drunk by the Fathers, full of sweetness, being invited, I, invited, partake of thee. Thus [he says].
Having invited one another, these three consume from the *hotṛ*’s cup alone; they consume from the other cups according to their respective cups.
With the words, "Impel me," they touch themselves.
They do not swell the cups;
having consumed the entire contents, they perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*).
Then, with the formula "For Indra thee! For Indra thee!", he proceeds in this manner through the three *ukthya* rounds.

When the *uttama* cup has been filled in that same manner, he says: "Fill the cups following the *acchāvāka*'s goblet! O *unnētṛ*, draw out the entire *rājā* [Soma]; do not leave any remainder! O *pratiprasthātṛ*, rest with this cup! Come, O sacrificer!

Having thus caused him to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he then turns the *ādhavanīya* vessel upside down and pours all the *vasatīvarī* waters into it, and likewise all the *ekadhana* waters.
Having wiped the *vasatīvarī* pitcher in front of the axle, he turns it face down; [he does so] with the *ekadhana* jars behind the axle.
They draw the *acchāvāka*’s cup first.
Having poured out the others as they arise, they pour out all the kings and set them down upon the high altar.
Then he takes the auxiliary cup from the Ukthya vessel.
Into that [cup], he draws this entire king [Soma] which is in the *ukthya* vessel;
and that indeed belongs to Indra alone.
Then, having responded to the midday pressing with "The hymn has been recited," he says, "O *praśāstṛ*, give the impulse!"
"Creep along! says the Praśāstṛ;
thus the midday pressing is concluded.

They proceed toward the third pressing with the formula, "O divine doors! Having perceived them thus proceeded from that very point upward, the Adhvaryu, moving eastward, says: "O Agnīdh, bring the enclosure! O Pratiprasthātṛ, bring the milk-mixture! Bring curds for the *āditya* cup, which is to be heated! Come, O sacrificer!"

Having caused [the sacrificer] to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he pours into the midday *ṛjīṣa* that stalk which has been placed in the *upāṃśu* cup. Then, taking whichever pressing-stone he pleases, he says to the *unnetṛ*: "Bring it!
Pour it in! The *unnetṛ* pours from the *ādhavanīya* jar using a ladle.
Having pressed an unlimited amount, he then collects it well-pressed into the *saṃbharaṇī* vessel and hands it over to the *unnetṛ*.
The Unnetṛ pours that [mixture] into the Ādhavanīya vessel. In this very manner, the second round is completed;
likewise the third.
(8.9:245.16) Having wrapped the *ṛjīṣa* with the fringe of the *daśāpavitra*, he hands it to the *unnetṛ*.
(8.9:245.17) The *unnetṛ*, having rinsed it in the *ādhavanīya* jar and squeezed it out, carries it between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and places it in the interior (*nīḍa*).
(8.9:245.19) They enclose both the eastern and the western doors.
(8.9:245.19) Then he takes the supplementary cup from the Aditya-vessel.

(8.9:246.1) Into that, he draws the third portion of this King Soma which is in the Aditya-vessel, reciting: "Never art thou barren," and having run through [the rest], "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas."

Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the vessel and the milk], he mixes [the soma] with the *śrītātaṅkya* [mixture], reciting: "Never indeed do you fail... and continuing with: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas."

Having set aside two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he draws the half-measure of the King [Soma], reciting: "The sacrifice of the gods approaches for their favor," and then: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas."

(8.9:246.8) Then he mixes it with the thick portion using the *upāṃśusavana* stone, saying: "O Vivasvat Āditya, this is your draught of Soma; rejoice in it, be satisfied by it! May we, as those who satisfy you, be satisfied by you! With that which is the divine rain, with that I mix you.
(8.9:246.10) Then he lifts it up.
In this case, if the consciousness enters [the vessel] immediately, Parjanya becomes one who rains quickly; if it takes a long time, he becomes one who does not rain.
"He does not set it down"—so says the Brāhmaṇa.
Then, having wrapped that Upāṃśusavana stone with the fringe of the *daśāpavitra*, he scoops up the vessel from below with it, forming a wave-shape without spilling.

(8.10:246.14) "From the ocean and from the atmosphere, may Prajāpati cause the reservoir to flow; may Indra cause it to stream forth, and may the Maruts cause it to rain. "Make the earth swell; burst open this celestial cloud. Grant us of the celestial water; as the Lord, release the leather bag.
(8.10:246.16) Then, having wiped the *upāṃśusavana* stone with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*), he places it among the pressing stones.
(8.10:246.17) They open the eastern door and the western one.

(8.10:246.18) Then, having covered this cup with his hand by means of a blade of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and rising up, he says: "Recite for the dear Ādityas, whose abodes are dear, whose vows are dear, the lords of the great dwelling, the overseers of the wide mid-region!

(8.10:247.2) Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the dear Ādityas, whose abodes are dear, whose vows are dear, the lords of the great dwelling, the overseers of the wide mid-region!"
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, having cast the plants into the fire, he offers to Āditya only once.
Without having offered, he does not look back.
As soon as [the Adhvaryu] has turned around, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes up the vessel.
At this time, the Pratihartṛ, having spread the filter over the opening of the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, pours two or three ladlings of the King [Soma] into it.
The Adhvaryu takes up the Āgrayaṇa vessel,
and the Pratiprasthātṛ takes up the Āditya bowl together with its auxiliary.
From those three or four streams, having brought the Āgrayaṇa vessel over [the strainer], he receives it underneath.

Having likewise uttered the *abhihiṅkāra* three times over it and wiped it around, he sets it down. Having removed the filter and placed two blades of *barhis* grass in between, he pours in the *āśira* mixture while the wife maintains contact with him, reciting the four verses in their proper meters beginning with: "O gods, look upon us for the sake of beauty."
Having removed two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he consecrates the drops in the cavity of the *pūtabhṛt* vessel. He draws two cups for the *pavamāna*.
Likewise, he says: "O *unnetṛ*, cause the King [Soma] to flow forward into the *pūtabhṛt*; having cleansed the *ādhavanīya* with the fringes of the filter, turn it upside down."
He does so;
having likewise touched water and taken two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he steps out.
While they have likewise maintained contact with him, he offers a spoonful (*sruva-āhuti*) into the Āhavanīya fire.

(8.11:247.18) "This is the third pressing of the seers, who by means of the *ṛta* set the cup in motion. May those sons of Sudhanvan, having attained the heavenly light, lead our well-performed sacrifice toward greater prosperity—*svāhā*! With this verse, the two *adhvaryu*s offer the oblation.
The others offer according to their respective *veda*s. Then, having turned to the right, they proceed toward the *sadas* where the Soma is being pressed.

Likewise, they sit in the assembly hall according to their respective positions; then he gives two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) to either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, saying, "Thou art the under-layer for the Ṛc and the Sāman, for the procreation of the couple," or silently. Then he mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the maker of the *hiṅ* sound."
This very Ārbhava Pavamāna consists of seventeen verses.
When the ninth verse has been introduced, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art a companion, having the Jagatī as thy metre; I take hold of thee; convey me safely across.
At this point, he recites the Pañcahotṛ formula.

When the *sāman* has been chanted, he issues the direction: "O Āgnīdh, distribute the fire-sticks; spread the sacrificial grass; prepare the sacrificial cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, hold the dialogue regarding the animal sacrifice.
They perform according to the direction. Then, having touched water, he says: "Come, O Sacrificer."
Having caused [the sacrificer] to enter the Havirdhāna shed by the eastern door, he worships the King Soma in his entirety;
he does not perform the ritual with the *avakāśa* formulas here.
Likewise, he draws [the butter] nine times into the *pracaraṇī* ladle.

In the same manner, this Āgnīdhra distributes the fire-sticks (*śālākā*) from the Āgnīdhrīya hearth onto the other hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*) in successive order. Likewise, sitting in front and facing westward, he sprinkles the distributed fire-sticks with clarified butter.
Likewise, he places the *pracaraṇī* ladle on the front corner (*cubuka*) of the northern *havirdhāna* cart.
Likewise, he spreads the *pṛṣṭhyā* line continuously along the *sāṃkāśina* path from the *gārhapatya* fire to the *āhavanīya* fire.
Then he proceeds with the animal sacrifice, beginning with the *manotā* and ending with the *iḍā*.
Likewise, he requests the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) for the *savanīya* offerings.
Taking portions from them in the same manner, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for the sacrificial cakes being cut off for Indra at the third pressing."
Having cut from the front half, he cuts from the rear half;
he pours clarified butter over it and anoints it back.
Likewise, for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering in the *upabhṛt* ladle, he cuts portions once from the northern half of each [oblation];
he pours clarified butter over them twice;
he does not re-anoint [the offering substance].
Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the sacrificial cakes set forth for Indra at the third pressing.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. Likewise, while pouring together [the portions], he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni."
Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Agni.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings.
Then, having stepped across toward the north and placed the two ladles in their proper places, and having likewise gathered the *iḍā* in the vessel, he sends the sacrificial cakes westward.
Some follow along, saying, "The cattle are the *iḍā*.
Then, as they go forward toward the east, he says: "Recite for those being filled! Fill the cups following the *hotṛ*'s cup! Make them strong and mixed with milk! O *unnētṛ*, prepare the *soma*!
Thus, they fill the *hotṛ*'s cup first.
Having filled the other vessels as they come to hand, they place them upon the *uttaravedi*.

Then, having gone forward to the east and taken up the *hotṛ*’s cup, having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "Prompt [the *maitrāvaruṇa*] to recite the offering prayer for the Somas set forth for Indra—belonging to the third pressing, which are abundant, pervasive, powerful, rich in vigor, accompanied by Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods, and which are strong and mixed with milk."
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers with: "To the flying falcon, svāhā!
At the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* utterance, [he offers] with: "May the oblations of the honeyed ghee satisfy themselves, svāhā!
At both the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* utterances, he offers twice.
In the same manner, they offer all the *camasa* cups twice each.

Likewise, he issues the direction: "Let the *camasa* of the Hotṛ go forward; let that of the Brahman, the Udgātṛ, the Sacrificer, the Sadasya, and the Hotrakas go forward! O *camasādhvaryus*, having drawn [the soma] once each with the formula for the blessing (*āśīr*), return!
Then these *camasa*s of the great officiants proceed.

In the same manner, these cup-attendants (*camasādhvaryu*) of the *hotṛ*-assistants (*hotraka*), having drawn [the soma] once for each with the formula containing the word "blessing" (*āśīrvat*), withdraw.
For them, in that same way, having taken the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa and having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "O *praśāstṛ*, recite the offering-verse!
At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering with: "To the support of the cosmic order (*dharman*), svāhā!"
"For the enclosing-stick, for the spreading of the people"—thus for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
"For the vigor of the Hotṛ-offices"—thus for the Potṛ. "For the milk of the Hotṛ-offices"—thus for the Neṣṭṛ.
(8.12:250.5) “To Prajāpati, to Manu”—this is for the Acchāvāka. (8.12:250.6) “The Truth, the protector of Truth, the winner of heaven”—this is for the Agnīdh.
He pronounces the *anuvaṣaṭ* for each and every cup, saying: “May the Hotṛ-offices be satiated with the honey and the ghee; Svāhā!”

Having performed the *saṃyājya* offerings for the seven *hotṛ*s, he turns to the right, runs back toward the west, and sits down in front of the *hotṛ*. [The *maitrāvaruṇa* says: "The *agnīdh* has sacrificed.
[The *hotṛ* says: "He has done what is auspicious—he who will cause us to drink King Soma.
Having likewise touched water, they lift up the *iḍā* at the *hotṛ*’s station.
While the *iḍā* is being invoked, they hold the cups near.
When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places the sixfold portion (*ṣaḍavatta*) into the *agnīdh*.
They consume it.
They cleanse themselves.

They consume the cups for which the *iḍā* has been invoked, reciting the long *bhakṣa*-formula: "O food, come hither, enter me! Having recited this, they say: "Of thee, O divine Soma, who art accompanied by the host of the Ādityas, who knowest the mind, who belongest to the third pressing, whose metre is the *jagatī*, who art drunk by Indra, who art full of sweetness, and who art invited—I, being invited, consume thee.
Thus these three, having invited one another, consume the *hotṛ*'s cup alone.
Each touches his own cup with the formula, "Impel [the Soma] for me," and they cause the cups to swell with the formula, "Swell up; let [the milk] come together with thee."
The *nārāśaṃsa* cups, having been replenished, are set down one below the other along the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the sake of the *vaiśvadeva*.
For each and every cup, he places three fragments of sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa-śakala*) upon it;
nine [fragments] are placed upon the *hotṛ*-cup.
He addresses them with this very formula: "O fathers, rejoice here according to your respective portions.
At this time, the sacrificer eats the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) in the Āgnīdhra shed; if there is food, the wife eats it in the wife's quarters.
Then, while moving eastward, he says: "Recite for the god Savitṛ! O Pratiprasthātṛ, having drawn the Sāvitra cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Antaryāma cup, attend to it; do not let it settle!

Having heard this, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the Sāvitra cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Antaryāma cup, reciting: "O Savitṛ, what is lovely today... and continuing: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the god Savitṛ."
"He does not set it down," so says the Brāhmaṇa.
Without setting it down, having gone out and caused the announcement to be made, he says, "Prompt for the god Savitṛ!
and when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation.
Now, it is indeed said: "With the *savitṛ* cup, he draws the *vaiśvadeva* from the jar; he draws soma upon soma.

Thus, with the *savitṛ* cup, he draws the *vaiśvadeva* from the jar; he draws soma upon soma [with the formula]: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art a good refuge, a firm foundation. Homage to the Great Bull! I take thee, acceptable to all the gods."
Having wiped it around, he sets it down with the formula: "This is thy womb; for the Viśve Devas, thee!
Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and facing west, looks at the Hotṛ and turns away with the formula: "Iḍā, the invoker of the gods.
He mutters this as long as the recitation of this *yajus* continues.
The Hotṛ calls out to him; the Adhvaryu responds;
[the Hotṛ] recites.
He responds.

Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation, “With one and with ten, O self-existent one,” at that point the Pratiprasthātṛ, having cleansed the vessels for the dual-deity offerings at the Mārjālīya mound, places them back into the [original] vessels.

Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation, “The Heaven and Earth, increasers of Truth, through sacrifices,” at that point he responds to the *anyatomada* chant: “Othā moda iva, madā moda iva,” continuing until the call (*vyāhāva*).

Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ reciting, "That desirable gift of Savitṛ today," he responds with a *pratigara* that is "intoxicating on both sides": "madā moda iva madā moda iva," continuing thus until the *vyāhāva*.
Having responded to the *uktha* in the established manner, he goes forward and lifts up this cup for the Viśve Devas;
they lift up the Nārāśaṃsa goblets after him.
Then he causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be hearing! "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice the Soma!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he offers twice.
In the same manner, they shake the *nārāśaṃsa* cups twice each.
The Nārāśaṃsa cups follow this vessel.
The consumption is at each pressing with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the All-gods.

Both the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu consume this vessel together with the Narāśaṃsa cup, [reciting]: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, belonging to the third pressing, having the Jagatī metre, drunk by the Pitṛs, full of sweetness, and invited—I, being invited, partake."
These three, having invited one another, consume from the *hotṛ*’s cup alone; they consume from their respective cups according to the cup.
With the words, "Impel my [vital breaths]," they touch themselves.
They do not swell the cups;
having consumed the entire contents, they perform the ritual purification.
Then he asks the Hotṛ: "Will you perform the *pariya* for the *saumya* [oblation], or will you not?
Having heard how the Hotṛ replies to him, he approaches the prepared *saumya* [oblation].
Then, having taken four portions into the *sruc* ladle, stepped across, and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Recite the offering prayer (*yaja*) for the clarified butter."
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. Then, having spread a base of clarified butter, he takes two portions from the *caru*.
Having taken a portion from the eastern half, he takes a portion from the western half.

He pours the clarified butter over [the oblation], but does not anoint it back. Having stepped across and caused the announcement to be made, he says: "Recite the offering prayer for the Soma-oblation."
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*), he offers the oblation to Soma in the eastern part of the southern half of the fire.
Then he makes a supplementary offering (*abhijuhoti*) with a spoonful using a verse addressed to Viṣṇu: "O Viṣṇu, you are our nearest [kinsman].
If, however, the Hotṛ priest performs the concluding sacrifice (*pariyajati*) with a verse addressed to Agni and Viṣṇu, one need not take heed of whether the rite has been completed.
Having poured clarified butter into it, he gazes at it: "The Soma-vessel is indeed a purifier; they purify themselves."
"One who does not perceive his own self would be as one whose life has departed.
"Having made an *abhidadi* [a vessel with a handle], he should look into it.

Having poured more clarified butter (*ājya*) into that [vessel], he looks into it, saying: "That mind of mine which has gone away, or that which has not gone away—from King Soma, we maintain that [mind] within us."
(8.14:253.17) “The mind alone sustains the self; one whose mind has departed does not exist,” so says the Brāhmaṇa. (8.14:254.1) Then they carry him away to the Udgātṛs;
they perform upon him whatever rites they know.
(8.14:254.2) Then, as they are proceeding eastward, he says: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, having drawn the Pātnīvata cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Upāṃśu vessel, wait; do not let it settle.

(8.14:254.3) Having heard this, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the Pātnīvata cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Upāṃśu vessel, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; O Soma (Indu), I draw the Pātnīvata cup of thee, who art pressed by Bṛhaspati and possessed of power. [For Agni] who is accompanied by his wives... (agnā3i patnīvā3s).

Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the cup and the ground], he mixes it with ghee, reciting: "I am on high, I am below; by light I have dispelled the darkness. That which is the intermediate space became my father; I have beheld the sun on both sides. May I become the highest among my equals.
Having removed the two blades of *barhis*, he does not set the cup down—so says the Brāhmaṇa.
Without setting it down, having gone out and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "O *agnīdh*, recite the offering prayer for the Pātnīvata [cup]."

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers with the formula: "In unison with the god Tvaṣṭṛ, drink the Soma, svāhā! Having offered this in a low voice (*upāṃśu*) when the second *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he carries away the portion for consumption.
If that [Agnīdh] desires an invitation (*upahava*) from him in the Āgnīdhra shed, he indeed invites him; however, they do not consume together.

Then he says: "O Agnīdh, sit in the lap of the Neṣṭṛ! O Neṣṭṛ, lead the wife forward! Have her counted by the Udgātṛ; cause the waters to flow forth; cause them to flow forth with the thigh; cause them to flow forth after having uncovered the thigh! Fill the cups following the Hotṛ’s cup! O Unnetṛ, draw out the entire King Soma; do not leave any remainder! O Pratiprasthātṛ, make room for the Dhruvā in the Hotṛ’s cup! Come, O Sacrificer! Thus he says.

Having caused the sacrificer to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he makes him stand near the *dhruva* vessel with the formula: "Thou art the existent; place me in the existent! Thou art the mouth; may I become the mouth!
They draw the *hotṛ*-cup first, and the others as they come along.
Having poured out the entire quantity for the king [Soma], they set it down upon the high altar (*uttaravedi*).
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he, restraining his speech, hastens westward and introduces the chant.
They chant with the *yajñāyajñiya* stotra.

At this point, he recites the Saptahotṛ formula. When the *sāman* has been chanted, the Neṣṭṛ, having caused the wife to be looked at by the Udgātṛ, makes her recite: "O Agni, may I, in the sight of thee who art all-encompassing, all-possessing, and full of virility, obtain all desirable things and all seeds. The sacrifice has gone to the gods; the goddesses have bestowed blessings upon the sacrifice for the sake of the gods. For this pressing sacrificer, may the blessings consecrated with *svāhā* abide in the ocean. Standing in the ocean, she has approached the Gandharva; in the flight of the wind, the *iḍā*s have been praised."
When the Udgātṛ approaches her, then this wife causes the washing waters to flow over her thigh;
she causes them to flow over her thigh after having bared it.
"To the Hotṛ: 'This is the last,'" they say. After the time of the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu turns away;
the Hotṛ calls out to him.
The Adhvaryu calls back, recites the Śastra, and responds with the Pratigara.

(8.15:255.13) Now, when he recognizes the Hotṛ reciting, "Truly this is sweet, and this is honeyed," then he responds with the *ubhayatomoda*: "Modā moda iva! Madā moda iva! until the call (*vyāhāva*).

(8.15:255.15) Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ reciting, "Stretching the thread, follow the light of the mid-region," the Pratiprasthātṛ takes hold of the *dhruva* cup, saying, "I take hold of you for Heaven and Earth."

(8.15:255.17) Then he causes it to move forward with: "May all the gods, belonging to all men, cause you to move forward. (8.15:256.1) Then he brings it back with: "Make the gods firm in heaven, the birds in the intermediate space, and the earthly beings on earth.
(8.15:256.2) Then he pours it into the Hotṛ's cup with: "Firm with the firm oblation, we lead Soma down, so that our entire moving world may be free from disease and full of goodwill."

(8.15:256.4) "Just as Indra might make all these subjects entirely ours, of one mind; just as all the quarters might be ours alone"—having responded with this well-known *uktha*, he goes eastward and lifts up this *hotṛ*’s cup;
the other cups are lifted up after it.
Then he causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O, cause to hear! "Let there be a hearing! "O reciter of the *uktha*, offer the *soma*s!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he makes two offerings.
In the same manner, they offer all the *camasa*s twice each.
(8.15:256.9) Then they run toward the west with the portions for consumption.
(8.15:256.9) The formula for the consumption at each pressing is: "Of that which has been drunk by Agni Vaiśvānara and the Maruts, which is honeyed and invited, being myself invited, I consume.
(8.15:256.11) Having thus mutually invited one another, these three consume the *hotṛ*’s cup alone.
According to their respective goblets,
they touch themselves with the words, "Impel [the breath] for me," but they do not cause the goblets to swell.
Having consumed all [the remnants], they purify themselves.
Then, having filled these cups with water, he causes them to flow out to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, either towards the east or towards the north.
Into them he throws three knots of *dūrvā* grass each, and one tuft of *darbha* grass each.
Then, having responded at the third pressing with "The hymn has been spoken for Indra," [the Adhvaryu] says, "O Praśāstṛ, give the impulse!
The Praśāstṛ says, "Proceed!
Thus the third pressing is concluded.

(8.16:256.19) Then he issues the command: "O Āgnīdh, bring the embers for the supplementary offerings! O Upayaṣṭṛ, sit down! O Brahman, we shall set forth! Having placed the kindling-stick, O Āgnīdh, cleanse the fires once each!
(8.16:256.20) They bring those embers for the supplementary offerings from the Āgnīdhra hearth. He pours them out in front of the Hotṛ.
The *upayaṣṭṛ* priest approaches with the third portion of the rectum.
Then the *adhvaryu*, having divided the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) and poured it into the *juhū* ladle, steps across, calls for the *śrauṣaṭ*, and says, "Prompt for the gods!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering, saying, "Prompt! Prompt!"

Having performed eleven after-offerings (*anūyāja*), having stepped across to the north and placed the two offering-spoons (*sruk*) in their respective places, he separates the two spoons with the two *vājavatī* verses.

Having scattered the prastara-bunch and the enclosing-sticks together with the *śaṃyu*-formula, having poured out the remnants from the spoons and released them, he says to the Unnetṛ: "O Unnetṛ, proceed with your cup."

Having heard that, the Unnetṛ draws the third draught from the Droṇakalaśa belonging to the Āgrayaṇa vessel, [saying]: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art the bay one, the yoker of bays; the rider of the two bays, the bearer of the thunderbolt, the lover of Pṛśni. O divine Soma, for thee who hast the *iṣṭayajus*, whose *stoma* has been praised, and whose *uktha* has been recited, I draw the draught accompanied by the bays.
Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the vessel and the grains], he mixes it with parched grains, saying: "Ye are the two bays; ye are the parched grains for the two bays."

Having removed the two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and taken hold of him, he rises and says: "Recite the invitatory verse for the roasted grains (*dhānā*) and Soma for Indra accompanied by the Haris.

Having placed [the offering] upon his head and stepped forward, he calls for the *āśrāvaṇa* and says: "Prompt the Hotṛ to recite the offering verse for the roasted grains and Soma set forth for Indra accompanied by the Haris.
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation with: "Together with the Soma, to Indra, svāhā!"
Having offered at the secondary *vaṣaṭ*-call, he carries away the portion for consumption.
As many officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) as there are, to them the Unnetṛ distributes the parched grains (*dhānā*). Having sought permission from the Unnetṛ, they consume them one by one.
One oppresses [the other] with the mind.

"O divine Soma, whose *yajus* has been offered, whose *stoma* has been praised, whose *uktha* has been recited, who art accompanied by the *hari* horses, who art drunk by Indra, who art honey-sweet, who art invited—I, being invited, partake of thee.

Then, having washed them, they pour them out upon the *uttaravedi* with the formula: "May you be full; fill me with offspring and with wealth. While pouring them out, the sacrificer retains three grains for himself.
(8.17:257.19) Then he asks for the wooden sword (*sphya*), a vessel of water, and sacrificial grass (*barhis*).

(8.17:257.20) Having taken these up, he says, "Come, O sacrificer. (8.17:258.1) Having gone around the two *havirdhāna* sheds by the south and behind them, having dug up the ground to the south of the *mārjālīya* hearth with the wooden sword and sprinkled it with water, and having spread the sacrificial grass with its points directed toward the south, he purifies [the ancestors] with water, saying: "May the fathers be purified; may the grandfathers be purified; may the great-grandfathers be purified."

Then he gives three grains, saying: "This for you, O father, N.N., and for those who follow you; this for you, O grandfather, N.N., and for those who follow you; this for you, O great-grandfather, N.N., and for those who follow you."
Having said, "O fathers, rejoice here according to your portions," he turns toward the north and recites the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula there.

Then, having turned back and likewise sprinkled himself with water for purification, he returns by the same way he came and offers two spoonfuls of oblation on the *āgnīdhrīya* fire with the two verses: "Whatever deficiency has occurred in my self... and "Agni has given sight back again."

Then they perform the rite with wood-shavings in the Āhavanīya fire, saying: "Thou art the expiation for sin committed against the gods, svāhā! Thou art the expiation for sin committed against men, svāhā! Thou art the expiation for sin committed against the ancestors, svāhā! Thus.

(8.17:258.12) Then, having sat down around the Soma-offerings in the water, they consume them with the *avaghra* [smell] method: "O divine Soma, of thee who art washed in the waters, pressed by men, for whom the *yajus* has been sacrificed, the *stoma* praised, and the *uktha* recited—of that portion of thine which wins horses and which wins cattle, of thee whose consumption has been prepared by the ancestors and who art invited, I, being invited, partake.
(8.17:258.15) Then, having poured out those [waters] and having stood up, they worship the sun.
"We have drunk Soma; we have become immortal; we have beheld the light; we have found the gods. What can hostility do to us? And what, O Immortal One, can the malice of a mortal do?
With this *yajus*, even if the sun has already set, they worship the Āhavanīya fire.
Then, having run to the Āgnīdhra, they consume the drops of curd at the Āgnīdhra with the mantra: "I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan."
(8.18:259.1) Then they mutter the formula for the release from friendship: "Both are young seers; they are true, the lords of the law. O lord of the law of truth, we release our friendships.

(8.18:259.2) Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, having performed the offerings for the wives and having gone eastward, having replenished the *dhruvā* ladle, offers six verses containing the word *ṛgmia*: "May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ enjoy this."
(8.18:259.5) There are three *yajus* formulas: "O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice! This is your sacrifice, O lord of the sacrifice! O gods who know the way!
(8.18:259.6) Then, having taken four portions into the *sruk*-ladle, he offers the tenth oblation, [the verse] beginning: "O Agni, giver of life, enjoying the oblation...

(8.18:259.7) At this time, the sacrificer throws the black antelope horn into the *cātvāla* pit, either with the formula: "Thou art the womb of Indra; I set thee in the womb of the sacrifice," or silently.
(8.18:259.9) Then the Pratiprasthātṛ leads the wife forward; she silently throws a wooden pin into the Cātvāla pit.
At this point, they set down this *avabhṛtha* vessel in front of the *āgnīdhra* shed,

either on a raised platform or upon a hide. From the *patnīśālā*, they take the offering for Varuṇa— already spread with a base of ghee and sprinkled over— with the butter-pot together with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*), the ladle (*sruk*), sacrificial grass (*barhis*), two garments for wearing, a throne-seat of Udumbara wood for the King [Soma],
the Udumbara pillar from the *sadas*, and the staff of the Maitrāvaruṇa.

From the two *havirdhāna* sheds [he brings forth] the *pūtabhṛt* and *ādhavanīya* vessels, the cups, the pressing-skin, the two pressing-boards, six pegs, the pressing-stones, the *vāyavya* cups, the jars, the *droṇakalaśa*, the two *daśāpavitra* filters, and the dregs; all this together with the black antelope skin, and whatever else has been smeared with Soma.
Now, indeed, it is said: "They cast away the jars; they carry up the *vāyavya* cups."
Having taken this up, he says to the Prastotṛ: "O Prastotṛ, sing the Sāman!
The Prastotṛ follows along with the Sāman; he approaches the Nidhana three times.
"Every man attains the Nidhana," so says the Brāhmaṇa.

Then, between the Cātvāla and the Utkara, they go out toward the north, reciting: "For King Varuṇa has made wide for Sūrya a path to follow; he has made feet to be set down where there was no place to stand, and he is the remover even of that which pierces the heart.
At the midpoint, they perform the second Nidhana.

Having looked back at the water, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "A hundred are your remedies, O King, a thousand; may your benevolence be wide and deep. Drive away hatred and Nirṛti to the far distance; release from us whatever sin has been committed.
At the edge of the water, they perform the third *nidhana*.
Then they step upon the limit of the water, saying: "The noose of Varuṇa is stepped upon."

(8.19:260.9) Then he throws sacrificial grass (*barhis*) into the water with the verse: "The face of Agni has entered the waters; O Son of the Waters, protecting the power of the Asuras, O Agni, you shall sacrifice the fuel-stick in every house.
(8.19:260.11) Then he makes an offering over it with a spoonful: "May your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter, Svāhā!
(8.19:260.12) Then, having taken four portions in the *sruva* ladle, he performs four fore-offerings (*prayāja*), excluding the one for the sacrificial grass.
Then he proceeds with the two portions of clarified butter, [saying] "To Agni," "To Soma.
Then, having spread a base of butter, while taking a portion from the eastern half of the sacrificial cake, he says:
"Recite the invitatory verse for Varuṇa," [he says].
Having cut a portion from the eastern half, he cuts a portion from the western half;
he then pours clarified butter over it.
He anoints [the offering]. Having stepped across and caused the announcement to be made, he says, "Sacrifice to Varuṇa.
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation.
(8.20:260.17) Then, having spread an underlayer [of ghee] on all sides and placing the portion for Varuṇa upon it, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni and Varuṇa, the two Sviṣṭakṛts.
(8.20:260.18) He pours [ghee] over it twice.
(8.20:260.18) Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Recite the offering verse for Agni and Varuṇa, the two Sviṣṭakṛts."
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings.

Then, having taken four portions into the *sruva*-ladle, he performs two after-offerings (*anūyāja*) without the *barhis* grass. Then he places the *sruva*-ladle into the water with the mantra: "In the ocean is thy heart, within the waters."
(8.20:261.4) Then he fills it with water, [reciting]: "May the plants and the waters enter into you.
(8.20:261.5) He offers water into the water itself, [reciting]: "O Lord of the Sacrifice, may we worship you with the oblations of the sacrifice, with the *sūktavāka* and the *namovāka*; svāhā!"

At this point, they pour out this *avabhṛtha* (concluding purificatory bath), whatever has been smeared with Soma. [He recites: "O *avabhṛtha*, you who are deep-dwelling; you are a glider, O deep-dweller! Through the gods, may you wipe away the sin committed against the gods; through mortals, may you wipe away the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect us from wide-reaching harm! Then, he scoops up water with his joined palms, saying: "May the waters and the plants be friendly to us."
He sprinkles water toward that direction in which he has an enemy, saying: "May ill friends befall him who hates us and whom we hate.

Then, having touched water, they cause this *ṛjīṣa* to float away together with the black antelope skin, saying: "O divine waters, this is your embryo; we have made it well-pleasing and well-nourished for you. Proclaim us among the gods as doers of good deeds. He merely touches the drops.
He does not consume [the soma].
Then, without immersing themselves, they cause each other to run over their backs; having loosened their girdles and put on their lower garments, the Unnetṛ says to the other, "O Unnetṛ, lead us up!
With the three verses beginning with "upwards," they go upward: "Up from the darkness," "Up that one," and "The bright one."

(8.20:261.17) Then he splashes water toward the edge [of the pit] with the words: "The noose of Varuṇa is cast off; the noose of Varuṇa is thrown away. (8.20:261.18) Then they return without looking back, for the sake of concealment from Varuṇa.
On the road, they prepare the fuel sticks with the formula: "Thou art fuel; may we prosper.
Having arrived, he places them on the Āhavanīya fire with the formula: "Thou art a kindler; thou art brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me.
Then they pay reverence to the Āhavanīya with the verse: "I have followed the waters; we have united with their essence. Rich in milk, O Agni, I have come; unite me with splendor."
They dismantle the enclosures;
they turn the two *havirdhāna* sheds around, the southern one by the south and the northern one by the north.

While the Adhvaryu is occupied there, the Pratiprasthātṛ prepares the Udayanīya offering from the scrapings of the Prāyaṇīya. This very same Veda, this same stirring-spoon, and this same sacrificial grass [are used]. Then, having lifted up that pot for the cooked rice (caru), together with its scorched crust, and having washed it, he cooks the Udayanīya in it.
While that [grain] is being cooked in that same manner, he carries the *stambayajus* from behind the *gārhapatya* fire onto the *aupasadā* altar.
This is the well-known procedure for the cake-offering (*pauroḍāśika*).
He performs it three times with the *yajus* formula and a fourth time silently.
He performs the first tracing of the altar;
he mutters the *karaṇa* formula;
he digs up [the earth].
From the *uddhata* [fire], the Āgnīdhra carries it three times;
the ritual procedure is the same as that of the *prāyaṇīya* [offering].
Only this much is different.
He sacrifices the *pathyā svasti* first there [in the model sacrifice], and he sacrifices it as the penultimate offering here [in the modified sacrifice]. The quarters do not shift.
Then, prior to the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering, he offers an oblation with the *sruva*-ladle, saying: "O Agni, those which are all thy fuel-sticks..."
By means of the under-spreading and the over-sprinkling, they thus consume the clarified butter from the *dhruvā* vessel.
Some, however, offer the *samiṣṭayajus* oblation; the concluding rite (*udayanīya*) concludes with the *śaṃyu* formula.
At this point, he pours out this full vessel within the altar.
Then, having taken the portions of clarified butter mixed with speckled butter, he dedicates a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa.
Having performed the ritual with its omentum in the established manner, he has his hair and beard shaved at the southern edge of the altar.
He trims the hooves;
they perform the entire ritual procedure for the animal victim.
Now, if he does not obtain a barren cow, he cooks *āmikṣā* dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa over the *gārhapatya* fire and proceeds with it at the *āhavanīya* fire.
It concludes with the *ājyabhāga* offerings, the *pratipad*, and the *iḍā*.

(8.22:263.8) Then, having consigned the fires into the two kindling woods, having descended from the sacrificial ground, having churned out the fire, and having spread the fires, he offers the *udavasānīyā* sacrifice consisting of a cake on eight potsherds for Agni.
(8.22:263.9) Having cooked it, he places it down.
(8.22:263.10) For this sacrifice, there are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses.
There are five fore-offerings (*prayāja*s).
The two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*) are dedicated to Vṛtrahan.
Then, for the oblation: "O Agni, him today... and "For thus, O Agni... Thus [the verses].
The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
Having placed the *anvāhārya* rice, he gives a bull as a gift. That well-known sacrifice is thus concluded.

(8.22:263.13) Then, having consigned the fires into the two kindling woods, having descended from the sacrificial ground, having churned out the fires, and having spread them out, he offers the first Devikā oblations: a pap for Anumati, a pap for Rākā, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ.
(8.22:264.1) Having set down the *anvāhārya* mess of rice, he gives a heifer as a gift.
(8.22:264.2) That sacrifice concludes in the well-known manner.

Then, at that very moment, having spread the *pṛṣṭhyā* grass and having carried forward the waters, he offers the subsequent *devikā* oblations: a *caru* for Sinīvālī, a *caru* for Kuhū, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ.
Having set down the *anvāhārya* rice, he gives a young bull as a gift.
That sacrifice concludes in the well-known manner.

(8.22:264.5) Then, having consigned the fires into the two kindling woods, having settled upon his own fire-places, having churned out the fires and distributed them, he performs the evening and morning Agnihotra offerings.
(8.22:264.7) The Agniṣṭoma is completed; the Agniṣṭoma is completed.

(9.1:265.1) One who is about to collect the materials for the *pravargya* procures: a wooden shovel (*abhri*) made of *khadira*, *udumbara*, *veṇu*, or *vikaṅkata* wood, measuring one fathom (*vyāma*) or one cubit (*aratni*) in length and sharpened at both ends; prepared clay suitable for the purpose; a black antelope skin; earth dug up by a boar; a termite mound; a clump of *ūtīka* grass or a clump of wild millet (*vādāra*); goat’s milk; potsherds from a deserted site; pebbles ground with collyrium; wool from a black sheep; hair from a black antelope skin; a sieve; a workman skilled in his craft; a bamboo stalk; and boiling water.
(9.1:265.6) Then, having sacrificed with the new-moon oblation or under a [favorable] lunar mansion, they perform the preliminary pacification rite with the mantra: "Homage to Speech!
(9.1:265.7) Then, in front of the hall, at a distance of one bow-length from the altar, he causes a pit to be dug;
he then smears it with prepared clay.
He makes it level with the opening.
He places nearby a piece of earth dug up by a boar, a mound from an anthill, a clump of *ūtīka* grass, or a clump of *adāra* grass, as well as goat’s milk in a pan.
Then, having strewn grass with tips pointing eastward to the north of the ritual materials, he spreads upon them a black antelope skin with its neck toward the east and the hairy side upward.
(9.1:265.13) Then, having dug up the northern portion of the shed with the wooden sword from the front and having sprinkled it with water, he pours sand down.
(9.1:265.14) He makes that into a circular mound (*khara*).
(9.1:265.14) Then he makes it radiant by covering it with sand.
Having covered it with young *kuśa* shoots and knots of *dūrvā* grass, they then enclose it;
they make its door face north.
He places near it shards of pottery, pebbles, collyrium powder, black goat hair, hair from a black antelope skin, a hide-worker’s bench, a skilled worker, and a bamboo pole.
(9.1:265.18) Then he places the boiling water over the Gārhapatya fire. (9.1:265.19) He sets down the wooden shovel within the altar.
(9.1:265.20) They enclose the doors.
In the wife’s hall, they enclose the wife;
they strew grass around it.
To the south, the Brahman and the sacrificer sit down.
In this case, they perform the preliminary *śānti* rite for those whose [initiatory] rite has not yet been performed.

Having melted the clarified butter over the *gārhapatya* fire and purified it, and having taken four portions into the ladle, he offers the oblation to Savitṛ in the *āhavanīya* fire while the sacrificer maintains contact with him.

(9.2:266.5) “The inspired ones harness the mind and they harness the thoughts of the great, inspired, wise one. He alone, knowing the ways, ordains the priestly functions. Great is the praise of the god Savitṛ—svāhā! With these words he offers for one who is not consecrated;
he mutters it for one who is consecrated.
(9.2:266.7) Then he takes up the spade with the formula: "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee.

(9.2:266.9) Having taken it, he consecrates it: "Thou art a spade; thou art a woman; thou art a performer of the sacrifice for the gods. (9.2:266.10) Then, taking it, he stands up with the verse: "Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! We, seeking the gods, call upon thee. May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward; O Indra, be swift in our company."
(9.2:266.12) "May Brahmanaspati go forth! May the goddess Sūnṛtā go forth! Toward the hero, the manly one who bestows fivefold gifts—may the gods lead our sacrifice!
(9.2:266.13) Then he pays reverence to the prepared clay with the words: "O divine Heaven and Earth, may you both approve of me.
(9.2:266.14) He strikes with the wooden shovel: "May I succeed today at the head of Makha."
"〈For Makha thee!〉" with these words he carries [the earth];
"〈For the head of Makha thee!〉" with these words he pours it out on the black antelope skin to the north, having moved aside the place of worship.
In this very same manner he carries the second [portion].
In this manner, he goes around three times.
He goes around a fourth time silently and leaves a remnant for her.
Then he stands over the earth dug up by a boar, saying: "In the beginning, you were so much."
He strikes with the spade, saying: "May I prosper today at the head of Makha.
He carries [the earth] away, saying: "For Makha, thee!
He pours it out on the black antelope skin to the north, saying: "For the head of Makha, thee!", having moved aside the place of worship.
In the same manner he carries the second;
likewise the third;
silently the fourth.
He leaves over a portion for Paryeta.
Then he pays homage to the ant-hill with the words: "O divine ants, you are the first-born of this being, followers of the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
With a wooden shovel, he strikes it, saying: "May I today prosper through the head of Makha."
"Thou for Makha," with these words he carries [the earth];
"Thou for the head of Makha," with these words he pours it out on the black antelope skin to the north, having moved aside the place of worship.
In this very same way, he carries the second [portion].
In this manner, he does so a third time;
the fourth time he does so silently.
He leaves a remnant for her to go around.
(9.2:267.6) Then he stands by a clump of *utīka* grass or a clump of *vādāra* grass [with the words]: "Thou art the vigor of Indra.
(9.2:267.7) With a wooden sword (*abhri*), he strikes it [with the words]: "May I succeed today at the head of Makha.
(9.2:267.8) [With the words] "For Makha, thee," he carries it away.
(9.2:267.8) "For the head of Makha thee!"—with these words he pours [the grain] onto the black antelope skin to the north, having moved away from the place of worship.
(9.2:267.9) In this very same manner he carries the second [portion];
likewise the third.
(9.2:267.10) He silently leaves over a fourth portion for one who has walked around.
(9.2:267.10) Then he approaches the goat’s milk with [the formula]: "Thou art born of Agni, the seed of Prajāpati.
(9.2:267.11) He places the spade down with [the formula]: "May I succeed today with the head of Makha."
(9.2:267.12) "For Makha thee!"—with these words he carries [the vessel].
(9.2:267.12) "For the head of Makha thee!"—with these words he lets it drip onto the earth on the black antelope skin to the north, having moved aside the place of worship.
In this very same way, he lets the second [vessel] drip.
In this manner, he does it a third time;
silently, a fourth time.
Together with the fourth [libation], he sprinkles all of this goat’s milk from the vessel onto the clay.
At this point, they throw these leftovers into the water;
or they scatter them right there;
or they leave them lying about as an expiation.
Then they take up the *pravargya* vessel while bending down their heads and not breathing out.
They do not allow anything to come between the *pravargya* and the sun.
"Many carry it," so it is known from the tradition.

(9.3:267.20) Then they lead him forward with [the verse]: "May Brahmanaspati come; may the goddess Sūnṛtā come; toward the hero, the manly one who bestows fivefold wealth—may the gods lead our sacrifice."

(9.3:268.1) Then they bring him down onto the mound with the formula: "Bestow life! Bestow out-breath! Bestow in-breath! Bestow diffused breath! Bestow sight! Bestow hearing! Bestow mind! Bestow speech! Bestow the self! Bestow a firm foundation! Bestow me! Bestow [me] in me!

(9.3:268.4) Then, having mixed it with potsherds from a deserted site, with pebbles ground down with unguents, with the wool of a ram, and with the hair of a black antelope skin, he pours hot water over it with the formula: "May honey make thee sweet."
He forms a lump [of clay] with the formula, "Thou art the head of Makha.
With the formula, "Ye two are the feet of the sacrifice," he presses it down with his two thumbs.
Then, having cut off a third portion from the clay, he forms three lumps.
(9.3:268.8) He gives one of those [portions] to the maker with the words, "Thou art Gāyatra. (9.3:268.9) With that, he fashions its base, saying, "I fashion thee with the Gāyatrī metre.
(9.3:268.10) He gives half of the remaining clay with the words, "Thou art Traiṣṭubha."

With that, he makes its middle part, saying: "I fashion you with the *traiṣṭubha* metre. Finally, he hands over all the remaining clay, saying: "You are of the *jāgata* [metre]. With that, he makes its cavity, saying: "I fashion you with the *jāgata* metre."
He makes it one span long, broad at the base, and attached in the middle.
Then, with a section of bamboo, he pierces through two parts of it; that becomes its milking-pail.
(9.3:268.15) Then, at a distance of three or four finger-breadths from it, he winds a girdle around it with the formula: "Thou art the girdle of Makha.

(9.3:268.16) Then he takes its opening with the formula: "May Aditi take thy opening with the *pāṅkta* metre. (9.3:268.17) Then he heats it over the sun with the formula: "Be heated by the heat of Sūrya."
(9.3:268.17) Then he places it upon the mound. (9.3:268.18) Having placed it, he consecrates it with the mantra: "Thou art Makha.
(9.3:268.18) In this very same manner, he prepares the second *mahāvīra* vessel.
In this same manner, he performs the third [pouring].
He silently pours [the milk] into the two *pinvana* vessels, the two *rauhiṇa* potsherds, and the butter-pot.
Then, with whatever clay remains, he causes it to dry by exposing it to a windless spot where the wind blows against it.
When those winds have subsided, he prepares twenty-one dung-clods of a stallion, as well as a spade and a fire for baking.

Then, having kindled a horse-hair torch, he fumigates the principal *mahāvīra* vessel with the formula: "Thou art the dropping of the stallion; may Varuṇa, whose vows are firm, fumigate thee by the steadfast law of Mitra and Varuṇa.
Having thoroughly fumigated it both inside and out, he sets it down.
In the same manner, he fumigates the second *mahāvīra* vessel;
likewise the third.
He does so silently for the two *pinvana* vessels, the two *rauhiṇaka* potsherds, and the *ājyasthālī*.
(9.3:269.4) Then, to the north of the hall, he has a pit dug out like a wide-mouthed bowl.
(9.3:269.5) Having spread it with a cooking vessel, he arranges the *mahāvīra* vessels upon it, facing either east or north,
with the two *pinvana* vessels in front.
(9.3:269.7) Behind [the fire] are the two Rauhiṇa potsherds and the vessel for clarified butter.
(9.3:269.7) Then, having covered them from above with a baking-pan, he smears them with clay.
(9.3:269.8) He leaves an excess of four finger-breadths on each side for the purpose of kindling.
(9.3:269.9) Then he fasts.
(9.4:269.10) "For the flame, thee!"—thus in the east; (9.4:269.10) "For the radiance, thee!"—thus in the south; (9.4:269.10) "For the light, thee!"—thus in the west.
(9.4:269.11) "<For austerity, thee!">— thus [he offers] to the north.
(9.4:269.11) They ripen either by day or by night,
if he fasts in the morning and enters [the ritual] in the evening.

If it is in the evening or morning, when those [cakes] have been baked, he prepares cow’s milk, goat’s milk, a stirring-stick, a stone for grinding, a sieve, a pair of tongs, a winnowing-basket, a sling, and a black antelope skin.
Having taken all this together, he approaches [the fire] with the verse: “By his greatness, Mitra has become co-extensive with this heaven, and also with the earth through his glory.”
"Of Mitra, the supporter of the people, the fame of the god is winning; his splendor is most wonderful in renown.
Then he takes up the stirring-ladle with the formula, "For success, thee!
With it, he draws out the embers from the principal *mahāvīra* pot with the formula, "May the god Savitṛ draw thee out, he of the good hand, the good finger, and the good arm, by his power."

(9.4:269.18) Then he raises it up with: "Arise, become great; stand upright, you who are firm. (9.4:269.19) Then he establishes it in its base with: "Not falling upon the earth, fill the regions and the quarters.
(9.4:270.1) Then he gazes at it with: "I gaze upon you with the eye of Sūrya; for the upright, for the virtuous, for a good dwelling, for prosperity."

(9.4:270.3) Then he piles earth around it from left to right, saying according to the respective caste: "Here I enclose so-and-so, the son of such-and-such, with subjects, cattle, and Vedic splendor."

(9.4:270.4) Then, having grasped it with tongs and placed it in the vessel, he heats it with goat’s milk, [saying]: “I heat thee with the Gāyatrī metre; I heat thee with the Triṣṭubh metre; I heat thee with the Jagatī metre. May Vāc heat thee; may Urj heat thee; may the oblation heat thee. Sharpen Vāc; sharpen Urj; sharpen the oblation. O God, go forward; may I accomplish thee. Thus.
Having made it smooth both on the inside and on the outside, he moistens it with cow's milk.
In the same way, he coats the second *mahāvīra* pot;
in the same way, the third.
Silently [he prepares] the two milking vessels, the two Rauhiṇa potsherds, and the vessel for clarified butter.

Now, if a crack or a fissure occurs, he should scatter powdered stone into goat’s milk, sprinkle [the vessel] with that, and heat it over a firebrand while reciting the two verses: "The fleeing moon... and "Even when apart from the embrace...".
It indeed heals completely.

If, however, it should break entirely, he grinds these very potsherds without adding water, mixes them with that clay which lies set aside for expiation, kneads it, bakes it, and having let it cool, sets it down. When their hissing has ceased, he places them together in a winnowing basket, covers them from above with a black antelope skin, and hangs them on a sling in the northern part of the hall, so that the wife does not see them.
They remain lying there until that time.
Then they perform the subsequent pacification rite with the mantra: "May Vāta Mātariśvan blow auspiciously for us."

(9.5:270.21) "Tomorrow is the King's purchase. Thus [the Adhvaryu] should have prepared: a throne-seat (*samrāḍāsandī*) made of Udumbara wood; a pillar made of Udumbara wood; a milk-pail (*godohanī*) made of Udumbara wood; a pin for the she-goat made of Udumbara wood; a hoof-shaped support (*śaphopayamana*) made of Udumbara wood; a *sruva* ladle made of Udumbara wood; two *sruc* offering-spoons made of Udumbara wood; two unperforated *rauhiṇahavaṇī* vessels made of Udumbara wood; two fire-stirring sticks (*dhṛṣṭī*) made of Udumbara wood; three fans (*dhavitra*) with handles of Udumbara wood—or, according to some, with handles of bamboo (*vaiṇava*).

(9.5:271.3) Six chips of *udumbara* wood, a fuel-stick of *vikaṅkata*, thirteen enclosing sticks of *vikaṅkata*, a *vikaṅkata* offering-spoon (*pracaraṇī*), enclosing sticks made of *kārṣmarya* wood, two gold and silver plates, two milch-cows for the *gharma* oblation, one he-goat, two *kuśa*-grass altars, one *muñja*-grass altar, an unwashed *muñja*-grass rope-belt, cuttings of *muñja* grass, flour for the *rauhiṇa* cakes, and sand for the mounds.
Then he proceeds with the introductory sacrifice (*prāyaṇīya*).
Having performed the *prāyaṇīya* offering, he performs the *pada* rite;
having performed the *pada* rite, having purchased and brought back the King Soma, he offers the *ātithya*.
Having performed the *ātithya*, they proceed to the first *śānti* with the words: "Homage to speech! (*namo vāce*).

(9.5:271.10) Then, having strewn grass in front of the *gārhapatya* fire, they set down all these items used for the *gharma* rite: here the throne-seat of the sovereign (*samrāḍ-āsandi*), here the pillar for the *godohana* water-pot, and here the peg for the she-goat.
(9.5:271.12) Then, having dug up the ground to the north of the *gārhapatya* with the wooden sword (*sphya*) and sprinkled it with water, he pours down sand.
He makes that mound for the Pravargya rite one span high and circular.
Then he makes it free from cracks by covering it with sand.
Then, to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, having dug up the ground with the wooden sword (sphya) and sprinkled it with water, he pours down sand.
He makes that mound for the *udvāsanīya* offering one span wide and circular. Then he covers it with sand so that it is free from cracks.
Then, on the northern side of the wooden splinter (*śalākhaṇḍa*), having dug up the ground with the wooden sword (*sphya*) and sprinkled it with water, he pours down sand.
He makes that mound for the remains square and provided with a channel for drainage. Then he covers it with sand so that it is shining.
Then the Adhvaryu, having grasped the Mahāvīra vessel intended for use with its two lifting-prongs, places it upon the mound used for heating.
(9.5:272.1) Then he covers it with a cord of muñja grass.
(9.5:272.2) Then, having carried this throne-seat around the front of the Āhavanīya fire, he places it to the south.
(9.5:272.3) Upon it he spreads a black antelope skin with the neck pointing eastward and the hair side up.

(9.5:272.4) Then, having taken those two *mahāvīra* vessels that lie near by, and having carried them around the front of the *āhavanīya* fire, he places them on the black antelope skin upon the *samrāḍāsandi* throne to the south, with their openings facing east.
(9.5:272.6) Then, having carried this spade around the front of the *āhavanīya* fire, he places it on the black antelope skin upon the *samrāḍāsandi* throne to the south.
(9.5:272.7) Then, having carried this remaining clay around the front of the *āhavanīya* fire, he places it on the black antelope skin upon the *samrāḍāsandi* throne to the south.

(9.5:272.9) Then, having taken this pillar, the milking-vessel, and the peg for the goat, and having walked around the south of the Gārhapatya fire along its rear, and having brought them out through the southern door, they fix the pillar within the sight of the Hotṛ; they bind the calf of the Gharma-milch cow with a cord of muñja grass.
(9.5:272.12) Having fixed a peg to the north of that [pillar], they tie up the goat. (9.5:272.13) They turn the kid over onto its back.
(9.5:272.13) Then, having returned by the same way they came, they cause the Vṛṣalas to go out.
(9.5:272.14) They summon the Hotṛ;
they summon the Brahman.
They call for the Pratiprasthātṛ; they call for the Prastotṛ;
they call for the Āgnīdhra.
They enclose the doors;
they enclose the wife in the *patnīśālā*;
they strew [the grass] around.
The Brahman and the sacrificer sit down to the south;
here they perform the first *śānti* rite for those whose [ritual] has not yet been entered upon.

(9.6:273.1) Then the Adhvaryu, taking up the sprinkling waters together with the strainers, says: "O Brahman, we shall proceed with the Pravargya. O Hotṛ, recite for the Gharma. O Āgnīdh, place the two Rauhiṇa cakes on the fire. O Pratiprasthātṛ, spread out the Pravargya materials. O Prastotṛ, chant the Sāmans."

Then the Brahman gives the impulse: "The one yoked with the *yajus*, whose surface is anointed with the *sāmans*, who is authorized by all the gods and the Maruts, extended by the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*), and capable of carrying us across—let the chanters (*stubh*) carry him while he is well-disposed. Bestowing radiance upon us, do not be ill-tempered! Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ! Om! Accompanied by Indra, proceed! Thus he says.
(9.6:273.6) Then the Adhvaryu sprinkles the Mahāvīra vessel used for the performance with the formula: "For Yama thee! For Makha thee! For the heat of Sūrya thee!
(9.6:273.8) Reaching each successive set of materials, he sprinkles them;
the Pratiprasthātṛ distributes that very Pravargya equipment.
Then he lays the enclosing-sticks made of *kārṣmarya* wood around the Āhavanīya fire.

He places nearby six chips of *udumbara* wood, a fuel-stick of *vikaṅkata* wood for the Gārhapatya fire, thirteen enclosing-sticks of *vikaṅkata* wood, two plates of gold and silver, cuttings of *muñja* grass, and the flour for the *rauhiṇa* cakes.
Then the Āgnīdhra priest, having sat down behind the Gārhapatya fire, draws out embers toward the west with two stirring-sticks and places upon them the two *rauhiṇa* potsherds.

(9.6:273.14) Then, having mixed the flour combined with the coarse ingredients, he places the two *rauhiṇa* sacrificial cakes on the fire. (9.6:273.15) Then he pours out the clarified butter; then he places the clarified butter on the fire.
(9.6:273.15) Having carried fire around both [the Mahāvīra and the Rauhiṇa cakes], he bakes the two Rauhiṇa sacrificial cakes.

(9.6:273.16) At this time, the Pratiprasthātṛ wipes with a mat of Muñja grass the vessels intended for the oblation—the Mahāvīra, the dipping-spoon (*sruva*), the two milking-bowls (*pinvana*), the two Rauhiṇa-offering spoons, and the supporting-stand (*upayamana*).

(9.6:273.18) Then the Pratiprasthātṛ, having purified the clarified butter, having removed the two Rauhiṇa sacrificial cakes after spreading a base of ghee and pouring ghee over them, and having grasped them with the two Rauhiṇa-offering spoons, places them within the altar.
(9.6:273.20) One [wick] along the southern junction of the enclosing sticks, (9.6:273.21) the other along the northern junction of the enclosing sticks;
(9.6:273.21) both directed eastward during the morning session.
(9.6:273.21) The two [offerings] for the afternoon are directed westward.

(9.6:274.1) Then the Adhvaryu, having grasped the Mahāvīra vessel used for the performance with the two hooves and having turned it into his left hand, offers seven continuous Prāṇa-oblations on the Gārhapatya fire with clarified butter taken once from the butter-pot, without drawing breath, [reciting]: "To the out-breath, svāhā! To the diffused-breath, svāhā! To the in-breath, svāhā! To the eye, svāhā! To the ear, svāhā! To the mind, svāhā! To speech, Sarasvatī, svāhā! Thus.
(9.6:274.5) The four subsequent [offerings] are made as they arise: "To skill, svāhā! To resolve, svāhā! To vigor, svāhā! To strength, svāhā!
(9.6:274.7) Then he anoints it with clarified butter, saying: "May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey.
At this time, the Pratiprasthātṛ hides a silver plate in the mound for the heating-fire, saying: "Protect the earth from the heat."

Then, having intertwined stalks of *muñja* grass, he sets them on fire with the formulas: "Thou art flame," "Thou art glow," "Thou art light," "Thou art heat. Having scattered them upon the mound for the *pravargya*, he places the *mahāvīra* vessel to be used in the *pravargya* rite among them.
(9.7:274.12) “Sit down; you are great. Shine forth, O best invoker of the gods! O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, emit your ruddy smoke, O praised one, that it may be beautiful to behold.

(9.7:274.13) Then he fills it with clarified butter, saying: “Him whom the inspired poets anoint, spreading him out like a skin, heating him with fire as if he were fat—like a son in the lap of his father, the beloved Gharma has sat upon the fire, performing the rite.”
(9.7:274.15) Then, with a span, he establishes the directions for it: "Unassailable from the east, under the overlordship of Agni, may you grant me long life," thus in the east;

(9.7:274.17) "Possessing sons from the south, under the overlordship of Indra, may you grant me progeny," thus in the south; (9.7:274.18) "Easy to sit upon from the west, under the overlordship of the god Savitṛ, may you grant me breath," thus in the west.
(9.7:274.19) "May hearing be granted to me under the overlordship of Mitra and Varuṇa from the north," he says as he places [the stone] to the north.

(9.7:275.1) "May support be granted to me from above under the overlordship of Bṛhaspati; may you grant me spiritual power (*brahman*); may you grant me sovereign power (*kṣatra*); may you bestow radiance upon me; may you bestow luster upon me; may you bestow glory upon me; may you bestow ascetic heat (*tapas*) upon me; may you bestow mind (*manas*) upon me," he says as he places [the stone] from above.
