If his [Agnihotra] should have been commenced with clarified butter or with vegetable food, having offered that, he should make the remnant of the Agnihotra from that very same substance."
"The sprinkling of the vessels for the *sāṃnāyya*."
Baudhāyana says that one should sprinkle with water consecrated silently;
Śālīki says [with water] contained in a water-pot.
Then, having sat down behind the Gārhapatya fire, he draws out embers toward the north with the *upaveṣa* stick.
Śālīki holds that there is a specific sūtra for this.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should remove the embers silently; indeed, this entire formula should be the mantra for placing [the oblation] upon the fire."
(20.4:11.14) Regarding the placing of the milking-strainer: thus it is said.
"One should prepare [the offering] with the mantra and place it in the pot with the mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"one should prepare it silently and place it in the pot with the mantra," says Śālīki;
"one should prepare half with the mantra and place half in the pot," says Aupamanyava.
(20.4:12.1) "The consecration of the cows."
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should consecrate each one of these with its respective mantra, and then have each one of them milked.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should consecrate all of them together with a single mantra, and then have each one of them milked.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should consecrate all of them together with a single mantra, have them all milked at once, and in this very manner complete the pouring out of the drops."
Aupamanyavīputra says that one should bring each individual [rite] to completion by means of the entire ritual procedure in its entirety.
(20.4:12.7) "The consecration of the drops."
The *sūtra* belongs to Śālīki.
The explanation belongs to Aupamanyava.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should indeed recite the mantras over the drops after they have been curdled.
For it is precisely here that the end of the drops occurs.
"The milking of the Uttarās is [to be performed]."
"Baudhāyana says that one should cause the other cows to be milked after releasing speech and without maintaining physical contact.
Kātya says that one should maintain contact while the cow is being led forward and should restrain speech."
"Of one who obtains milk. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the mantras beginning with the driving away of the calves;
Śālīki says they begin with the pouring [of the milk].
Regarding the term "ātañcana" (the act of curdling).

Baudhāyana says that one should bring the dipping-spoon (sruva) at the fourth [pouring], with as much [milk] as one thinks will cause it to curdle; Śālīki says that one should bring the dipping-spoon at the third [pouring], with as much as one thinks will cause it to curdle.
"He sprinkles the remnant of the Agnihotra with [the milk]," so it is said.
Śālīki holds that the sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having brought the remnants of the agnihotra, one should bring the curdling agent for the oblation;
in this way, both [the oblation and the remnants] become thoroughly mixed."
"He covers it with water," so it is said.
Baudhāyana says that one should cause it to lie overnight covered with water;
Śālīki says that, having covered it with water, one should pour out those waters and then cover [the vessel] again.
Regarding the strewing around the fires: thus it is said.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should strew around the fires on the very day of the fast (upavasatha), according to how they were produced.
For thus the Brāhmaṇa says: "The deities dwell with him who, knowing this, strews around the fire, thinking, 'Tomorrow I shall sacrifice to them.'"
"Eating and fasting."
"One should eat forest produce and water," says Baudhāyana;
"only water," says Śālīki;
"neither forest produce nor water," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the touching of the hands.
Standing to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, one should rub one's hands together—so says Baudhāyana.
To the north of the Gārhapatya fire—so says Śālīki.
Regarding the strewing around the fires: thus it is said.
The rule is that of Śālīki.
That of Aupamanyava has already been explained.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first strew around the Gārhapatya fire to the east, then to the south, then to the west, and then to the north."
"In the same way one should strew around the Anvāhāryapacana fire, and in the same way the Āhavanīya fire."
Regarding the placing of the vessels.
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should spread grass to the north of the Gārhapatya fire and place the vessels upon them;
one should place the vessels to the north of the fire-hall.
Rāthītara says that one should take from them according to their respective shares.
Regarding the seating of the Brahman priest.
Baudhāyana says that one should move away and sit down to the south of the Āhavanīya fire; Śālīki says that one should sit down to the south of the Āhavanīya fire without moving away at all.
"The seating of the sacrificer."
"One should move away and sit down to the south," says Baudhāyana;
"one should sit down to the south without moving away," says Śālīki.
"The spreading of the *pṛṣṭhyā* [line]," so it is said.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should spread the *pṛṣṭhyā* line only for the Soma sacrifice.
Regarding the preparation of the two strainers.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Aupamanyava says [it should be] of the grasses from the pṛṣṭhyā line.
Śālīki says [it should be] of those other kuśa blades that have not been used.
He remains silent from the time the *praṇītā* waters are being poured out until the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*).
Baudhāyana says that one should converse with these [priests] while smiling inwardly during the ritual junctions;
Śālīki says that one should have released speech.
(20.5:15.4) This is the explanation of the Hotṛ priests.

(20.5:15.4) One [view] is that [the offerings are made] with the *graha* cups and without the *svāhā* calls; (20.5:15.5) another is that [they are made] without the *graha* cups but with the *svāhā* calls at the end; and yet another is that [they are made] for all [of them].
The first option is that of Baudhāyana; both the latter ones are those of Śālīki.
"This is the exposition of the Daśahotṛ."
(20.5:15.7) Having led forward the *praṇītā* waters, the two teachers say that one should recite the *daśahotṛ* formula while running toward the west.
(20.5:15.8) Aupamanyava says that one should do so only when about to take the handful [of grass].
(20.5:15.9) Regarding the pouring out [of the oblation]: |||
Śālīki says that one should [use] the sūtra [of Baudhāyana].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should pour out [the grain] from the cart itself;
having touched both poles, one should step across the axle-end with the formula: 'May Viṣṇu step over you.'"

Having looked at the materials for the sacrificial cakes, he should touch them with the formula, "May the five restrain themselves," three times with the *yajus* and once silently for those who follow the four-fold portioning (*caturavattin*). For those who follow the five-fold portioning (*pañcāvattin*), he does so three times with the *yajus* and twice silently.
Kātya says that one should perform all of them with the sacrificial formula.
(20.6:15.14) Regarding the taking of a fivefold portion: it is thus.
Baudhāyana says that one should proceed with the fivefold cutting from the time of the pouring out [of the oblation];
Śālīki says from the time of the cutting; Aupamanyava says from the time of the offering.
Aupamanyavīputra says [the rule applies] from the *cātuṣprāśya* onwards.
"The sowing of the remaining [grains]."
"Baudhāyana says that one should sow them either in a granary or in a pit;
Śālīki says that one should sow them right here."
"The pouring out of the clarified butter."
Śālīki holds that the *sūtra* [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having reached the end of the vegetable offering, one should pour out the clarified butter;
in this way, it obtains sprinkling together with the other oblations."
(20.6:16.3) "Entrusting" means:
"One should hand over [the oblation] exactly as it was poured out," says Baudhāyana.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should simply say, 'O Agni, protect the oblation'; and for milk, 'O Viṣṇu, protect the oblation.
For Viṣṇu is the protector of milks, and Agni is the protector of plants."
The purification of the sprinkling waters.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should recite this verse while pouring it out; Śālīki says that one should pour it out three times while reciting this verse.
Regarding the sprinkling of the materials for the sacrificial cakes.
"One should sprinkle [the water] by sections," says Baudhāyana;
"having recited the names of the deities in succession, one should do so exactly three times," says Śālīki.
Regarding the sprinkling of the vessels.
Śālīki holds that the sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Be purified for the divine rite; the vessels for the sacrifice to the gods."
"The remaining [food] is for lying down around."
"Baudhāyana says that one should lie around these very [bricks].
Śālīki says that after pouring water over them, one should prepare other [bricks] on top."
(20.6:16.16) Regarding the shaking out of the black antelope skin.

(20.6:16.16) Having gone out from the fire-hall, one should shake out the black antelope skin in the northwestern intermediate direction, says Baudhāyana. (20.6:17.2) One should do so within [the hall] toward that same direction, says Śālīki.
Regarding the spreading of the black antelope skin: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform this ritual action without releasing the focus [of concentration]: from the shaking out of the black antelope skin until its spreading;
likewise from the placing of the mortar until the pouring in of the grains for the sacrificial cakes;
likewise from the setting down of the pestle until the pushing forward of the winnowing basket.
Thus from the pouring [of the grains] until the scattering;
thus from the placing of the potsherds until the two acts of arranging and piling on the fuel; thus from the *prastara* grass-bundle until the setting down of the offering-spoons.
Thus [the procedure is] from the taking up of the spade until the digging;
thus from the offering over the Audumbarī post;
thus for the sacrificial post until the encircling with the cord.
Śālīki says that one should perform these rites exactly as they happen to arise.
"The receptacle for pouring out the grains for the sacrificial cakes."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should pour out five handfuls for those who perform the five-fold cutting.
(20.7:17.12) "They strike the lower and upper grinding stones loudly with a bull's bellow."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says it should be with the yoke-pin alone.
(20.7:17.14) "The sweeping of the winnowing basket."
Śālīki says that one should follow the *sūtra*.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should silently shake out the winnowing basket;
with that same mantra, one should pour out the grains for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśīya*), saying: "Thou art increased by rain; may the rain-increased [grain] receive thee!"
(20.7:18.1) Then, having turned toward the north, he purifies [the water] by sprinkling.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
“Having turned toward whichever direction [he chooses], he purifies,” says Śālīki.
"The discarding of the husks."
Śālīki says that one should [use] the sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having cut off as much as is required from right there, one should scatter [the hair] starting from the neck of the black antelope skin with the formula, 'Thou art the portion of the Rakṣases. Then one should touch water."
(20.7:18.6) Regarding the re-spreading of the black antelope skin: it is as follows.
The thread [should be placed] by the two teachers;
according to Aupamanyava, with its ends pointing eastward and its knot facing north.
(20.7:18.8) Regarding "grinding":
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "With 'For breath, thee,' one should push it forward; with 'For out-breath, thee,' one should push it backward; with 'For diffused breath, thee,' one should drag it across. Then one should push it forward again with 'Along a long extension, may I establish myself for life.'"
He should cause the flour to fall onto the black antelope skin with the formula: "May the god Savitṛ, the golden-handed, receive you."
(20.8:18.13) Śālīki says that the taking up of the *dhṛṣṭi*-spoon does not occur when there is only one sacrificer, nor when there are many.

(20.8:18.13) Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should take up the *dhṛṣṭi* from the very beginning with the formula, 'Thou art the *dhṛṣṭi*; restrain the Brahman. (20.8:18.15) He should then address the *gārhapatya* fire with the mantra: 'O Agni, drive away the fire that devours raw food.'"
(20.8:18.16) Reciting, "Drive away the flesh-eater," he should cast out a coal from the southern side.

(20.8:18.16) Then he should arrange the others. (20.8:18.17) Reciting, "Bring the one who sacrifices to the gods," he should place the pot for the *caru* offering upon them. [He should recite: "Thou art firm; make the earth firm; make life firm; make offspring firm; heap around the kinsmen for this sacrificer."
Then he should surround it clockwise with embers, saying: "The Rākṣasas are burnt up! The enemies are burnt up!
In this very manner, he should place all the pots for the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) upon the fire.
"At the mouths of the sacrificial offerings," it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should take up the *dhṛṣṭi* from the very beginning and prepare the portions for consumption from the principal [oblation] itself.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the taking up of the *dhṛṣṭi* indeed occurs at the time of joining the potsherds.

(20.8:19.6) While about to place the potsherds, he should take up the fire-stirring stick (dhṛṣṭi), thinking, "I shall prepare the portions for consumption from the sacrificial cake itself. (20.8:19.7) Thus it is said.
Regarding the placing of the potsherds: [the rule is as follows].
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Indeed, his potsherds are placed according to the traditional injunction; however, one should first apply that same mantra which is used for the turning over of the embers during the placing of the potsherds, and then turn over the ember silently."
"One-potsherd" and "two-potsherd."
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Whether it be a cake on one potsherd or on two potsherds, one should place it using all the mantras for the potsherds.
On this point, Śālīki used to say: "One should place the potsherds according to their respective positions;

however, one should not imply the addition of further formulas, but rather recite the heating mantra here: 'Be heated by the heat of the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases; may you two be heated; may you all be heated.'"
This is the application of the potsherds.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "These [bricks] of his are joined with those very mantras with which they were originally laid down;
thus, for the other [bricks], there should be only the mantra for unloosing."
(20.8:20.4) Regarding the placing [of the grains] upon the boiling waters: |||
Baudhāyana says that one should pour the water across the strainer and then place [the vessel] over the fire;
Śālīki says it should be done as the occasion arises.
(20.8:20.6) "The kneading."
Śālīki says that one should [use] the sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should take up water with the dipping-spoon from the *praṇītā* waters and pour it [into the vessel]; likewise from the *madantī* waters."
As both of these are being brought forward, he should address them with the mantra: "The waters have come together with the waters."
(20.8:20.9) "Sexual assault," it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should indeed touch [the offering] separately even for a single oblation,
and likewise for various seeds. Regarding this,
Śālīki used to say that the separate touching arises indeed from the mixing [of the grains].
One should not touch the sacrificial oblations while they are being mixed together, nor a single oblation.
For who would perform a separate touching for various seeds?
"The pouring out of the clarified butter."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki;
the explanation is that of Baudhāyana.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Having completed all the oblations, one should then pour out the clarified butter."
Regarding the pouring out of the water for the *āpya* offering: [the rule is as follows].
(20.8:21.3) "One should pour out [the water] for the Āpyas behind the Gārhapatya," says Baudhāyana. (20.8:21.4) "Having passed along the front," says Śālīki.
(20.8:21.4) "Either along the front or along the rear," says Aupamanyava.
(20.9:21.6) "The disposal of the wooden sword."
The rule is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "That mantra which is for lifting up the wooden sword (sphyah), one should employ it first among those performing the consecration; then one should lift up the wooden sword silently."
Regarding the tracing out of the altar: [the view is that] it is for the sake of the altar.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first enclose the buttock, then the right shoulder, and then the left.
Aupamyava, however, says: "One should enclose it from the front, proceeding in a clockwise direction."
"The one who stirs up [the fire]."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should level it with the fourth [layer] and then raise it up with the fifth.
Regarding the placing of the *prokṣaṇī* waters: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana says that one should pour [the water] along the track of the wooden sword (*sphya*) and then set it down;
Śālīki says that one should do so without pouring [it].
Regarding the placing of the fuel and the sacrificial grass.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says it is the northern fuel-bundle.
"In the cases of the *vedaparivāsana* offerings."
"Baudhāyana says that one should wipe the spoons after dividing them into five parts; Śālīki says that one should do so with all the water at once, pouring it over each."
The wiping of the *prāśitraharaṇa* vessel.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should wipe [the ladle] silently; Aupamanyava says that one should not wipe it at all.
(20.10:22.11) Regarding the throwing into the fire of the wiping-off of the *sruva* and *sruk* spoons:
Śālīki says that one should throw away the cord.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should sprinkle it with water and cast it aside in a place where people pass, or on the rubbish-heap;
the same applies to the firewood-bands.
(20.10:22.14) Regarding the girding of the wives: thus it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should gird each cow individually; one should have each look at the Gārhapatya fire; one should have each look at the clarified butter.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should gird all of them together at once; one should have each look at the Gārhapatya fire; one should have each look at the clarified butter."

Regarding this, Aupamanyava said: "One should bind all of them at once, cause them to look at the Gārhapatya fire at once, and have each one look at the clarified butter. Aupamanyavīputra, however, said: "One should complete each one individually with the entire ritual procedure."
(20.10:23.4) "The making of knots."
"The noose is cast downward and the release is upward," so say the two teachers;
"the noose is cast upward and the release is downward," says Dīrghavātsya;
for in this very way offspring are born.
"When the wife is not present."
Baudhāyana used to say that the sacrificer himself, sitting in his own place, should recite these formulas.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "These formulas are indeed seen to be connected with the wife;
if she is absent, one should not pay any heed to them at all."
(20.10:23.11) Then he causes her to look at the clarified butter.
The sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should take up that which has been looked upon by the wife with the formula, 'Thou art brilliance' (*tejo 'si*). Then, having taken it up with a splinter of wood, one should carry it away with the formula, 'Follow after the brilliance' (*tejo 'nu prehi*)."
(20.10:23.13) Then he should place it over the Āhavanīya fire [with the formula]: "May Agni not take away your brilliance.

(20.10:23.14) Having lifted it up and set it down to the north of the *prokṣaṇī* waters, and having looked at it, he should purify the *prokṣaṇī* waters with the two [spoons] containing clarified butter.
(20.10:23.16) Regarding the inspection of the clarified butter: //
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should purify the clarified butter that has been inspected by all [the priests], says Śālīki.
Regarding the taking of the portions of clarified butter (*ājyagraha*).

Baudhāyana used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas, those belonging to the cake-offering (pauroḍāśika) and those belonging to the sacrificer (yājamāna); and the sacrificer should follow along with the formulas belonging to the sacrificer. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas, those belonging to the cake-offering and those belonging to the sacrificer.
"One should not have the sacrificer recite the formulas belonging to the sacrificer," [it is said].
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Just as the formulas pertaining to the cake-offering do not recur, even so the formulas belonging to the sacrificer should not recur."
(20.10:24.8) Regarding the sprinkling of the fuel and the sacrificial grass: //
"One should sprinkle each one three times," says Baudhāyana;
"once each," says Śālīki.
Regarding the sprinkling of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
The sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: one should stand and sprinkle the tips with the formula, "For heaven thee!"; then, bending down, sprinkle the middle parts with "For the intermediate space thee!"; and sitting down, sprinkle the roots with "For earth thee!"

Having sprinkled the knot from the front toward the west together with the offering-ladle, he should pour out the remaining sprinkling water from the southern hip to the northern hip with the formula: "Svadhā to the fathers! Be nourishment for those who sit on the sacrificial grass! Go to the earth with nourishment!"
"The lifting up of the offering-spoons."
"One should throw it up towards the north in front of oneself," says Baudhāyana;
"One should throw it up towards the north behind oneself," says Śālīki.
He inserts the two strainers into the *prastara* bundle, either with the formula, "I place the out-breath and in-breath in the sacrificer," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
He hands it over either to the sacrificer or to the Brahman priest.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
"The place for the cord," [he said].
(20.11:25.7) Regarding the sūtra, Baudhāyana says that one should spread the cord after untying it at the southern edge of the altar; Śālīki says that one should spread it [after untying the cord].
Regarding the strewing of the altar.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should spread it from this very point toward the east, layer by layer.
Regarding the laying down of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should place the southern [fire] on top and push the northern one underneath.
Śālīki says: "One should enclose them while they are still touching at their front."
(20.11:25.14) Now, [the rule] says: "Then he should enclose [the fire] from the east with the Sūrya [verse]."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should worship the Āhavanīya fire alone with this sacrificial formula.
"One places two fuel-sticks upright," so says the Sūtra; this is the view of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki, however, says that one should place these two upright and not let them fall over.
Regarding the making of the *vidhṛti* strainers.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.

Regarding this, Dakṣiṇākāra Rāthītara used to say that both of these [fires] should be interlaced across the altar; Aupamanyava says they should be situated from the middle layer without an inner womb.
(20.12:26.4) "The setting down of the milking-strainer."
Baudhāyana says that one should set down the *prastara* after untying it; Śālīki says that one should do so without untying it at all.
(20.12:26.6) "The placing of the offering-spoons."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should set down the *upabhṛt* as if it were slightly tilted back, and one should hold it down with the two *vidhṛti*s.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should set them down in their proper sequence and should not hold the *upabhṛt* down with the two *vidhṛti*s.
Regarding the removal of the sacrificial oblations.

Baudhāyana says that [the portions] are not removed from the front and are removed from the rear; Śālīki says that they are removed from the rear and not removed from the front; Aupamanyava says [this is done] by means of cutting off.
Regarding the term "pratyañjana" (counter-anointing).
Baudhāyana used to say that one should anoint both [the vessels], namely the bowls for the caru-offerings and the potsherds; Śālīki says that one should anoint only the potsherds.
The ritual release of the potsherds belongs to the office of the Adhvaryu priest.
At the point [of the text] "having removed the oblations," the two teachers release [the sacrificial implements].
Aupamanyava says that one should release the potsherds at the conclusion of the consuming of the portions, while still in the act of consuming them.
"The two libations," he says.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that the two reins should be interlaced like those of a chariot;
this refers to the formal command (*saṃpraiṣa*).
(20.12:27.8) "O Agnīdh, [bring] the fires," says Baudhāyana. "O Agnīdh, [bring] the fire," says Śālīki. "O Agnīdh, [bring] the enclosing sticks and the fire," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding "stepping across": [it refers to] stepping over [the fire].
(20.12:27.10) Baudhāyana says that one who intends to offer with the left hand should step across after having shaken [the grass] from that side, [and offer] with the right;
(20.12:27.11) Śālīki says that one who intends to offer with the right hand should step across after having shaken [the grass] from that side, [and offer] with the left.
(20.12:28.1) [This concerns] the call for the *āśrāvaṇa*.
"O, cause [the announcement] to be heard! says Baudhāyana;
"Cause [the announcement] to be heard! says Śālīki; "Announce! says Aupamanyava.
"The Pravara."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having struck the wooden sword (sphya) with its point upwards into the rubbish-heap (utkara), one should choose the Pravara; then one should cast the wooden sword aside right there and touch [the earth] above it."
"The choosing of the Hotṛ."
Baudhāyana used to say: "If his father, or teacher, or an elder should be the *hotṛ*, he should pronounce the names of these elders in a low voice.
Śālīki says: "One should pronounce the name of the *hotṛ* loudly."
"One offers while stepping forward."
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should step forward with the whole body—with the feet, with the oblations, and with the voice;
one should offer each subsequent oblation in a larger measure than the preceding one.
Śālīki says: "One should step forward only with the feet and offer the oblations in the same place."
Aupamanyava says that while standing in one place, one should advance toward the oblations.
Āñjīgavi says that while standing in exactly the same place, having offered to each direction in clockwise order, one should make an offering with the utterance of *svāhā* in the center.
The oblation of the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*).
Baudhāyana says that one should offer the oblations facing each other with arms extended in the eastern half; Śālīki says they should be offered with arms extended in the eastern half alone.
Regarding the portioning of the sacrificial oblations.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first take a portion from the front half of the principal oblation, and then from the rear half;
in this way, the portions of the oblations are taken in a clockwise direction.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should first take a portion from the rear half of the principal oblation, and then from the front half."
"In this way his oblations are oriented toward the east," says Aupamanyava; "for those who take five cuttings, [the portions are] from the middle, from the eastern half, and from the western half."
"The abode of the oblations," [he said].

Baudhāyana used to say: "These three alone have their places specifically prescribed: the two *ājyabhāga* offerings and the *sviṣṭakṛt*. As for the others, one should offer them according to available space.
Śālīki says: "While offering the *praṣṭi* oblations, one should offer the *sviṣṭakṛt* in the eastern part [of the fire]."
"One should offer the oblation in the ladle along the path of the *āghāra*," says Aupamanyava;
"in the middle, moving clockwise in a circular form," says Rāthītara.
Regarding the performance of the *upāṃśuyāja* offering.
This is the Sūtra of Maudgalya.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform the *upāṃśuyāja* with the herb-offering: the *agnīṣomīya* at the full moon and the *vaiṣṇava* at the new moon.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should perform the *upāṃśuyāja* with clarified butter: the *saumya* at the full moon and the *vaiṣṇava* at the new moon.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should perform the *upāṃśuyāja* with an herb-offering for Sarasvant on the full moon day, and for Sarasvatī on the new moon day.
Rāthītara says: "On both occasions, it should be performed with clarified butter for Viṣṇu.
Regarding this, Kauṇapatantri used to say: "There should be a rice-pap (*caru*) for Viṣṇu, and the sacrificer himself should consume it."
"By the increase of the fifth portion."
Baudhāyana says that one should increase the quantity of the medicinal herbs;
Śālīki says that one should increase the quantity of the clarified butter alone.
Regarding the throwing of the stirring-spoon into the fire: [the view is that] it should be thrown in.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should not throw the two omentum-spits into the fire according to the rule for the stirring-stick."
Regarding the cutting off of the *prāśitra* portion.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should cut off the *prāśitra* portion only while actually about to carry it around.
When the *anvāhārya* rice is prepared, there is an oblation of clarified butter (*ājya*).
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the *anvāhārya* rice.
Baudhāyana says that one should carry it around in front of both the sacrificer and the Brahman and place it on the southern buttock;
Śālīki says that one should place it on the southern buttock from that very spot.
Regarding the removal of the *anvāhārya* rice.
Baudhāyana says that one should remove the offering-ladle northward in front of it;
Śālīki says that one should remove it northward behind the ladle.
(20.14:31.3) Regarding the removal of the remnants of the sacrificial oblation: |||
Baudhāyana says that one should remove [the oblation] northward in front of the offering-spoons;
Śālīki says that one should remove it northward behind the offering-spoons.
The offering of the after-offerings (*anūyāja*).
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that one should conclude these oblations facing westward.
Regarding the spreading out [of the altar] with the two *vājavatī* verses.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should push back the *upabhṛt* oblation-ladle diagonally toward the west and touch it with water.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should drag these two [ladles] apart while their bowls face eastward, and one should not touch the *upabhṛt* with water."
(20.14:31.12) Regarding the smearing of the *prastara* grass-bundle.
"One should anoint each [part] three times," says Baudhāyana;
"once each," says Śālīki.
Regarding the throwing of the *prastara* grass-bundle into the fire.

Baudhāyana used to say: "The Adhvaryu alone should perform the final offering with both sets of formulas—those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* section and those belonging to the sacrificer (*yājamāna*).
The sacrificer should recite the formulas along with the Adhvaryu.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "The Adhvaryu alone should perform the final offering with both sets of formulas—those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* section and those belonging to the sacrificer."
"One should not have the sacrificer recite the formulas belonging to the sacrificer," [it is said].
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Just as the formulas pertaining to the cake-offering do not recur, even so the formulas belonging to the sacrificer should not recur."
Regarding the placing of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should place them on the fire only at the time of departure.
(20.14:32.5) Then he makes an offering over them with the residue of the oblation.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should offer oblations over both the *prastara* and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*); Śālīki says that one should do so only over the *prastara*.
(20.14:32.7) "The release of the two offering-spoons."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
(20.14:32.9) Regarding the circumambulation of the officiating priests during the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: “All should circumambulate to the north of the Gārhapatya fire,” says Śālīki.
(20.15:32.11) "The joint sacrifice for the wives."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
one should perform the offerings to the wives with the clarified butter from the *dhruvā* vessel while making a humming sound; thus says Śālīki.
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the offerings to the wives of the gods with an intervening [oblation]; Śālīki says that one should do so without any intervention at all.
(20.15:32.15) Regarding the recitation of the *śamyuvāka* during the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
(20.15:32.17) Regarding the swelling of the *dhruvā* ladle.
Baudhāyana used to say that both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer should cause the *dhruvā* ladle to swell;
Śālīki, however, says that the Adhvaryu alone, having caused the *dhruvā* to swell, should offer the *samiṣṭayajus*.
The offering of the *samiṣṭayajus* oblation.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.

Regarding this, Gautama used to say: "Svāhā to speech! Having sacrificed thus, having torn off portions from the base of the sacrificial grass (barhis), and having anointed them with clarified butter and cast them into the Dhruvā ladle, he should sacrifice over them, saying: "Svāhā! Place [it] in the wind, svāhā!"
Now, therefore, we shall explain the establishment of the sacred fires (agnyādheya).
(20.16:33.8) "Regarding the requisites."
The *sūtra* [prescribes] the *rāthītara* verses.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should not perform the *aśanihatam* (the 'struck by lightning' hymn), for it is of a terrible form.
[However, one] should indeed perform the *aśanihatam*.
But not a nest of muñja grass;
for its lineage is not known, says Śālīki.
(20.16:33.12) Regarding the making of the vessels: [the rule is as follows].

Baudhāyana used to say that one should have the pouring-channels made at the edges with the lotus-petals facing forward; thus his offering-ladles, when placed down, have their petals directed toward the east. On this point, however, Śālīki used to say that one should have the pouring-channels made at the edges with the lotus-petals facing toward the base.
Thus it is known: "In this way his offering-ladles have their bowls facing eastward when set down; therefore the trees dwell upon the earth with their tips pointing downward."
(20.16:34.1) Regarding the measurement of the offering spoons (*sruc*): [the text continues].
"They should be the length of an arm," says Baudhāyana;
"the length of a cubit," says Śālīki; "the length of a span," says Aupamanyava.
(20.16:34.3) "It is a modification of the shape of the offering-ladles."
Baudhāyana says they should have the lips of an elephant; Śālīki says they should have the tails of crows; Aupamanyava says they should have the beaks of swans for pouring.
(20.16:34.6) "Regarding the preparation of the *ambarīṣa*."
Baudhāyana says that one should place the fire-pan to the north of the fire-hall;
Śālīki says that one should go to wherever the fire-pan may be.
The circumambulation of the fire-hall.
(20.16:34.9) "To the south," says Baudhāyana;
"to the north," says Śālīki.
"On a red hide," [he says].
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that it may even be without a mounting-block.
(20.16:34.13) Regarding the *brahmaudana*: with mantra or without mantra?
Baudhāyana says that one should perform it with the mantra, while Śālīki says it should be done silently.
(20.16:34.15) "The offering of the *brahmaudana*."
Baudhāyana says that [the water] should be poured with a vessel provided with a strainer and accompanied by a mantra; Śālīki says it should be done with a vessel without a strainer and silently.
(20.16:35.1) Regarding the cooking of the *brahmaudana* (the rice for the Brahman).
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana;
"in water," says Śālīki.
"One should neither pour into this [vessel] nor pour out from it," says Baudhāyana;
"One may pour into it at will, but not pour out from it," says Śālīki; "Having let it drain, it should be provided with broth," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the spreading of the base for the *brahmaudana* rice porridge.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not spread an underlayer.
(20.16:35.8) "The concluding rite of the *brahmaudana*."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that they should sit around right here.
(20.16:35.10) "The pushing away of the *brahmaudana*."
"May the sacrifice approach me," he says, or silently;
the former alternative is Baudhāyana's, the latter is Śālīki's.
(20.16:35.12) Regarding the consumption of the *brahmaudana* rice porridge.
(20.16:35.12) "Only those belonging to the lineage of ṛṣis (ārṣeya) should consume the *brahmaudana*," says Baudhāyana. (20.16:35.13) "Whoever are restricted in their diet," says Kātya.
(20.16:35.14) Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that only the great officiating priests (*mahartvij*) should consume the *brahmaudana*.
"For in this very case, these [officiants] become accompanied by the *anūnaptrī* offerings."
Regarding the placing of the fuel-sticks upon the fire.
Śālīki says that this is the rule of the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Once the [sacrificial food] has been tasted and before it is wiped away, one should anoint the fuel-sticks and place them on the fire.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should anoint these very sticks along their sides right there and set them down."

When they have all eaten, he should then wash this vessel, spread a base of ghee in it, pour into it once whatever ghee remains in the pot, and having anointed the fuel-sticks with that, he should place them on the fire.
(20.16:36.7) "The making of a cow," so it is said.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
One may even perform many [such acts].
Kātya says that there should also be a meritorious recitation of praise for this [person].
Regarding the handing over of the two kindling woods.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "At the very end of the night, one should hand over the two kindling woods (*araṇī*) to him;
or rather, one should release the speech [with the words], 'I grant you a boon.'"
(20.16:36.13) Regarding the smearing of the fire-places: [the rule is as follows].
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should smear only the site of the Gārhapatya fire-altar, for it is that which becomes burnt.
(20.16:36.16) [The ritual rule concerning] the scattering of the preparatory materials.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Having completed these [pots] with all the mantras at the very site of the Gārhapatya fire, one should distribute them into three parts."
(20.17:36.19) "The carrying of the sacrificial fuel."
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first carry [the earth] knee-deep, then navel-deep, and then neck-deep;
however, one must not carry it so high as to exceed the vital breaths.
While taking it up, one should ensure these measurements are precisely attained.
"One should not, however, cut away the vital breaths," says Śālīki.
"The treading upon the ritual requisites."
Śālīki says that this is the rule for the Sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In this very manner, one should have him step forward with the right front foot, turned back toward the east, so that he might tread upon the materials from the side on the north, such that the embers of the fire already established would fall down [upon them]."
Regarding the gift of a horse.

Baudhāyana says that one should give this horse, which stands in the place of Agni, to the Adhvaryu, and another to the Brahman; Śālīki says that one should give this to the Brahman, and another to the Adhvaryu.
Regarding the placing of the fuel.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should place the fuel silently.
Regarding the establishment of the Sabhya and Āvasathya fires.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
(20.17:37.12) Regarding the ritual distribution of the *sabhya* and *āvasathya* fires.
"One should carry these two [fires] from the Āhavanīya," says Baudhāyana;
"from the village fire," says Śālīki;
"they should be produced by friction," says Aupamanyava.

Regarding this, Aupamanyavīputra used to say: "One should designate the *sabhya* fire as being in the assembly hall (*sabhā*), and the *āvasathya* fire as being in the guest-quarters (*āvasatha*); and on the festival days (*parvan*), having cooked two *sthālīpāka* offerings for these two, one should offer them to the Brahman.
Āñjīgavi, however, said that even this should not be done.
(20.17:38.1) "Regarding the making of a chariot wheel."
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should cause this very chariot, when yoked, to move forward in an easterly direction.
"One should give that to the officiating priests"—
even this he should not do, says Āñjīgavi.
This is the enumeration of the bodily forms.
Baudhāyana says that one should recite [the mantra] in response and then direct [the offering];
Śālīki says that one should simply say: "O Agni, with those forms of yours which are terrible, go to so-and-so."
"In the sequences of the Virāj," so it is said.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana:
[one should recite] "O manly one, protect my offspring. Śālīki says that one should simply say this.
Regarding the offering of the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
one should offer the full-offering (pūrṇāhuti) only after the altar has been enclosed, says Śālīki.
At the *pūrṇāhuti*, however, the *agnihotra* offering is performed silently.
The *sūtra* belongs to the Rāthītaras.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer only the *pūrṇāhuti* (full-offering), and not the silent *agnihotra*.
Śālīki says: "One should offer only the silent *agnihotra*, and not the *pūrṇāhuti*."
"This is the exposition of the Daśahotṛ."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Whenever one is about to pour out the oblation or is about to recite the *sāmidhenī* verses, one should indeed recite the *daśahotṛ* formula there. Śālīki says that this is seen only in these ritual procedures (*tantra*) pertaining to the establishment of the sacred fires (*āgnyādheya*).
Aupamanyava says that this is seen specifically in this very *āgneya* cake on eight potsherds.
(20.18:39.4) Regarding the performance of the ritual manual: "tantrakaraṇa" means the composition of the ritual manual.

Baudhāyana used to say that there should be fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should have the *vārtraghna* formulas, and the deities should be invoked loudly. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that there should be seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should have the *vṛdhanvat* formulas, and the deities should be invoked in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that for the cake on eight potsherds for Agni, the two *ājyabhāgas* should have the *vārtraghna* formulas; for those for Indra-Agni and the Ādityas, they should have the *vṛdhanvat* formulas; for the oblations to Pavamāna, they should have the *rayimat* and *puṣṭimat* formulas; and for the *anvārambheṣṭi*, they should have the *vītavat* formulas.
"The performance [of the ritual] belongs to the sacrificer."
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the sacrificer’s duties by calling out the names [of the priests].
Śālīki says that one should perform the duties of the sacrificer according to the available opportunity.
(20.18:40.1) Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
The Sūtra [follows] Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should perform all these offerings as being accompanied by sacrificial fees;
one should give three [cows] for each [offering], and a pair [of animals] for the last one."
(20.18:40.4) "A compound with an intervening word."
There is no common ritual procedure (*tantra*) for the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava said: "The cake on eight potsherds for Agni Pavamāna should constitute the first ritual procedure;
then [the cakes] for Agni Pāvaka and Agni Śuci constitute the second."
(20.18:40.6) Then, let the oblation for Indra and Agni and the oblation for Āditya go around to the end.
(20.18:40.8) Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā).
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki. That which has been explained is the view of Baudhāyana.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should perform all these sacrifices as being accompanied by sacrificial fees; one should give four [cows] at each [of the first three], and a pair at the last."
(20.18:40.11) Regarding the performance of an expiation for one who has not performed the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices in their proper sequence.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"At the Anvārambheṣṭi," so it is said.

Baudhāyana says that one should perform the Caturhotṛ, the two Sārasvata oblations, and the Anvārambheṣṭi on the day of preparation (upavasatha), while the rest should be performed on the day of the sacrifice (iṣṭyaha). Śālīki says that one should perform the Caturhotṛ and the two Sārasvata oblations on the day of preparation, while the rest should be performed on the day of the sacrifice.
Aupamanyava says that one should perform only the Caturhotṛ on the day of preparation, while the rest should be performed on the day of the sacrifice.
Aupamanyavīputra says that one should perform all of this on the day of the sacrifice.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the re-establishment of the sacred fires.
"In the *sarparājñī* verses," so it is said.
The Sūtra [prescribes] that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should establish the Gārhapatya fire with the verses of the Serpent Queen; having established it with six [verses], one should worship it with the seventh."
Regarding the performance of the *pūrṇāhuti* offering.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
(20.19:41.7) Regarding the formulation of the ritual manual (*tantra*):
Śālīki says that the Sūtra [is correct].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform both types of rituals: those pertaining to the re-establishment of the fires (*paunarādheyika*) and those pertaining to the original establishment of the fires (*āgnyādheyika*).
One should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni.
Before the sun has risen, he should give the sacrificial fee for the establishment of the fires (*agnyādheya*).
Then follows the offering to Agni on five potsherds.
Before the sun has risen, he should again give the sacrificial fee for the re-establishment of the fires (*punarādheya*).
(20.19:41.11) Then there is the oblation of cooked rice for Indra and Agni, and that for Aditi; then that for Agni and Varuṇa.
(20.19:41.12) "At the end of the twelve-day rite, [one offers] to the bodies."
(20.19:41.13) [The word] *dhāna* [is used] for the case endings (*vibhakti*).
The rule is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should sacrifice after reciting every single verse in its entirety.
Aupamanyava says that one should add dual-syllable case-endings in the verses addressed to Agni.
(20.19:42.1) This is the supplementary oblation of the sacrificial cake.
"One should offer the oblation to the deities," says Baudhāyana;
"including the sviṣṭakṛt offering," says Śālīki.
(20.19:42.3) This is the etymological explanation of the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
"One should recite [the formulas] in their own respective places," says Baudhāyana. "Having recited them in their own respective places, one may then recite them at will thereafter," says Śālīki.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say, "There are these five places for the Sviṣṭakṛt."
(20.19:42.6) One should recite [the formulas] for all of them.
Now, [the procedure] for one whose fire has been removed and whose kindling woods have been lost is as follows.
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "If the fires have been lost or carried away, one need not concern oneself with the re-establishment of the fires (*āgnyādheya*);
from the moment of their original installation (*ādhāna*), the fires reside in the sacrificer himself."
His out-breath is the Gārhapatya fire, his in-breath the Anvāhāryapacana fire, and his diffused breath the Āhavanīya fire;
one may, if he so desires, descend [the fires] and offer oblations.
(20.19:42.12) Regarding the spreading out of the fires: thus it is said.
(20.19:42.12) Regarding this, the rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki, however, maintains that these fires should remain perpetually maintained from the very time of their installation.
(20.19:42.14) Regarding the setting down of the vessels: thus it is said.
Śālīki says that one should place the vessels upon the *sūtra*.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should set down the vessels either on a grass mat or on blades of grass; for wood is joined to wood by means of the *apasavya* [leftward] motion.
"The oblation is for two," so it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say: "If the first [verse] should lead to an error, one should perform the expiation with the second;
but if the second should lead to an error, both would have caused the error, and one should perform the expiation with another [verse].

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Whichever one, whichever it may be, should lead to an error, both would have caused the error; therefore, one should perform the expiation with yet another [verse]."
(20.20:43.6) "Blazing forth," it is said.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should kindle it with a coal from the Gārhapatya fire and then carry the fire around it three times.
"Making a path, he carries it out toward the north," so it is said.
Śālīki says that one should recite the *sūktavāka*.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In that very place, as if establishing it three times, one should take it away [from the fire], [reciting]:
'These are the three worlds.'"
"He finds firm support in these very worlds," so it is said.
(20.20:43.11) Regarding the "lifting up" (unnayana).
Regarding the rule "either full vessels or verses following [the offering]," the former alternative is that of Baudhāyana, while the latter is that of Śālīki.
(20.20:44.1) "Examination."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should touch both [the butter] that is in the pot and that which has gone into the offering-spoon;
Śālīki says it should be only that which has gone into the offering-spoon.
(20.20:44.3) Then he places it behind the Gārhapatya fire.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says [one should recite] "having passed over" at the front.
(20.20:44.5) "The invocation," so it is said.
"One should offer the oblation after having understood it for oneself," says Baudhāyana.
"If he has a son or a pupil who is capable of performing the ritual, that person, sitting to the south, should offer it," says Śālīki.
The oblation of the two offerings.
"One should offer [the oblations] at the front and the back," says Baudhāyana;
"at the two sides," says Śālīki.
"Baudhāyana says that one should wipe upwards twice and wipe downwards twice;
Śālīki says that one should wipe upwards once and wipe downwards twice."
Having tasted it twice with his finger, having turned toward the north, he consumes [the remainder] with the ladle whose handle points eastward.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should consume [the soma] with the stalk pointing northward.

Having washed the ladle, heated it, and filled it with water, he pours it out toward the north behind the Gārhapatya fire, saying: "Here I offer immortality into Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! Or he says: "An imperishable offering into the imperishable."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The worship with the Āgnipāvamānī verses."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having performed the ritual attendance upon the Āhavanīya fire as it has been established for a year, one should then attend upon the Gārhapatya fire with the verses addressed to Agni-Pavamāna, then with the Gāyatrīs, then with the Dvipadās; then, on the following day, one should proceed according to the regular order."

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Whatever [rites] come before and after the *agnipāvamānī* verses, having performed the worship of the Āhavanīya fire according to its presence during that time for a year, one should thereafter worship the Gārhapatya fire with the *agnipāvamānī* verses, then with the *gāyatrī* verses, then with the *dvipadā* verses; then, on the following day, one should proceed according to the regular order.
Aupamanyava says: "It should be thus; and from that point onward, the *agnipāvamānī* verses should not reach either the Āhavanīya or the Gārhapatya.
From that point onward, they should serve solely the purpose of private Vedic study (*svādhyāya*)."
Having performed the worship with the *vyāhṛtis*, one should say: "May I be able to support you; may my faith not depart," so says Āñjīgavi.
"In the case of blessings," so it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first make a prayer for oneself, then for those already born, and then for the progeny.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should first make a prayer for those already born, then for oneself, and then for the progeny.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should make a prayer for oneself and for the progeny while [the children] are still unborn."
Aupamanyavīputra says that one may indeed wish for [the fulfillment of desires] both in the evening and in the morning.
Regarding the performance of the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.

Baudhāyana used to say: from the very beginning one should wear the sacred thread over the right shoulder (prācīnāvīta); he should remain wearing it in that manner until the offering of the oblations;
when about to offer the oblations, he should put on the sacred thread over the left shoulder (yajñopavīta).
He should remain with the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder until the spreading of the *sakṛdācchinna* grass.

When he is about to spread the *sakṛdācchinna*, he should place the cord over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). He should remain with the cord over the right shoulder until the *prājāpatyā* offering.
"One should worship the Gārhapatya fire while wearing the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder with the verse addressed to Prajāpati.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "From the very beginning, one should wear the cord over the right shoulder;
he should remain thus, with the cord over the right shoulder, until the verse addressed to Prajāpati."
Wearing the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder, he should go northward while reciting the verse addressed to Prajāpati.
Baudhāyana says that one should silently winnow them once, sprinkle them once, and perform the form of the *haviskṛt* call once.

Śālīki says that having made them well-purified by winnowing just once, having poured them into a pot provided with a strainer, and having cooked the *sthālīpāka*, one should pour clarified butter over it and remove it from the fire toward the north.
The offering of oblations.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should not offer the middle oblation here;
Śālīki says that the stirring-spoon itself should be the third [offering].
Regarding the spreading of the *sakṛdācchinna* grass.
Having gone out from the fire-hall, one should spread a single-cut blade of grass in the intermediate space between the south and the east, and place a burning coal to the south—so says Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should do this within [the hall] toward that same direction, and one should not place a burning coal there.
Regarding the giving of the funeral cakes (*piṇḍa*).
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer the rice-balls from beyond [the boundary] toward this side, moving backward."
(20.21:47.11) "The application of collyrium and ointment is the concealment of the mind."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the throwing of the rice-balls into the fire: [the rule is as follows].
Śālīki [prescribes] the *sūtra* [as follows].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In this very place these rice-balls (*piṇḍas*) should remain; for they have become remnants, having been made into food by the ancestors."
"The eating of what remains."
(20.21:47.16) "The sacrificer himself should consume [the portion]," says Baudhāyana;
(20.21:47.17) "He should give it to his son or to a resident pupil," says Śālīki; (20.21:48.1) he should have the wife consume it.
"This [earth] becomes her offspring," says Aupamanyava.
"Having smelled as much as can be taken up by a finger, one should then throw the remainder into the fire," says Aupamanyavīputra.
"Having moved it to a heap of ashes, one should completely cover it," says Āñjīgavi.
"One should cast [the remains] into water," says Maudgalya.
(20.22:48.5) "The ritual procedure for the Āgrayaṇa is a contraction."
There is no combination of ritual procedures for two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Having offered the oblation to Soma, one should then offer the other oblations;
in this way, his oblations have the *caru* as their opening."
Regarding this, Aupamanyavīputra used to say that the Soma-oblation should be an *āvāpika* (an insertion) because it is an interruption;
one should offer it between the Vaiśvadeva and the cake on one potsherd (*ekakapāla*). Regarding this, Añjīgavi used to say that there are three such oblations.
"These are the three worlds;
he finds firm support in these very worlds.
Thus, by means of this *śyāmāka* sacrificial grass-bundle (*prastara*), it becomes attained for him.
The oblation of the *ajyāni* verses.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should offer the *ajyāni* oblations before the *sviṣṭakṛt*.
(20.22:48.14) Regarding the cooking of the Āgrayaṇa oblations.
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana;
"in water," says Śālīki.
(20.22:49.1) "The performance of the cake on one potsherd at the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice."
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
(20.22:49.3) "Regarding the composition of the treatise."

Baudhāyana used to say: "There should be fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses; one should perform the two *ājyabhāga* offerings with the *vārtraghna* formulas and the deities loudly, as well as the *yājamāna* portion.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "There should be seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should have the *vṛdhanvant* formulas and the deities should be recited in a low voice (*upāṃśu*)."
One should perform the duties of the sacrificer.
Regarding "putting on [the garment] in reverse order": [this refers to the following].
Baudhāyana used to say that one should depart after enclosing oneself with the Āhavanīya fire alone; having gone abroad and returned again, one should worship the Āhavanīya with all the formulas.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should depart after enclosing oneself with the fires as they happen to be available.
Having gone abroad and returned again, one should perform the ritual worship for each [deity] with all the mantras.
"For one who has gone forth without having performed the formal attendance."

Baudhāyana says that one should worship him with the regular formula at whatever place one remembers [him] while he is absent; Śālīki says that if one does not remember, then upon returning from the journey, one should worship with the regular formula alone.
Regarding the offering made while away from home: "In the *pravasatha* offering..."
Baudhāyana used to say: "If an expiation has already been performed, one need not pay attention to offering there;
but if it has not been performed, one should offer this [oblation] there.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "In the case of those lapses for which specific substitute expiations have been prescribed, those very expiations should be performed there."
"Now, as for those lapses for which no expiation has been prescribed, one should simply not pay heed to them.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Whether an expiation has been performed or whether it has not been performed, one should nevertheless offer the *pravasathāhuti* in that case."
"In the sequences of the Virāj," so it is said.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
(20.23:50.10) "The sipping of water."
Baudhāyana says that one should sip water twice with the mantra and once silently;
Śālīki says that one should sip water once with the mantra and twice silently.
(20.23:50.13) "Making manifest" means:

Baudhāyana used to say that one should make all these deities witnesses [with the formula]: "O Agni, lord of vows, I shall perform the vow. Śālīki says that since Agni is indeed the lord of vows among the gods, one should not disregard this very point.
"If the potsherd is lost or broken."
This is the rule of the two teachers.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: having offered these two spoonfuls with the formulas, "May the mind, the light, enjoy [the oblation]" and "The thirty-three threads," one should then pour in another [substance] with the formula, "May the cauldron go to the gods.
This is the mantra: "I pour you together with the Yajus."
He should sprinkle milk, clarified butter, or water with this very same mantra.
Regarding the taking of the *ājya* ladlings.
Baudhāyana used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas, those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* and those belonging to the sacrificer (*yājamāna*);
the sacrificer should then recite the consecratory formulas (*anumantraṇa*) with the *yājamāna* formulas.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas, those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* and those belonging to the sacrificer.
"One should not have the sacrificer recite the formulas belonging to the sacrificer," [so says the rule].
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Just as the formulas pertaining to the cake-offering do not recur, even so the formulas belonging to the sacrificer should not recur."
Regarding the laying down of the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*).
Baudhāyana used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should perform the concluding rite with both sets of formulas— those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* section and those belonging to the sacrificer—
and that the sacrificer should follow along with the formulas belonging to the sacrificer. Regarding this,

Śālīki used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should perform the concluding rite with both sets of formulas— those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* section and those belonging to the sacrificer— but the sacrificer should not follow along with the formulas belonging to the sacrificer.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Just as the formulas belonging to the cake-offering do not recur, even so the formulas belonging to the sacrificer should not recur."
(20.23:51.20) He mutters [the formula] while the two fuel-sticks are being placed upon the fire.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki holds that this entire mantra should be used for the yoking of the fire.
Then, one should set down the Agnihotra with these *vyāhṛtis*: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar."
"Year by year," says Śālīki; this is the rule.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "On whichever night one first sets it down, when that year has elapsed, having set it down on that same night, one need not pay further heed to it thereafter.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Indeed, for him the year becomes fully completed [only] when it has recurred."
On whichever night one should first set down [the fires], when a year has elapsed, on the night preceding that one, having set them down, he need not pay further heed to them thereafter.
One performing the New and Full Moon sacrifices should set out the oblations with these *vyāhṛti*s.
"Year by year," thus says Śālīki regarding the rule.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "On whichever full moon day one first sets [the fires], when that year has elapsed, having set them on that same day, one need not concern oneself with them thereafter.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Indeed, for him, that very year becomes repeated."

"On whichever full moon day one should first set [the vessels] down, when the year has elapsed, on whichever full moon day occurs prior to that, having set them down on that day, one need not pay further heed beyond it."
One performing the Cāturmāsya sacrifices should set out the oblations with these *vyāhṛti*s.
(20.24:52.17) "In this very manner, year after year," is the rule of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "On whichever full moon day one should set out the Vaiśvadeva oblations, when that year has elapsed, having set out the Vaiśvadeva oblations on that [subsequent] day, he need not concern himself with anything beyond that.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Indeed, for him, that very year becomes repeated."

"On whichever full moon day one should set out the Vaiśvadeva oblations, when the year has elapsed, on the next preceding full moon day one should set out the Śunāsīrīya oblations; from that point onward, one need not pay further heed [to the regular sequence]."
"The Dhāna [is the name] of the *vyāhṛtis*."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
He mutters [the formula] while the portion for the *prāśitra* is being cut off.

This is the Sūtra of Maitreya. Now, when the *prāśitra* portion is being cut for the two teachers, he mutters: "May Agni protect me from ill-sacrificed rites; may Savitṛ protect me from the malevolent."
In the portion belonging to the sacrificer, [he recites]: "May I conquer by this [rite] whoever acts as an enemy to me, whether he be near or far."
Aupamanyava maintains that this entire mantra for the consecration of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering should be used as a single formula.
(20.24:53.14) [The ritual manual] says: "He causes the sacrificer to recite from the Veda."
Śālīki holds that the *veda* [grass-bundle] is used [at this point].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One makes the sacrificer recite over the *veda*: 'Thou art the *veda*; thou art acquisition; may I acquire.'"
Whatever one might covet from an enemy, one should utter its name;
thus one seizes all of that from him.
Now, if the sacrificer has either drunk *surā* liquor or is away on a journey.

Baudhāyana used to say: "For one who is away on a journey, one should throw the sacrificer’s portion into the fire along with the *prastara* bundle itself; having spread [ghee] around the *dhruvā* ladle with clarified butter and having placed [the portion] into the *juhū*, one should offer it.
Thus the sacrificer’s portion attains the status of the *prastara*.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "From the very beginning, he should not even come into contact with a drinker of *surā*."
"But if he should associate with them, one should indeed have him recite the mantras; why then should he not consume the portions?
Thus said Aupamanyava: "And he should certainly consume the portions."
"The worship of the Sun."
(20.24:54.10) Baudhāyana says that, having gone out from the fire-hall, one should worship the sun;
Śālīki says that one should do so while remaining right there.
On the full moon day, there is the making of the fire-brick scraper.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
(20.24:54.14) "The release from the vow."
"One should sip water with a mantra and release the vow with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"one should sip water silently and release the vow with a mantra," says Śālīki;
"having performed the rite with the *upaveṣa* stick, one should release the vow," says Aupamanyava.
He mutters the formula for the re-seizing of the sacrifice.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should worship the Āhavanīya fire alone with this Yajus formula.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the animal sacrifice.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "The *iṣṭi* and the animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*) are accompanied by the *upavasatha* day.
Śālīki, however, says: "They may be accompanied by the *upavasatha*, or they may be performed on the same day (*sadyoyajña*)."
(20.25:55.6) "Regarding the performance of the sacrifice."

Baudhāyana says that one should sacrifice with the cake on eight potsherds dedicated to Agni for both the animal and the victim. Śālīki says that this is seen to apply specifically to a brown-eared female goat and a barren ewe.
"The wooden sword becomes the sacrificial post."
Baudhāyana says that this sacrificial post (yūpa) is of the same form as a wooden sword (sphyaprakāra), provided it has a top-ring (caṣālavān).
Śālīki says that this post belonging to the fire-hall (agnyagārika) should be without a wooden sword and without a top-ring.
"The sacrificial post is forked," so it is said.
Baudhāyana says that above the time for the cord, there should be two four-cornered shafts with four-cornered tops, while the other sacrificial post should be eight-sided.
Śālīki says that this [first post] should have a shaft but no top-ring, while the other sacrificial post should be eight-sided.
Regarding the preparation of roasted barley flour: [the rule is as follows].
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should perform the rite even with rice grains.
(20.25:56.5) This is the oblation of the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should offer the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula on the very day of the Upavasatha.
"At the offering for the sacrificial post, [there is] the invocation."
Śālīki holds that the *sūtra* [is authoritative].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should take the clarified butter and the two fire-drills, churn the fire near the sacrificial post, and offer the *yūpāhuti* oblation.
(20.25:56.10) "The offering over the wood-cutter's block."
Śālīki says that one should [use] the *sūtra*.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In this very manner, having placed gold within the *juhū* ladle, one should offer [the oblation] with the formula: ‘O Lord of the Forest, grow forth with a hundred shoots, svāhā!
Then, one should touch oneself with the formula: ‘May we grow forth with a thousand shoots!’, and thereafter touch water."
Regarding the invocation of the sacrificial post (*yūpa*).
Baudhāyana says that one should cause [the guest] to enter who has fallen [prostrate] facing either east or north.
Śālīki says that one should cause him to enter regardless of which direction he has gone, provided he is not impaired.
(20.25:56.17) "Regarding the preparation of the altar."
The Sūtra belongs to Aupamanyavīputra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "It should be measured by a chariot; it should be as long as a chariot-axle across at the back, as wide as a chariot-pole toward the east, as wide as a chariot-yoke in front, and its northern nave should be as wide as the upper yoke.
Śālīki says: "Or it may be marked by the eye-measure, or it should be ten paces on all sides, for the Virāj is perfected by ten."
Regarding the tracing around of the *cātvāla* pit.
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "While tracing the outline in this very manner, one should draw [the lines] on the outside, both from the east and from the north."
(20.26:57.7) "The carrying away of the world-fires."
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having seated the Āgnīdhra on the Uttaravedi, one should then carry forth the Lokāgnis.
Aupamanyava says: "One should carry forth the Lokāgnis from their very locations."
Regarding the measurement of the *uttaravedi*.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should measure [the altar] with the yoke-pin of a draft-ox on a track equal to a chariot;
there is no middle altar here."
The tracing around the sacrificial post-hole has been explained.
Regarding the decoration of the high altar (*uttaravedi*).
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should complete the northern navel on the very day before.
(20.26:58.3) Striking with the wooden sword, the Āgnīdhra follows the footprints of the Hotṛ.
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having gathered the dust from step to step, one should scatter it to the north of the northern *nābhi*."
Regarding the sprinkling of the high altar (*uttaravedī*).
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should sprinkle it with the formulas according to their direction and according to the order of the formulas.
"The pouring out of what remains."
"One should pour [the water] on the southern shoulder of the altar," says Baudhāyana.
"On the high altar (uttaravedi)," says Śālīki.
"One should pour it specifically on the southern shoulder of the altar that has been measured out by a chariot," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the sprinkling of the high altar.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: “One should pour out this [libation] over the opposing sides,” says Śālīki.
Aupamanyava says: “Pouring it out diagonally, having offered in the middle, one should then offer toward the northern shoulder.”
"At the placing of the fuel."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should place the fuel silently.
(20.26:58.16) "The offering of the oblations of the *adhvara* sacrifice."
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should offer four portions taken in four ladlings; Śālīki says that one should offer four [portions].
The wiping and placing of the vessel for taking the speckled butter.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should obtain the wiping and the placing of the *aupabhṛta* ladle. Aupamanyava says that one should not wipe it.
Regarding the taking of the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya).

The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should take [the portion] with the formula ending at the heart; Śālīki says one should do so with the formula ending at the heart. Aupamanyava says that having mixed the clarified butter and the curds, one should take [the portion] with these five formulas.

Regarding this, Aupamanyavīputra used to say: "Having silently spread [a base of butter] twice, having brought the curds while reciting all the formulas, one should silently pour [butter] over it twice."
Regarding the performance of the expiation for the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*).

Baudhāyana says that if [the vessel] is taken up or moved forward before its time, one should perform the expiation for this very act right here. Śālīki says that if it is moved forward before it is set down, one should perform it right here.
Aupamanyava says, however, that it is not [an offense] merely by being sprinkled.
(20.26:59.10) Regarding the washing of the sacrificial post: |||
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki, however, says that one should wash the sacrificial post silently.
(20.26:59.12) Regarding the sprinkling of the sacrificial post: |||

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having placed together the sacrificial post-top-ring, the cord for the Maitrāvaruṇa, the chip from the sacrificial post, gold, and a vessel of water, one should sprinkle the sacrificial post.
Śālīki says: "In this manner, one should sprinkle the items connected with the sacrificial post using the post, and the items connected with the animal using the animal."
Regarding the circumambulation of the sacrificial post.
Baudhāyana says [it should be] to the south; Śālīki says [it should be] to the north.
"The anointing of the sacrificial post."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says it should be only the post standing nearest the fire.
Regarding the pouring of water from a vessel.
"One should pour it out while moving clockwise," says Baudhāyana;
"as may be convenient," says Śālīki.
Regarding the encircling of the sacrificial post.

Baudhāyana says that one should recite the mantra three times and repeat the ritual action three times; Śālīki says that one should recite the mantra only once and perform the ritual action only once.
"He girds [the post] at the height of the navel."
The rule of Baudhāyana is that [the fire] is from the Madhyadeśa; Śālīki says it is from the Madhyadeśa.
"The concealment of the *svaru*."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says [the fire] faces toward the Agniṣṭhā post.
(20.27:60.14) Regarding the ritual preparation of the animal victim.
The Sūtra belongs to Aupamanyavīputra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should perform the *upākaraṇa* in this very manner, but one should not cause [the animal] to be gratified.
Śālīki says: "One should both cause it to be gratified and offer the oblation at the time of the *upākaraṇa*."
