Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "In this very manner, one should strike it from the front while it is turned toward the west with two blades of sacrificial grass and a branch of the Plakṣa tree; and having placed the heart upon that Plakṣa branch, one should cut the portions."
(20.27:61.1) "The rubbing together of the two kindling woods."
The Sūtra [is] that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: one should take up a wood-shard with the formula, "Thou art the birthplace of Agni"; one should place it upon either a blade of *dūrvā* grass or another wood-shard with the formula, "Ye two are stallions."
Saying, "Thou art Urvaśī," he should take up the lower kindling-stick; saying, "Purūravas," the upper kindling-stick.
Then, having anointed both of them with clarified butter from the butter-pot, he should place them together with the formula: "Anointed with ghee, do ye two produce the bull. Thus it is said.
"The taking up of food by the animal."
"One should take it up with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the naming of the sacrificial animal.
Regarding the thread, Baudhāyana says it should be placed on the neck; Śālīki says it should be placed on the neck itself.
Regarding the tethering of the sacrificial animal.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should tie the animal to the sacrificial post itself; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the sprinkling of the sacrificial animal: [the rule is as follows].
"One should sprinkle with water consecrated silently," says Baudhāyana;
"with water from water-pots," says Śālīki.
(20.27:61.14) Regarding the anointing of the sacrificial animal: thus it is said.
Śālīki says that the sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having placed the ladle against the forehead, one should draw it across without breaking the line as far as the southern hip."
Regarding the production of the girdle for the sacrificial post.
Baudhāyana says that one should produce the sacrificial post (*yūpa*), the *svaru* chip, and the *raśanā* rope;
Śālīki says it is the animal (*paśu*);
Aupamanyava says it is the ritual procedure (*tantra*).
"It is the deity," says Aupamanyavīputra.
(20.28:62.4) Regarding the *atyāśrāvaṇa* (the call for assent): |||
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should cause the *atyāśrāvaṇa* call to be made only for the Soma sacrifice.
(20.28:62.6) The anointing of the sacrificial animal.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should not cut from that [portion] with which one has anointed; nor indeed should one cut from the cooked [oblation] with this [same means].
Śālīki says: "As the occasion arises."
Regarding the carrying of fire around the sacrificial animal.
Baudhāyana says that one should carry fire around the *śāmitra* fire together [with the other fires].
Śālīki says [it should be done] with whatever is other than the *śāmitra*. Rāthītara says [it should be done] with both the animal and the clarified butters.
"A cow indeed," says Aupamanyava.
The oblation of the *apāvya* formulas.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should offer one oblation in the first round, two in the middle, and two in the last; Śālīki says it should be according to what is available.
(20.28:62.15) [Regarding] the *upapraiṣa* and the *āśrāvaṇa*.
The rule is according to Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not cause the announcement to be made.
Regarding the slaughter of the animal.
(20.28:62.17) Baudhāyana says [the corpse should be placed] with its head toward the west and its feet toward the north;

(20.28:63.1) Śālīki says [it should be placed] with its head toward the north and its feet toward the west; (20.28:63.2) Aupamanyava says [it should be placed] with its head toward the east and its feet toward the north.
"The animal is the casting out of hunger."
"One should throw the rope into the *cātvāla* pit," says Baudhāyana;
"having sprinkled it with water in a place where there is no passage," says Śālīki.
(20.28:63.5) Regarding the leading forward of the wife.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should lead her forward with the words, 'Go, unassailable! and then, having made her look up at the sun, one should lead her forward with those very same words, 'Go, unassailable!'"
Regarding the gazing at the waters.
Baudhāyana says that one should cause [the sacrificer] to look down from above the *catvāla*;
Śālīki says that one should do so from the side of the animal.
(20.28:63.10) Regarding the smearing of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
Śālīki says that this is the rule of the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In this case, the other [portion] should be smeared exactly as described;
having smeared it on the other side, one should discard it with the formula: 'Thou art the portion of the Rakṣases.'"
(20.28:63.12) "Then he should touch water," so it is said.
Regarding the offering of the omentum.
"The ladles may be made of clarified butter or of gold on the second and fourth [pressings]," says Baudhāyana; the former alternative is Baudhāyana's, the latter is Śālīki's.
(20.29:63.15) Regarding the offering of the sacrificial cake for the animal sacrifice: //
The rule is that of Baudhāyana: "Having immolated the animal, one should offer the sacrificial cake," says Śālīki.
Regarding the removal of the sacrificial animal.
Baudhāyana says that one should cause the heart and the tongue to fall out;
Śālīki says that one should cause only the heart to fall out.
"The cooking of the heart."
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should cook it on a spit;
right there one should complete the ritual for the heart-spit."
And one should touch [the water] from above with the mantra.
Regarding the portioning of the *iḍā* from the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) of the animal sacrifice (*paśu*).
Śālīki holds that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having first made the portions for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering, one should then cut off the *iḍā* portion from it;
such is the rule for the *savanīya* offerings."
(20.29:64.7) "Regarding the performance of the *iḍā-sūna*."
Regarding the sūtra of Baudhāyana,
Śālīki says that one should place the heart upon a Plakṣa branch on the sacrificial grass itself and then cut the portions.
Regarding the dialogue concerning the sacrificial animal.

Śālīki says that one should recite the *sūtra* [as prescribed]. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having asked the first question, one should step forward with the words, 'May Pūṣan, the protector of cattle, protect me';
having asked the second, one should step forward with the words, 'May Pūṣan protect me on the path.'"
Having asked for the third time, he should step forward, saying: "May Pūṣan, my overlord, protect me."
Regarding the sprinkling of the animal victim with clarified butter.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should sprinkle the heart with speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) and the other organs with clarified butter (ājya).
Regarding the placing of the victim animal.
"One should set down the five *hotṛ*s," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the cutting of portions from the sacrificial animal.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should take portions from the heart, the tongue, and the chest in this very sequence; and in this case, those who follow the five-fold cutting should make a third portion.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should take portions from all [the organs] in sequence, and one should not make a third portion for those who follow the five-fold cutting in this case."
Regarding the touching of the sacrificial animal.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should touch both [the portions]— those from which he cuts and those contained in the ladle—
whereas Śālīki says that one should touch only those contained in the ladle.
"He mixes it with the pitcher," so it is said.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
one should mix the fat-offering with the entire side [of the liver], says Śālīki.
Regarding the carrying around of the sacrificial animal.
"One should carry it back around," says Baudhāyana; "one should not carry it back around," says Śālīki.
Regarding "stepping across": [it refers to] stepping over [the fire].
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should cause the announcement to be made after walking around the back of the Uttaravedi.
"Regarding the sacrifice to the quarters."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: one should offer oblations to the common quarters prior to the Vanaspati offering, saying, "To the quarter, svāhā!
Having offered thus, one should stand in worship, saying, "Svāhā to the quarters! Homage to the quarters!"
"Of the tree and of the wandering life."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should perform the rite with four spoonfuls taken from the speckled butter.
"The placing of the rectum."
"One should prepare it as a sixfold portion," says Baudhāyana;
"it should be entirely whole," says Śālīki.
Regarding the *aupayaja* offerings.
Śālīki [holds] the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having drawn out embers from the Āhavanīya fire towards the north, the *upayaṣṭṛ* should perform the *upayaj* offerings upon them."
"With the anus as the third."
"Baudhāyana says that one should perform the *upayaja* offerings after dividing [the heart] into eleven parts. Śālīki says it should be done by cutting off [the portions].
Aupamanyava says that having thrown the whole of it into the fire, one should consecrate it with all the formulas."
(20.30:66.10) Then he wipes his hands on the sacrificial grass.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that they should also bring water for him at this point.
"The oblation is for the *svaru*."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should offer after having placed [the oblation] upon four spoonfuls of ghee.
"The joint sacrifice for the wives."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should perform the Saṃyāja offerings for the wives with clarified butter alone.
He sacrifices to the wives of the gods with the tail-end portion held upward, and to Agni Gṛhapati with it held downward.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should perform all of this with the tail of the animal while it is held with the belly upwards.
From the upward-turned tail-portion, he cuts the *iḍā* for the *hotṛ*; from the downward-turned portion, he cuts the sixfold portion for the *agnīdh*.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s;
Śālīki says that one should perform all of this with the tail-end of the animal held face upwards.
Regarding the performance of the oblation of husks.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"The swelling of the *dhruvā*."
Baudhāyana used to say that both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer should swell the *dhruvā* ladle;
Śālīki, however, says that the Adhvaryu alone, having swollen the *dhruvā*, should offer the *samiṣṭayajus* oblations.
(20.31:67.12) [The section on] the offering of the *samiṣṭayajus* oblations.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should offer three portions taken four times each; Śālīki says that one should offer three [portions].
(20.31:67.14) Regarding the removal of the heart-spit: [the rule is as follows].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should perform [the rite] for both those who are good friends and those who are bad friends;
Śālīki says that one should not perform it.
"The preparation of the fuel-sticks."
Baudhāyana says that all [the sacrificial posts] should be made moist and provided with leaves; Śālīki says that this applies only to the post of the sacrificer and that of his wife.
Regarding the burning of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
"One should burn it around the southern shoulder of the altar," says Baudhāyana;
"around the high altar (uttaravedi)," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the oblation of parched grain flour.
"One should perform three offerings of groats," says Baudhāyana;
"only one," says Śālīki;
"one should proceed with the offering of groats at the forest fire itself," says Aupamanyava.
The worship of the deities has been explained.
Regarding the worship of the sacrificial post (*yūpa*).
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should worship the Āhavanīya fire alone with this Yajus formula.
"Bring them together," he said.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should not heed [the other], says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"The giving of the sacrificial fee."
"One should give either a milch cow or a bull," says Baudhāyana; "or something else that is of singular value," says Śālīki; "or something else that is of singular value," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.

Baudhāyana used to say that the Cāturmāsya sacrifices should be performed throughout one's life, with the sexual union occurring within [the intervals], but that one should observe the vow only during the very first year.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, indeed, are to be observed for a full year and must include the practice of celibacy (*brahmacarya*).
"According to the specific application," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the milks, there is the question of whether they are accompanied by mantras or without mantras.
Baudhāyana says that both the evening and morning milkings should be accompanied by mantras, while Śālīki says they should be silent.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava said: "The milk-offerings for the Cāturmāsya sacrifices prior to the Soma sacrifice should be silent, but after the Soma sacrifice, they should receive the mantras."

Regarding this, Añjīgavi used to say: "These five milks alone are accompanied by mantras: that in the New and Full Moon sacrifices, in the curd offering to Mitra and Varuṇa, in the Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice, in the Kauṇḍapāyina sacrifice, and in the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice."
Regarding the performance of the Vaiśvānara and Pārjanya [offerings].
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
On the full moon day of Phālguna or Caitra, the calves are separated from their mothers for the sake of the Viśvedevas.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says it should be during the northern course of the sun, on an auspicious day of the waxing fortnight.
"The sacrificial grass-bundle consists of shoots."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: Śālīki says that all this sacrificial grass (*barhis*) should consist entirely of *prasūma* grass.
The oblation of the Pañcahotṛ.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"One should offer the Pañcahotṛ oblation on the very day of the Upavasatha," so says Śālīki.
Regarding the consecratory formulas for the *prayāja* offerings: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana says that having consecrated four [cups] with four [formulas], one should follow the others with the fifth.
Śālīki says that having consecrated four [cups] with four [formulas], one should consecrate them all at the end with the fifth.
Regarding the cakes on one potsherd, there is the question of whether they are accompanied by mantras or are mantra-less.
Baudhāyana says that they should be accompanied by mantras; Śālīki says they should be silent.
Regarding the cutting of portions from cakes offered on a single potsherd.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should not cut portions from the Cāturmāsya offerings alone; rather, one should cut portions from the others. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should cut portions only from those that carry the ritual sequence (*tantra*); one should not cut portions from the others."
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should not cut a portion from the *puruṣī* of the Vaiśvadeva; rather, one should cut portions from the others."
The supplementary offering (*abhihoma*) for the cakes baked on a single potsherd (*ekakapāla*).
Baudhāyana says that one should make an offering with whatever residue remains in the *sruva* ladle.
Śālīki says that one should offer each [oblation] with four names of the seasons at a time.
Regarding the single-pot offerings, it is the "collecting of the remains" (*anusaṃharaṇa*).
"One should join [the verses] together," says Baudhāyana; "one should not join them together," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the *vājina* offering.
"One should perform it in a whisper," says Baudhāyana;
"aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the *vājina* [mixture].
Śālīki holds that [the rule] is according to the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "The others should consume [the portion] merely by smelling it;
only the sacrificer should consume it directly."

(21.2:71.11) Baudhāyana says that after shaving with the *nivartana* formula, one should have both the hair and the beard shaved. (21.2:71.12) Śālīki says that after shaving with the *nivartana* formula, one should shave only the beard, not the hair.
(21.2:71.13) Aupamanyava says that after shaving with the *nivartana* formula, one should neither shave the beard nor the hair.
(21.2:71.15) Regarding the preparation of the vessels for the southern sacrificial fire-pit during the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.
(21.2:71.16) According to Baudhāyana, the [spoons] should be made of wood; according to Śālīki, they may be either golden or silver;
according to Aupamanyava, they should be made of *śamī* wood.
(21.2:72.1) Regarding the removal of the *stambayajus* grass-bundle.
Baudhāyana says that they should exchange the *stambayajus* formulas; Śālīki says they should do so together.
"The gazing at the clarified butter."
Baudhāyana says that one should sit to the south of the offering for the New and Full Moon sacrifices, look at the southern [altar], and then look at the northern one.
Śālīki says that one should sit at the junction of the altars, look at the southern one, and then look at the northern one.
Aupamanyava says [one should do so] from the middle.
"The winnowing basket is made of reeds."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says it should be made of *darbha* grass or *kuśa* grass. Aupamanyava says it should be actual [grass].
Regarding the throwing-in of the winnowing basket:
Baudhāyana says that one should throw it in;
Śālīki says that one should not throw it in.
"Aupamanyava says that one should sprinkle [the food] with water and then eat it."
"The cutting of portions from the two curd-mixtures."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having taken portions from the two curds (*āmikṣā*), one should place the ewe; one should not take portions of the *śāmī* leaves and *karīra* flour, for these are said to be fodder.
Aupamanyava says: "One should combine the entire *viśvalopa* with the final portion."
Regarding the performance for Mārutī.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should perform the offering to the Maruts on the northern fire alone.
(21.3:73.1) Regarding the throwing of the stirring-stick into the fire at the offering to the Maruts.
"One should throw it into the fire," says Baudhāyana; "one should not throw it into the fire," says Śālīki.
"The purificatory bath," he says.
The Sūtra [states] that of the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should go to the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) with both the chaff and the scrapings."
The throwing back of the water's edge has been explained.
The ritual bath has been explained.
The preparation of the fuel-sticks has been explained.
(21.3:73.8) Regarding the offering of the Ānīkavata oblation: |||
"One should wait for the rising of the sun by touching [the hand]," so say the two teachers;
"only when about to take the fist," says Aupamanyava;
"one should proceed together with the rays," says Aupamanyavīputra.
This very same is the rule for the Sāṃtapana sacrifice; this is also the rule for the Kraiḍina sacrifice.
Regarding the Gṛhamedhīya sacrifice, there is the question of whether it is with mantras or without mantras.
Baudhāyana says that one should be accompanied by the mantra; Śālīki says it should be done silently.
Regarding the pouring out of the Gṛhamedhīya offering.
Baudhāyana says that [the water] should be poured with a vessel provided with a strainer while accompanied by a mantra; Śālīki says it should be done silently with a vessel without a strainer.
Regarding the cooking of the Gṛhamedhīya offering.
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana;
"in water," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the *śākalas*, it is said: "In the case of the *śākalas*, [the rule] applies."
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the setting down of the Gṛhamedhīya oblation.
Baudhāyana says that one should place the offering on the sacrificial grass itself;
Śālīki says it should be placed on those other kuśa blades that have not yet been used.
Regarding the performance of the Gṛhamedhīya rite.
"One should perform it in a whisper," says Baudhāyana;
"aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the throwing-in of the *śākala* pieces according to the Śākalas.
"One should throw [the fire] into it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not throw it into it," says Śālīki.
"The cooking of the neighbor," so it is said.
"One should cook it on the Anvāhāryapacana fire," says Baudhāyana;
"at the head of the village," says Śālīki.
The oblation of one who has filled the ladle is called the *pūrṇadarvya-homa*.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Gautama says that one should offer the oblations at the *hiṃkāra* of the Brahman priest after having uttered the *vyāhṛtis*.
"The two blades of sacrificial grass for the Mahāpitṛyajña," so [it is said].
(21.4:74.16) "This sacrificial grass (*barhis*) is [to be] with its roots," says Baudhāyana;
in that case, there is no touching back [of the grass]. "It is [to be] with a remainder," says Śālīki.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava says that since the touching back [of the grass] has been established there, one should cut it so as to be completely uprooted.
Then this half-vessel of milk is for the cow that has been milked by her own calf.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Now, Śālīki says that if there should be less [soma], one should replenish it with water.
Among those [offerings], he causes the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*) to be uttered over the rice alone; they lift up the barley.
Śālīki holds that the sūtra [is correct].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "From the pouring [of the grain] onwards, the ritual action involving mantras should be repeated for the barley; however, the call to the *haviṣkṛt* should be performed as a single *tantra*."
Regarding the pouring out of the water for the consecration.
(21.4:75.9) "One should pour out [the water] for the Āpyas behind the Gārhapatya," says Baudhāyana.
(21.4:75.10) "In front, having passed beyond," says Śālīki. (21.4:75.10) "Either in front or behind," says Aupamanyava.
(21.4:75.12) "Regarding the preparation of the altar."
(21.4:75.12) Having gone out from the fire-hall, one should construct it in the southeastern intermediate direction, says Baudhāyana. (21.4:75.13) "Right within this same direction," says Śālīki.
(21.4:75.14) "Precisely around the Anvāhāryapacana fire," says Aupamanyava.
(21.4:75.15) Regarding the kindling of the Anvāhāryapacana fire: thus it is said.
Baudhāyana says that they should kindle [the fires] in their own places;
Śālīki says that they should simply carry forward the fuel-bundle (*idhma*).
(21.4:76.1) Regarding the taking of the portions of clarified butter: //
Baudhāyana says that there may be either five portions or six portions; Śālīki says that there must be exactly six portions.
(21.4:76.3) Regarding the sacrificial grass-bundle (*prastara*): with mantra or without mantra?
The taking up and the placing down of this [fuel] should be performed silently;
however, Baudhāyana says that the other [actions] should be accompanied by mantras.
The gathering and the placing down of this [fuel] should be performed silently.
(21.4:76.5) Now, Śālīki says that the other [rites] should be accompanied by mantras.
(21.4:76.6) But [the rite] up to the very placing [of the fire] should be performed silently.
(21.4:76.6) Aupamanyava says that the other [rites] should be accompanied by mantras.
"Three times he goes around strewing [the grass] from right to left."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should strew [the grass] exactly as it has grown.
Regarding the strewing of the altar.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should simply say: "I spread thee, O wool-soft one."
Regarding the laying down of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
Śālīki holds that the sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should lay down all the enclosing sticks;
when the rite for the ancestors is being performed, one should place the northern stick to the south.
Regarding the removal of the sacrificial oblations.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should remove the sacrificial oblations exactly as they were cooked, says Śālīki.
The movement of the oblations and the duties of the Adhvaryu priest.
"To the south," says Baudhāyana;
"to the north," says Śālīki.
(21.5:77.1) "These officiating priests move about; they transpose the sacrificial oblations," [it is said].
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that the two oblations should not be exchanged here. Aupamanyava says that the two oblations should not be exchanged here, but the Adhvaryu and the Āgnīdhra should walk around each other.
"The call for the *āśrāvaṇa*," [he says].
"O svadhā," says Baudhāyana;
"ā svadhā," says Śālīki; "svadhā," says Aupamanyava.
"The *pravara*," he says.
The two teachers [hold] that the *sūtra* is [the verse],
while Aupamanyava holds that it is "vidvān cikitvān" (the wise and knowing one).
The offering of the rice balls has been explained.
The procedure for applying collyrium and ointment has been explained.
The ritual throwing-in of the rice-balls has been explained.
(21.5:77.12) Regarding the Traiyambaka offerings, there is the question of whether they are performed with mantras or without mantras.
"They should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana;
"they should be silent," says Śālīki;
"one may even bake them on a single potsherd," says Aupamanyava.
(21.5:77.15) "The carrying of a single firebrand."
"One should carry [the fire] from the *anvāhāryapacana* fire," says Baudhāyana;
"from the village fire," says Śālīki.
Having taken this [fire], they stand in attendance upon the *gārhapatya* fire.
Baudhāyana used to say that this mantra belongs to both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer;
Śālīki, however, says it belongs to the sacrificer alone.
(21.5:78.1) Regarding the extraction of the Traiyambaka offerings: thus [it is said].
Śālīki says that one should follow the sūtra [as given].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having gone around three times without interlinking, one should dig up [the earth] three times, saying: 'For Bhaga you! For Bhaga you!'"
(21.6:78.4) Then he pours them into the joined palms of the sacrificer.
Śālīki holds that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should pour [the grain] for the sacrificer alone with the mantra, and silently for the wife, if she desires fortune."
(21.6:78.7) Then, having placed them in a bag and tied them with two threads—one blue and one red—he fastens them to a dry stump or to a forked branch.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana;
the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the pouring of water from a vessel: it means pouring [water] from a water-pot.
"One should pour it out while moving clockwise," says Baudhāyana;
"as may be convenient," says Śālīki.
Regarding the sacrifice at the joint of the Śunāsīrīya [season]: thus it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In whichever fortnight of the waxing moon follows from this point onward one may arrive, on that one should perform the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice;
for this is seen as being for the purpose of worship even for the thirteenth month."
(21.6:79.3) "Regarding the preparation of the altar."
"It should be according to the New and Full Moon sacrifices," says Baudhāyana; "it should be according to the Animal Sacrifice," says Śālīki.
Regarding the giving of the sacrificial fees.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should give gold to the Vaiśvānara [offering], a milch-cow to the Pārjanya; twelve to the Vaiśvadeva, twelve for the Varuṇapraghāsa oblations, three to the Ānīkavat, three to the Sāṃtapana, four to the Gṛhamedhīya, a bull to the Pūrṇadarvya, three to the Kraiḍina, twelve to the Mahāhavis oblations, three to the Āditya, and twelve to the Śunāsīrīya oblations.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Sixty-four sacrificial fees for the Cāturmāsya sacrifices are traditionally prescribed."
If he should not obtain them, he should give as many garments, or as many stirred drinks, or as many portions of cooked rice;
by that means, indeed, he attains this desire.
"At the end of the Cāturmāsya sacrifices."
Baudhāyana says that they should end with the Soma offerings;
Śālīki says they should end with the animal sacrifices; Aupamanyava says one should sacrifice with the Savaneṣṭi.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Agniṣṭoma.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should not initiate the officiating priests without having first seen the King [Soma].
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If the initiations are long, those who perform the *āśvāsika* [breathing exercises] should do so, and likewise the *udgātṛ*; one may initiate them at will."
(21.7:80.5) Regarding the settling upon the hall.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should occupy the sacrificial hall at midday;
the waters should go first, followed by the sacrificer, the King [Soma], and the two churning sticks.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one may occupy the sacrificial hall at will, either in the forenoon or in the afternoon.
One should cause the *dīkṣaṇīyā* offering to be completed before sunset.
(21.7:80.10) Regarding the carrying away of the fires.
"One should carry them as perpetual fires," says Baudhāyana;
"having consigned them into the two kindling woods," says Śālīki.
(21.7:81.1) "The oblation of the seven hotṛs."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that after having offered the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula, one should offer the Saptahotṛ formula.
"The offering for the sacrificial post is the invocation."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
(21.7:81.5) "The preparation of garments."
Baudhāyana says there are eight; Śālīki says there are seven.
"The preparation of black antelope skins."
Baudhāyana says there are five;
Śālīki says there are six.
(21.7:81.9) "The preparation of the black antelope horn."
"It should have three folds," says Baudhāyana; "five folds," says Śālīki;
"it should be entirely whole," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the "bestowal of the vow."
Regarding the vessel: Baudhāyana says it is a *kaṃsa*, while Śālīki says it is a *camasa*.
Regarding the performance of the *pravargya* rite.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should not perform the Pravargya at the first Soma sacrifice;
for the subsequent sacrifice will be one that inclines toward him.
Śālīki, however, says: "One should not even go near the Pravargya."
(21.8:81.17) Regarding "visiting sacred fords":
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having turned clockwise, one should go to this bathing-place; then one should turn back from that point by moving away from the center.
On this point, Śālīki used to say: "Having turned away from the center, one should go to this bathing-place; then one should turn clockwise from that point."
Then, while he is facing eastward, [the teacher] moistens his right godāna lock with water.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should perform both [actions] for him with the mantra.
"Anointing. Thus [it is said].
The Sūtra [prescribes] the method of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having taken [the ointment] with the formula, 'Thou art the milk of the great ones,' one should anoint [the eyes] with the formula, 'Thou art the bestower of luster; bestow luster upon me.'"
"O collyrium! (21.8:82.6)
The Sūtra [prescribes] Śālīki’s view.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having taken it with the formula, 'Thou art the pupil of Vṛtra,' one should apply the ointment with the formulas, 'Thou art the protector of the eye; protect my eye.'"
(21.8:82.9) "He anoints three times without setting [the vessel] down, and twice more; 'he anoints five times,' so says the Brāhmaṇa; indeed, five times on the right and five times on the left."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"Purification," it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having divided [the hair] into three groups of seven, one should purify it at the region of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) with one [group], then at the region of the navel with another, and then at the region of the ankles with the other. Then, having sprinkled them with water, one should pull them out toward the north.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One purifies with two [groups], one purifies with three; having purified him by means of these [hair-tufts] twenty-one times, each in a separate grasp, then, having sprinkled them with water, one should pull them out toward the north."

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should purify him at the place of the vital breaths with all [the verses] together: 'May the Lord of Thought purify you; may the Lord of Speech purify you; may the god Savitṛ purify you with a flawless filter, with the rays of the bright sun.
Having sprinkled [him] with water over each deity as it is recited, one should dig up [the plant] toward the north."
Then, having placed him upon his left hand, he says: "Come hither."
"It is to the south," so it has been stated.
The former ritual procedure is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Then he should lead him around in front of the Āhavanīya fire.
"Behind," it is said.
The former procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
Regarding the leading forth of the wife: [the rule is as follows].
Śālīki holds that one should [use] the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having purified it while it is indeed pure and having brought it forward with the entire verse, one should cause it to sit behind the Gārhapatya fire."
"The consecration of the wife," so [it is said].
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should initiate the wife at the end of the *haviṣkṛt* formula during the introductory oblation (*prāyaṇīya*)."
"He does not lead the sacrificer to the vow."
Śālīki holds that the sūtra [is correct].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In the ritual procedure (*tantra*) of the Soma sacrifice, the *yājamāna* section pertaining to the cake-offering (*puroḍāśa*) should be repeated, except for the re-grasping of the sacrifice."
"He does not gird the wife," so it is said.
Śālīki says that the procedure is according to the Sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having bound her at the Dīkṣaṇīyā offering, one should unbind her once it is completed, either together with the Adhvaryu’s ritual or the Sacrificer’s ritual, or in each respective ritual sequence;
from that point onward, one should bind her with the rites pertaining to the cake-offering."
"The swelling of the *dhruvā*."
Baudhāyana used to say that both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer should swell the *dhruvā* ladle;
Śālīki, however, says that the Adhvaryu alone, having swollen the *dhruvā*, should offer the consecration oblations (*dīkṣā-āhutis*).
(21.8:84.6) [This is] the offering of the initiation oblations.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should offer the fifth oblation after having recited the fourth.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Having offered three consecutive oblations with the formula *ākūtyai prayuje*, and having passed over [the next two] with *sarasvatyai pūṣṇe 'gnaye*, one should offer this [oblation] with *āpo devīr bṛhatīr viśvaśambhuvas* and then perform the lifting of the vessel."
(21.9:84.11) "Of the two black antelope skins."

"Baudhāyana says that one should consecrate [the sacrificer] with two pieces of black antelope skin joined together. Now, if there should be only one, he should sew it against the right shoulder-blade. Śālīki says that there should be only a single piece of black antelope skin."
"The touching together of the white and the black."
"The thumb is on the white part and the finger on the black part"—
thus one should touch the white and the black, says Baudhāyana;
"one should touch this junction with the flat of the hand," says Śālīki.
Aupamanyava says that one may even touch him with only a single finger.
(21.9:85.3) Regarding the crawling upon the black antelope skin:
Śālīki holds that this is the rule for the *sūtra*.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should pause after either the first or the second half-verse; with the third [half-verse], one should proceed to the middle part."
The tying of knots has been explained.
Then he wraps his head with a turban, moving it from left to right.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that he should be completely covered by his garment alone.
(21.9:85.9) Regarding the handing over of the black antelope horn: //
Śālīki says that one should [hand over] the cord.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should hand over the black antelope horn to him with the entire mantra,
and one should dig up the edge of the altar silently.
(21.9:85.11) He should silently touch the hair-parting.
(21.9:85.12) Regarding the bestowal of the staff:
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should hand over the staff to him with the entire mantra: "May the divine tree be well-established; standing upright, protect me from misfortune."
(21.9:85.15) Then he causes him to recite the formula for taking hold of the sacrifice.

Śālīki holds that the *sūtra* [is authoritative]. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Indeed, these mantras are seen to be for the purpose of making the offering (*maṣṭikaraṇa*): 'Svāhā! I take up the sacrifice with the mind; svāhā! To Heaven and Earth; svāhā! From the wide mid-region; svāhā! I take up the sacrifice from the wind.'"
Regarding "forming a fist": [it refers to] making a fist.
Baudhāyana says that there should be the clenching of the fists while joined with the utterance of the *vācya* formula;
Śālīki says it should be from the release of the intermediate consecration (*āvāntaradīkṣā*).
(21.9:86.5) Regarding "making known": [it refers to] the act of announcing.
"One should announce [the initiate] according to his caste," says Baudhāyana;
"one should simply say, 'This Brāhmaṇa has been initiated,'" says Śālīki.
"The milking for the vow."
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that the sacrificer’s vow should consist solely of what is brought through the western door.
"The two *yajuṣ* formulas are to be supplied as continuations."
Baudhāyana says that the two should continue together until the casting away of the black antelope skin;
Śālīki says until the release of the intermediate consecration; Aupamanyava says until the bringing forward of the sacrificial gifts.
"The two *yajuṣ* verses for lying down."
The sūtra belongs to Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: one should lie down with the words, "O Agni, do thou watch well. Intending to observe the vow, one should sip water with the verse, "We meditate upon the divine thought."
(21.10:86.15) Now, he sends out those who carry gifts.
(21.10:86.15) "Except for the Ugra and the Śūdra," says Baudhāyana. (21.10:87.1) "Except for the Ugtras," says Śālīki.
"All [should be excluded] for the sake of the success of the sacrifice," says Aupamanyava.
The *yajus* for lying down, the *yajus* for waking up, the *yajus* for setting out, and the *yajus* for mounting.
"Baudhāyana says that these [rites] are to be performed as appendages;
Śālīki says that they should be performed only once, either for the day or for the night."
(21.10:87.6) Regarding the acceptance of sacrificial gifts: thus it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should receive with the mantra whatever has been born; even when it has come again, one should receive it with the mantra alone.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should receive with the mantra whatever has been born; for that [first portion] it would be as if already received. But from this point onward, only what is newly arrived should be received with the mantra."
"The gift for one whose [lineage] is unknown."
The former option is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
(21.10:88.1) Regarding the departure: //
The former ritual procedure is that of Śālīki; the latter is that of Baudhāyana.
Now, if someone should encounter him while he is walking at the time for his vow-food.

Baudhāyana says that one should churn the fires, spread them out, and then observe the vow. Śālīki says that one should place the two kindling woods to the north, enclose the area to the south, and then observe the vow.
Now, if he comes upon water that is not bridged over.

Śālīki says that one should recite the *sūtra* [as prescribed]. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "At whatever place one comes upon water that has not yet been crossed over, there he should mutter: 'O divine waters, O son of the waters, that wave of yours which is fit for oblation, powerful, and most intoxicating—that I take from you. Having said this, he should pick up three clods of earth."
He should place one of them at the edge of the water with the words: "May I not step upon you. Then, while shaking another, he should run after it with the words: "The unbroken thread.
Then he should place another at the edge of the water with the words: "May I follow along the earth."
"He either plunges into it or crosses over it;
having made a bridge, he passes beyond. So says the Brāhmaṇa.
"On a red hide," [he says].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that it may even be one that has not been mounted.
At the drawing of the *aṃśu* cup, there is gold.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"The settling upon the sacrificial ground for the gods."
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should first settle upon the sacrificial ground (*devayajana*) among those places belonging to the three Vedas; for it is known: "This earth, indeed, is the entire altar."
The offering of the Prāyaṇīya oblation has been explained.
"The cooking of the *prāyaṇīya* [oblation]," so it is said.
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana;
"in water," says Śālīki.
Regarding the setting down of the *prāyaṇīya* [offering].
"One should set down the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ [offering]," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the Prāyaṇīya [offering]: thus it is said.
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
"The gazing at the sun."
"One should gaze at the sun after placing gold in between," says Baudhāyana;
"without placing anything in between," says Śālīki.
(21.11:89.9) "The over-measuring of the Soma-purchase cow."
Baudhāyana says that one should cause [the sacrificer] to pass beyond at the time of the *sadas*;
Śālīki says it should be at the time of the *uparava* holes.
(21.11:89.11) "The stepping along the footprint of the Soma-purchase cow."

Baudhāyana says that for one who has passed beyond the time of the *pṛṣṭhya* [stotra], she should step out following the front foot of the southern [altar]. Śālīki says that for one who has passed beyond it, she should step out along the Great Altar (*mahāvedi*) itself, regardless of which [foot] it may be.
(21.11:89.14) [The ritual] regarding the tracing around the footprint of the cow for the purchase of Soma.
Śālīki says it should be with the cord.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should trace around the footprint with both the wooden sword and the black antelope horn;
the black antelope horn should be on the inside.
(21.12:89.17) Regarding the pouring of water from a vessel: it means pouring water from one vessel into another.
"One should pour it out while moving clockwise," says Baudhāyana;
"according to convenience," says Śālīki.
"The attendance upon the king."
Baudhāyana used to say: "There is a plant named Uṣas;

one should make that the messenger [with these words]: 'Tell Soma for me: "This is your Gāyatra portion"; tell Soma for me: "This is your Triṣṭubh portion"; tell Soma for me: "This is your Jagatī portion"; tell Soma for me: "May he attain the sovereignty of the Chandomas."'"

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "This king is indeed manifest; one should worship him as if he were manifest, saying: 'This is your Gāyatra portion; this is your Triṣṭubh portion; this is your Jagatī portion; go to the sovereignty of the Chandomas.'"
"The pride of the king," so it is said.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should measure this verse five times while reciting it as a *nigada*, says Śālīki.
"The king's wager. (21.12:90.11)
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"One should say, 'I will buy [the Soma] from you with a cow,'" says Śālīki.
(21.12:90.13) "The taking hold of a goat."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should recite the mantra for the goat without holding it down.
(21.12:90.15) Regarding the handing over of the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa priest: [the rule is as follows].
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should approach the soma-seller with a water-pitcher and hand over the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa right there.
"The king's counter-strike."
"One should cover it with a skin having the hair on the inside," says Baudhāyana;
"with one having the neck upwards and the hair on the outside," says Śālīki.
"The grasping of the shaft."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should mutter the mantra while running westward, without maintaining physical contact with them at all.
(21.12:91.7) Regarding the royal procession: [the rule is as follows].
"One should carry it around clockwise," says Baudhāyana;
"as may be convenient," says Śālīki.
(21.12:91.9) "Regarding the attendance upon the king."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should worship the King [Soma] with rice, two fire-drills, and the royal throne.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should worship the King with a goat seized by the ear, a firebrand, and the royal throne. It is known from tradition: "That animal for Agni and Soma should be a reddish-brown, hornless, castrated, dewlapped, and fat bull."
"The consecration of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) used for the guest-offering (*ātithya*)."
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the mantras beginning with the taking up of the sword;
Śālīki says they begin with the cord;
Aupamanyava says they begin with the gathering of materials.
"The offering of the guest-offering."
Śālīki holds that one should [perform] the *sūtra* [as prescribed].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having unyoked both [the horses], one should lead the King [Soma] forward and perform the *ātithya* offering."
"Regarding service to the king."
Śālīki holds that one should recite the *sūtra*.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should attend upon the King with a *ṛc* verse, and one should present the *arghya* offering with a *ṛc* verse."
(21.13:92.8) "Worship," it is said.
"One should honor them in the order they arrived," says Baudhāyana;
"having honored the king, one should honor the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*)," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the guest-offering (*ātithya*).
Baudhāyana says that there should be both a sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) and a cow;
Śālīki says there should be only a sacrificial cake.
Regarding the taking of the portions of clarified butter.
"They may be taken four times or five times," says Baudhāyana;
"they must be taken five times only," says Śālīki.
Regarding the setting down of the *ātithya* [oblation]: thus it is said.
"One should set down the Caturhotṛ cups," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the guest-offering (ātithya).
"One should perform it in a whisper," says Baudhāyana;
"aloud," says Śālīki.
(21.13:92.19) This concerns the consumption of the *tānūnaptra* [offering].
Śālīki says that one should follow the sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should have it placed in concealment and consume it together with the vow-food at the time of the vow.
"It is the consecration of the sacrificial grass used for the *aupasada* ceremony."
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the ritual recitations beginning with the taking up of the sword;
Śālīki says they begin with the cord;
Aupamanyava says they begin with the gathering of the materials.
(21.13:93.6) Regarding the mantras of the *upasad* rites: whether they are with mantras or without mantras.
"They should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana;
"they should be silent," says Śālīki.
That which is the clarified butter used for the circumambulation should be silent.
"Apart from that, it should be accompanied by the mantra," says Aupamanyava;
"one should perform this entire rite with the ritual repetition (āvṛt)," says Aupamanyavīputra.
The offering of oblations.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: Śālīki says that one should conclude these oblations while they are still directed eastward.
The oblation of the Upasads.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should offer the upasad oblations without stepping across at all.
Regarding the overnight storage of the offering-ladles: [the rule is as follows].
"They should lie around for a full day and night," says Baudhāyana;
"only during the day," says Śālīki; "one should employ [the ritual] at the beginning of each individual rite," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the carrying away of the *stambayajus*.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that the Āgnīdhra should carry [the fire] even from the time of the *uparava* holes.
The tracing around of the *cātvāla* pit has been explained.
The carrying forth of the fires of the worlds has been explained.
"The worship of the wooden mallets and the striking-sticks."
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having performed the second tracing around while it possesses the fire, having leveled the ground, and having held the wooden sword (sphya) crosswise, one should cause the sacrificer to stand upon the rubbish-heap (utkara) facing the wooden sword and the mallets."
"The consecration of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) belongs to the offering to Agni and Soma."
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the mantras beginning with the taking up of the sword;
Śālīki says they begin with the cord;
Aupamanyava says they begin with the gathering of the materials.
(21.14:94.12) [The rule] regarding the following along with the animal dedicated to Agni and Soma.
"One should walk along [the path]," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not walk along [the path]," says Śālīki.
(21.14:94.14) Regarding the placing of the fuel and the sacrificial grass: [the rule is as follows].
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "In this very place, one should bring the fuel and sacrificial grass for him while he is seated;
having taken that, he should go toward the east, and with kusha grass in his hand, he should go forward while spreading it along the *pṛṣṭhyā* line."
Regarding the turning toward the two *havirdhāna* sheds.
"One should turn [the fire] back after placing either wood or grass in between," says Baudhāyana;
"without placing anything in between," says Śālīki.
(21.14:95.4) Regarding the sprinkling of the two *havirdhāna* carts:
Baudhāyana says that one should sprinkle [the site] with consecrated water silently;
Śālīki says that one should do so with water from water-pots.
(21.14:95.6) There is an oblation over the two tracks.
The Sūtra belongs to Aupamanyavīputra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should offer oblations upon the track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, anoint all the axle-sockets, and touch [the cart] on all sides.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should offer oblations upon all the tracks, anoint all the axle-sockets, and touch [the cart] on all sides.
"The slaying of the enemy."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should drive in the post to the south of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and to the south of the northern one;
Śālīki says it should be both to the south and to the north; Aupamanyava says it should be in the middle.
"The stitching together of the door-posts and the arms."
Baudhāyana says that one should sew around all the door-posts and cross-beams with the mantra;
Śālīki says [they should be sewn] from the front to the front; Aupamanyava says [they should be sewn] from the south to the south.
(21.15:96.1) "The offering over the Audumbarī post."
The Sūtra belongs to Aupamanyavīputra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer while sacrificing in this very manner, having placed gold in between.
Śālīki says: "One should place the gold in both forks and then offer."
Regarding the drawing of the *vasatīvarī* waters.
Śālīki holds that the *sūtra* [is authoritative].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should draw the *vasatīvarī* waters so that they are bright on both sides and contain the sun;
those [waters] are indeed bright.
"One should cause [the Soma] to swell with them;
one should press with them"— having thus established the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, one should take up the *vasatīvarī* waters, says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the tracing around the *uparava* pits.
"One should draw each [line] three times," says Baudhāyana;
"once each," says Śālīki.
(21.15:96.11) The carrying away of the dust from the *uparava* holes.
Śālīki says that one should [use] the *sūtra*.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should dig up the ground beneath the sacrificer’s feet, carry it to the *utkara*, and then touch it.
Regarding the sprinkling of the *uparava* holes: [the ritual procedure is as follows].

(21.15:96.14) "One should sprinkle each [part] three times," says Baudhāyana; (21.15:96.15) "once each," says Śālīki. (21.15:96.15) "In that [vessel] one should pour water, and into that one should scatter barley; in this very way one should perform this threefold rite," says Aupamanyava.
Aupamanyavīputra says that one should perform all of this according to the ritual procedure for the *karma*.
The pouring out of the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should pile the Āgnīdhrīya hearth at the edge of the altar and the Mārjālīya hearth at the edge of the altar;
having piled the Dhiṣṇiya hearths, one should effect an orientation toward the north.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should pile the Āgnīdhrīya hearth within the altar and the Mārjālīya hearth within the altar.
Having piled the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, one should not perform the rite with the conclusion toward the north.
(21.15:97.6) Regarding the strewing of the sacrificial altar: thus it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Three [strewings] to the south, three to the north, and the seventh in the middle; they should proceed while spreading them eastward at the time of the *pṛṣṭhyā*.
Aupamanyava, however, says: "They should descend upon it from the front, spreading them westward."
(21.15:97.10) Regarding the taking up and setting down of the clarified butter portions for the Agniṣomīya sacrifice.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should take the clarified butter portions for the Agniṣomīya sacrifice in the wife’s hall itself and place them on the mound; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the term "samanvānayana": it means causing [the student] to reflect upon or bring to mind [the teachings].
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should not heed [this], says Śālīki.
Regarding the "vow of giving half the breast" (*ardhastanavratapradāna*).
Baudhāyana says that one should give the old Gārhapatya fire, whether it has been joined with the new fire or not, as the *ardhastanavrata* (the vow of half the breast).
Śālīki says that one should not give the *ardhastanavrata*.
(21.15:98.4) [This is] the oblation for the rites of dismissal.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should offer four portions of ghee taken in four ladlings.
The collection of the *vasatīvarī* waters.
"One should recite [the verses] in succession," says Baudhāyana; "one should not recite them in succession," says Śālīki.
(21.15:98.8) Regarding the secondary oblation of the omenta: //
"One should offer oblations for each of those [verses]," says Baudhāyana;
"both at the beginning and at the end," says Śālīki.
(21.15:98.10) [The ritual] for the removal of the heart-spikes (*hṛdayaśūla*).
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki.
(21.15:98.12) Regarding the carrying around of the *vasatīvarī* waters.
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "While carrying them in this very manner, having placed them in front of the sacrificial post and having set them down behind the Gārhapatya fire, one should touch them while they are placed in the Āgnīdhra shed, saying: 'Be watchful at the sacrifice!'"
Regarding the taking up and setting down of the clarified butter for the *savanīya* offering.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"One should take the clarified butter portions for the *savanīya* offering in the Āgnīdhra fire-chamber itself and place them on the mound (*khara*)," says Śālīki.
Regarding the laying of the great enclosing-sticks made of Udumbara wood.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that these should indeed be formulas for the *sruva* ladle.
"The bringing down for the king."
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should bring down the King [Soma] at the morning pressing itself for the sake of all the pressings."
The oblation of the Pañcahotṛ.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that after having offered the Caturhotṛ oblation, one should offer the Pañcahotṛ oblation.
"The commencement of the Prātaranuvāka."
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Ārtabhāgīputra used to say: "One should commence the morning litany with a silent offering of a single potsherd."
(21.16:99.11) Regarding the offering of the *savanīya* oblations: thus [it is said].
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should offer the *savanīya* oblations at the morning pressing alone, for all the pressings."
(21.16:99.14) For those [offerings], he causes the call to the preparer of the oblation to be raised over the rice alone; they take up the barley.
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "In the case of barley, the ritual action accompanied by mantras should be repeated starting from the pouring [of the grains], but the call to the *haviṣkṛt* should be performed as a single, common procedure (*tantra*)."
Regarding the pouring out of the water for the consecration.
(21.16:99.17) "One should pour out [the water] for the Āpyas behind the Gārhapatya," says Baudhāyana. (21.16:100.1) "Having passed beyond it in front," says Śālīki.
(21.16:100.1) "Either in front or behind," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the placing of the vessels: thus it is said.
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should set down the vessels on the mound (khara) and take them up as required for their respective purposes.
Then he draws the Ekadhana cups, either with the formula, "I draw you, acceptable to Indra," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"Praskandana, the son of Apta."
Baudhāyana says that one should cause [the soma] to fall from the *hotṛ*’s cup;
Śālīki says it should be from the *vāsatīvara* jar.
"The performance of the sacrifice," he said.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that [the formulas] are fixed; Śālīki says that one should perform the ritual-formulating acts according to the specific sacrifice being performed.
Regarding the drawing of the *dadhigraha* cup: [the rule is as follows].
Śālīki says that one should use a wooden vessel.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should take it with a vessel made of udumbara wood, and having offered it, one should throw that very vessel into the fire right there.
"The gift is for the sake of the sacrificial fee."
This sūtra is indeed twofold.
Over those *nigrābhya* waters, he causes the sacrificer to recite.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having either pressed [the soma] against the thigh or against the chest, and having restrained them, he causes the sacrificer to recite while those [pressings] are being performed."
"The offering for the king."
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should extract the King [Soma] at the morning pressing itself for all the pressings.
"When the two portions have been spilled, he makes [the sacrificer] recite."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should cause [the sacrificer] to recite only when the Aṃśu cup has been spilled during the Upāṃśu sacrifice.
The offering of the *upāṃśu* and *antaryāma* [cups] is performed in a low voice.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should offer both oblations after sunrise.
Aupamanyava says that one should offer both oblations before sunrise.
Regarding the drawing of the Āgrayaṇa cup: [the rule is as follows].
Śālīki says that one should draw the Soma according to the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should draw two streams at the morning pressing, three at the midday pressing, and four at the third pressing.
(21.17:101.9) "In the case of the verses for consecrating the drops," it is said.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that one should offer these as oblations with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*) alone.
Regarding the drawing of the Pavamāna cups.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should set them down after wiping them while they are still joined together.
(21.18:101.13) This is the oblation of the *saṃtanī* verses.
Śālīki holds that one should [use] the sūtra [as it stands].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should also pour down the *vasatīvarī* waters with these same formulas.
(21.18:101.15) Regarding the introductory rite for the Pavamāna hymns.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
one should set it up after taking two blades of sacrificial grass from the *sadas* itself; thus says Śālīki.
"The seating of the Brahman priest."
Baudhāyana says that one should sit down just as [one does] in the *sadasya* hall;
Śālīki says it should be just as in the *darśapūrṇamāsa* sacrifices.
Regarding the seating of the sacrificer: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana says that one should sit down in the same manner as at the *sadasya* [sacrifice].
Śālīki says it should be in the same manner as at the New and Full Moon sacrifices (*darśapūrṇamāsa*).
(21.18:102.3) Then he hands two blades of sacrificial grass to either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"Thou art the under-layer for the Ṛc and Sāman, for the procreation of the pair," or silently.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
When the fifth [chapter] has been commenced, he causes [the student] to recite.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one may cause [the student] to recite on any [day] whatsoever.
"The oblation of the seven hotṛs."
The rule of Baudhāyana is that [one should offer the Saptahotṛ formula];
Śālīki says that one should offer the Saptahotṛ at each pressing.
Regarding the distribution of the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having taken embers from the Āgnīdhrīya fire, one should scatter them there in the Āgnīdhrīya; then, having spread the other hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*) in their proper sequence, one should effect an ending toward the north. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having taken embers from the Āgnīdhrīya fire, one should scatter them there in the Āgnīdhrīya; then, [one should proceed] with the others in their proper sequence."
Having spread out the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, one should not perform the concluding rite by moving toward the north.
(21.18:103.1) Regarding the sprinkling of the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths: |||
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the production of the sacrificial post and its cord: [the rule is as follows].

Baudhāyana says that one should cause the sacrificial post (*yūpa*), the *svaru*, and the *raśanā* to be produced; Śālīki says it is the animal (*paśu*); Aupamanyava says it is the ritual procedure (*tantra*).
"It is the deity," says Aupamanyavīputra.
(21.19:103.6) "Crawling," so it is said.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki maintains that the sacrificer should remain at the western door itself.
"In the case of the *ukthya* recitations belonging to the third pressing."

Baudhāyana used to say that one should indeed proceed toward the *ukthya-vigrahas* belonging to the third pressing, toward the *ṣoḍaśin*, toward the *rātri-paryāyas*, and toward the *saṃdhi* for the *rathaṃtara*.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "This is merely an extension of the third pressing; whatever one proceeds toward at the third pressing, that shall indeed be considered as already proceeded toward for them."
Aupamanyava says that one should proceed from all the pressings at the morning pressing itself.
Regarding the curdled milk (*āmikṣā*), there is the question of whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
"It should be accompanied by mantras and one should follow all the pressings," says Baudhāyana; "it should be silent and one should follow all the pressings," says Śālīki;
"it should be accompanied by mantras, and it should belong specifically to the morning pressing," says Aupamanyava.
(21.19:104.3) Regarding the removal of the *savanīya* offerings:
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should remove the *savanīya* offerings from their respective vessels.
(21.19:104.5) "<Of the morning pressing>," thus [he says].
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should simply say, "Of the morning pressing."
The subsequent collection of the *savanīya* offerings.
"One should join [the formulas]," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not join them," says Śālīki.
Regarding the taking up of those things to be seized in return.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should take up the *pratinirgrāhya* cups from the very *dvidevatya* offerings; so says Śālīki.
"The pouring of the oblation," he said.

(21.19:104.11) Regarding the *sūtra*, it is Baudhāyana’s view that one should offer this *āghāra* libation from the cup itself; Śālīki says it should be offered from the *droṇakalaśa* with the dipping-spoon (*pariplu-pātra*); Aupamanyava says [it should be done] from the *droṇakalaśa* with the dipping-spoon.
"Añjīgavi says that one should merely mutter this Yajus formula; one should not pour out this Āghāra libation."
"The lid for the residue."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
Śālīki says that one should cover over whatever amount of the residue remains.
"The place for the *camasa* cups."
Baudhāyana says that one should move the ladles forward to the east along their front; Śālīki says that one should move them backward to the north along their rear.
Regarding the conjunction of the two planets.
Baudhāyana says that one should join together both the two cubits and the two cups;
Śālīki says that one should join only the two cups.
(21.20:105.8) "<[For the Soma] rich in clarity, [rich in] the stirred draught... thus [he says].

The rule is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should simply say: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the Soma-pressings dedicated to Indra—the morning pressings, bright, stirred, and dripping with sweetness."
(21.20:105.10) [This is] the offering of the *manthin* and the *saṃsrāva*.
Śālīki says that one should use the *sūtra* [as it stands].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should draw out embers from the Āhavanīya fire toward the north and pour the residue of the *manthin* cup as an oblation upon them.
The offering of the goblets belonging to the *hotṛ* priests.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer these together with the Śukra and Manthin cups once, having drawn them up twice.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should not offer these together with the Śukra and Manthin cups once; rather, one should offer them only after they have been drawn up twice."
Regarding the consumption of the cups for two deities.

The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should consume the cups for the dual deities while holding them to the vital breaths; Śālīki says they should be consumed with the *dīrghabhakṣa* formula; Aupamanyava says they should indeed be consumed with the *dīrghabhakṣa* alone.
(21.20:106.4) Now, he makes these cups for the dual deities non-empty.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that these [vessels] should remain non-empty by means of Soma alone.
Then he sets them down on the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should set them down directly below the upahavya vessel.
"Either with the words, 'I place speech in speech,' or silently."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
(21.20:106.11) Regarding the individual consumption of the cups belonging to the *hotraka* priests.
"One should consume it in response," says Baudhāyana; "one should not consume it in response," says Śālīki.
Regarding the term "pratyabhimarśana" (the touching back).
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should touch [the vessels] while still consuming them, at the conclusion of the consumption of the portions.
Regarding the drawing of the cup for Indra and Agni.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Dīrghavātsya used to say: "One should take it with the primary vessel."
"The shaking after the *nārāśaṃsa* cups."
"They should cause them to shake," says Baudhāyana; "they should not cause them to shake," says Śālīki;
"one should not even lift them up," says Aupamanyava.
This refers to the pressing at the midday libation.
"Baudhāyana says that they should approach the *nigrābha* after pressing nine times each;
Śālīki says it should be an unlimited number."
Regarding the drawing of the two Marutvatīya cups.
Śālīki says that one should draw the *sūtra* cup.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should draw it immediately after the *āgrayaṇa*; for this [cup] belongs to the world of what is to be drawn.
When the eighth [day] has begun, he causes [the student] to recite.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should cause [the student] to recite on whichever [day] one pleases.
(21.21:107.13) Regarding the drawing of the *dadhigharma* [curd-heat] libation.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that the Āgnīdhra should take it up.
Aupamanyava says that, having enclosed it and performed the pacification on both sides, the Āgnīdhra alone should take it up.
Regarding the performance of the *dadhigharma* offering.
"One should perform it in a whisper," says Baudhāyana;
"aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the curd-mixture (dadhigharma).
Śālīki holds that there should be a *sūtra* [on this point].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "The others should consume [the portion] by means of the *avadhra-bhakṣaṇa* formula; only the sacrificer should consume it directly with the mantra recited in the forest (*araṇye 'nuvākyena*)."
Regarding the non-performance of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should carry only a single sacrificial fee along the southern path,
while the others should proceed according to available space.
"It is called 'transmigration'."
Baudhāyana says that once the sacrificial fees have been led forward, they may move about according to their purpose;
Śālīki says that the Adhvaryu must not pass westward toward the Sadas before the Soma sacrifice has been concluded.
Regarding the throwing away of the black antelope horn.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that once the sacrificial fees have been led away, one should throw the black antelope horn into the *cātvāla* pit.
"In the dialogue with Ātreya."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should ask three times without interweaving [the names], saying: 'Who is the Ātreya? Who is the Ātreya?'"
Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
Baudhāyana used to say that one should give these [gifts] to the great officiating priests (*mahartvijas*), but they should not follow after the *hotraka* priests;
Śālīki says that they should neither follow after the *hotrakas* nor give them to the *sadasya*, for no specific enumeration of this [procedure] is known.
The oblation of the two Marutvatīya offerings.

Baudhāyana used to say: "That which the Adhvaryu offers should be both *vaṣaṭ*-uttered and *anuvaṣaṭ*-uttered, while the other [offering] should be *an-anuvaṣaṭ*-uttered. Śālīki said: "Both should indeed be *an-anuvaṣaṭ*-uttered. Aupamanyava said: "Both should indeed be *anuvaṣaṭ*-uttered."
Regarding the drawing of the third Marutvatīya cup: [the rule is as follows].
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Dīrghavātsya used to say: "One should take it with the primary vessel."
"The shaking after the *nārāśaṃsa* cups."
"They should shake them along," says Baudhāyana; "They should not shake them along," says Śālīki;
"One should not even lift them up," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the Soma sacrifice, there is the question of whether it is with mantras or without mantras.
Baudhāyana says that [the cake] should be accompanied by a mantra;
Śālīki says it should be silent.
Aupamanyava says that only the Soma-cake should be accompanied by a mantra, while the single-potsherd cake should be silent.
This is the pressing at the third libation.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that [the formula] should be recited as "that which makes swell"; Śālīki says that one should simply say "that which possesses rays" (*aṃśumat*).
Regarding the drawing of the Āditya cup: [the rule is as follows].
Śālīki says that one should take the *sūtra* [cup].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should take it before the pressing; one should silently pour in the boiled *śṛtātaṅkya*."
Regarding the lifting up of the Āditya cup.
Baudhāyana says that one should recite by half-verses;
Śālīki says verse by verse.
The mixing of the *maitrāvaruṇa* [cup] and the pouring of the *āśira* [milk mixture].
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should indeed mix the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa with milk, and one should pour the *āśira* (curd-mixture) into it."
When the ninth [chapter] has been introduced, he causes [the student] to recite.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one may have [the student] recite on any [day] whatsoever.
This is the satiation of the *hotṛ* priests.
Śālīki holds that this is the rule of the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should satisfy the Hotṛ-officiants at each pressing:
five at the morning pressing, six at the midday pressing, and seven at the third pressing; so says Aupamanyava.
"In the domestic fires," it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having walked around [the fires], one should consecrate the domestic fires with mantras; one should place pieces of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) into the cups, and at this very point, one should recite the *Ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should indeed consecrate the domestic fires while walking around them; one should place the pieces of the sacrificial cake beside the cups, and one should recite the *Ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula after [placing them]."
Regarding the taking up and setting down of the Sāvitra cup.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should wipe it with the formula "sa juṣṭam" and then set it down.
"Therefore, he responds with the *anyatomada* chant."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
one should respond with "madā moda iva," says Śālīki.
"The shaking after the *nārāśaṃsa* cups."
"They should shake them along," says Baudhāyana; "they should not shake them along," says Śālīki;
"nor indeed should one lift them up," says Aupamanyava.
"Regarding the conduct of the Soma sacrifice."
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the complete sacrifice of the Soma offering.
Baudhāyana used to say that whether the two deities, Agni and Viṣṇu, are joined together or separated, they should both be recited in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
Śālīki says that when they are joined together they should be recited in a low voice, but when they are separated they should be recited aloud (*uccais*).
This is the distribution of the hearths belonging to the third pressing.
Śālīki [holds] the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should distribute the four hearths (dhiṣṇiya) using the embers of the Soma-vessel, whether one has already performed the rite or not.
Regarding the mixing of the pātnīvata offering.

The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should mix the *pātnīvata* cup with curds or milk; thus says Śālīki. One should mix the *pātnīvata* cup with the remnant of the clarified butter used for sprinkling the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths; thus says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the leading forth of the wife.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that [the verses] beginning with "āsītāpohiṣṭhīyābhyah" should be recited at this very point.
"Therefore, he responds with a chant that is intoxicating on both sides."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana:
"One should respond with 'modā moda iva'," says Śālīki.
"The displacement of Dhruva."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki holds that this entire mantra should be used for the pouring down [of the water].
"The place for the *camasa* cups."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Into these [vessels], he throws three knots of *dūrvā* grass and one tuft of *darbha* grass each.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that these sacrificial spoons should be made of wood alone.
Regarding the *aupayaja* offerings.
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should bring embers from the Āgnīdhra fire for both the Agniṣomīya and the Savanīya offerings, and from the Śāmitra fire for the barren cow dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa.
The offering of the two oblations of self-reproach (*mindāhuti*) is performed as follows.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should offer the Mindā oblations beforehand;
having offered the Mindā oblations, one should draw the Hāriyojana cup."
"The performance [of the sacrifice] is with *śākala* [wood] according to the *caryā*."
Śālīki holds that one should recite the *sūtra* [as given].
