Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "As many sins as one may recognize having been committed, one should add [the fuel] with the formula: 'Thou art the expiation for them.'"
This is the worship of the Sun.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that they should worship the Āhavanīya fire alone with this Yajus formula.
(21.24:113.9) Regarding the throwing away of the black antelope horn: //
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The purificatory bath," he says.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Having planted this very [grain] mixed with potsherds upon this sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), one should go down for the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) with the cooking pots, the pressing-stones, and the Vāyavya cup."
"The floating of the pressing-stones for the Vāyavya cup."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that they should wash [the vessels] and then bring them forward.
Having washed these pots, they should bring them out;
in them they should cook these oblations for the Devikās—so says Baudhāyana. They should merely rinse them—so says Śālīki.
Regarding the washing of the black antelope skin: [the rule is as follows].
Śālīki says that one should [use] the thread.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: having unfastened the black antelope skin and sprinkled it with water, one should give it to a son or a pupil, or one should use it as a support for the offering-ladle;
or indeed, one may undergo initiation again with it.
Or rather, one should sacrifice again with this very same [offering].
"The preparation of the sacrificial grass for the concluding offering."
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the mantras beginning with the taking up of the sword;
Śālīki says those beginning with the cord;
Aupamanyava says those beginning with the gathering of materials.
The offering of the concluding oblation (*udayanīya*).
"Having placed it in the *sruc* ladle, or having placed it in the *sthālī* pot together with the charred scrapings, one should pour it out."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
(21.25:114.9) "Regarding the cooking of the *udayanīya* [offering]," it is said.
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana;
"in water," says Śālīki.
Regarding the non-circumambulation of the sacrificial porridge.
"One should carry it around," says Baudhāyana; "one should not carry it around," says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the concluding oblation.
"One should set down the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ [offering]," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the concluding oblation (*udayanīya*).
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should perform the *udayanīya* offering at the *āhavanīya* fire itself.
Regarding the performance of the *anūbandhya* animal sacrifice.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
"One should sacrifice with the curdled milk (*āmikṣā*) dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa," says Śālīki.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should also immolate a goat as an animal victim here.
"But one should indeed conclude the ritual procedure with the eleventh *parayāja* offering."
(21.25:115.4) This is the supplementary oblation for the omenta.
"One should offer oblations for each of those [verses]," says Baudhāyana;
"at the beginning and at the end," says Śālīki.
(21.25:115.6) This is the ritual for the removal of the heart-spikes.
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki.
"One should drive away all the cattle and sheep," says Baudhāyana;
"except for the bull and the cow," says Śālīki.
Regarding the curdled milk (*āmikṣā*), [the question is] whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
"It should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana;
"it should be silent," says Śālīki.
"To the [deity] of Mitra and Varuṇa, on the enclosing sticks," he says.
Śālīki holds that the rule is according to the Sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having broken off two front pillars of either the Sadas or the Havirdhāna sheds, one should fashion the enclosing sticks for the Maitrāvaruṇī offering from split bamboo."
(21.26:116.1) "The concluding ceremony" (udavasāna).
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should conclude the rite with the full-offering alone.
"The gift is for the sake of the sacrificial fee."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that in this case, the gift need not be given if it is not intended.
Regarding the performance of the offerings to the Devikās: [the rule is that] one should offer them in the order in which they are enumerated.
This is the Sūtra of Aupamanyavīputra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that three oblations should follow the animal-cake of the Anūbandhya sacrifice, and three should follow the Udavasānīyā offering;
Śālīki, however, maintains that all [the oblations] should follow the animal-cake of the Anūbandhya.
One should sacrifice to the Devikās with clarified butter alone; so says Āñjīgavi.
"Relinquishing [the sacred fires] by means of the fires."
"One should settle [the fires] with the eternal ones," says Baudhāyana;
"having consigned them into the two kindling woods," says Śālīki.
(21.26:116.11) Regarding the two Agnihotra offerings, there is a compensatory oblation (*pratihoma*).
"One should offer the counter-oblation," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not offer the counter-oblation," says Śālīki; "one should not offer the counter-oblation," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the ritual procedure for the sacred fires.
(22.1:117.2) Regarding the preparation of the mortar.
Baudhāyana says that one should perform it in the intermediate direction between the north and the east;
Śālīki says that it should be performed in the north alone.
The oblation of the Sāvitra verses.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; however, Śālīki says that for the sake of prosperity one should also offer a fourfold-drawn portion here.
(22.1:117.6) "The taking up of the donkey's halter."
"One should take it up with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
The placing of the ant-hill clod and the seating of the Vaiśya are [performed] at the Nidhana.

Śālīki prescribes the Sūtra. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should place a termite mound; one should not seat a Vaiśya there; one should go to where a natural excavation is found; and to whoever asks there, one should give an answer."
"Digging."
"One should dig by half-verses," says Baudhāyana; "verse by verse," says Śālīki.
He spreads it with a lotus leaf having its stalk pointing north.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should strew [the grass] with whatever has been produced; Śālīki says it should be done with exactly what has arisen.
Regarding the carrying away of the rice-balls.
The rule belongs to Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should take [the portions] four times with all [the verses] each time;
Aupamanyava says that one should take them with Gāyatrīs and settle them with Triṣṭubhs.
(22.1:117.19) Regarding the "running forth" of the horse.
Śālīki says that one should recite the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should lead the horse forward silently;
indeed, this entire formula should belong to the donkey.
(22.1:118.1) "The gazing at heaven and earth."
Regarding the two [fires], Baudhāyana says that one should look at them six times;
Śālīki says only three times;
Aupamanyava says that while looking at the junction in the eastern direction, one should mutter this mantra.
They throw the two cords into the water, or else they consume them after sprinkling them with water.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
(22.2:118.6) Regarding the making of the fire-pan: thus it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should also make a foot-measure of the *aṣāḍhā* brick for this *yājuṣī* [altar]; having taken a brick of whatever size, one should embed it in the clay. In this way, his entire fire-altar becomes *yājuṣa*.
Śālīki says: "One should fashion only a single *ukhā* with the mantra, while the others are done silently."
When all [the causes] have ceased, there is cognition.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should repeat the ritual actions accompanied by the mantras, including those dedicated to Savitṛ.
"Whatever else besides the Sāvitra [oblations]," says Śālīki.
Then he takes twenty-one dung-clods from a stallion, as well as a spade and a fire for baking.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one may take the horse of whichever horse it may be.
(22.2:118.16) "The fumigation of the fire-pan."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should fumigate with an unlimited number of mantras.
Regarding the heating of the fire-pans.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should heat only a single ukhā with the mantra, while the others are heated silently.
He causes them to extend either towards the east or towards the north.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The cooking," [he said].
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should bake the fire-pan (*ukhā*), the bulls, the *maṇḍala*-bricks, the *bārhaspatya* cake, the *mahāvīra*, and the *lokaṃpṛṇā* bricks from the Gārhapatya fire;
but everything else, including that which is prescribed for the village-fire (*grāmāgni*), from the village-fire.
Śālīki says: "Whatever is prescribed for the bricks should be baked with the village-fire, but that which is prescribed as an oblation (*havis*) should be baked from the Gārhapatya fire."
Regarding the fashioning of the animal heads: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana says they may be either actual [wooden] ones or made of clay; Śālīki says they must be actual ones;
Aupamanyava says they should be made of gold.
Aupamanyavīputra says that one should recite those mantras over the head of the victim dedicated to Vāyu.
Three times he sweeps around [the site] counter-clockwise with a branch of the *parṇa* tree.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should scatter beans all around and then chant the Yama-gāthās.
"The pouring of the libation," it is said.
"One should pour this Āghāra-libation with both mantras," says Baudhāyana; "One should pour this Āghāra-libation with this one alone: 'Hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre,'" says Śālīki.
(22.3:119.19) For one who has not yet performed the first Soma sacrifice, there is the offering of the oblations for the consecration of the Adhvara.
Having offered the oblations for the consecration of the *adhvara*, one should offer the *āgnika* oblations, says Baudhāyana;
only the *āgnika* ones, says Śālīki.
"During the consecrations on the Vairāja verses."
Baudhāyana used to say: "One who intends to perform the *sava* before a year has passed should not undergo the *vairāja* consecrations;
however, one who intends to perform the *sava* after a year has passed may undergo the *vairāja* consecrations.
Or, having maintained [the fires] for a year, he should perform the rites of a single-day sacrifice (*ekāhika*), for the fire is indeed of a single-day nature," says Śālīki.
Regarding the insertion [of fuel] for a rite performed for a specific desire.
Baudhāyana says that one should add the *kāmya* formulas after [the fire] has been produced;
Śālīki says that they should be added beforehand.
(22.3:120.6) Regarding the placing of fuel-sticks made of Udumbara wood: [the rule is as follows].
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should place only a single fuel-stick with the five-verse hymn; in that way, it shall be a rite destructive of demons."
"The placing of fuel sticks for Annapatīyā."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should add these [kindling sticks]—namely, the annapatīyā, the pratisamedhanīyā, and the vaiṣṇavī.
Regarding the conjunction of the Vātsapra and the Viṣṇukrama rites.
"One should assemble [the materials] day by day," says Baudhāyana;
"from the beginning and from the end," says Śālīki.
(22.3:120.14) Regarding the performance of an expiation when the fire in the hearth goes out.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having consecrated [the fire] and having handed it over, one should offer the *arkāhuti* oblations; then one should perform the rest of the ritual according to the regular procedure. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having consecrated [the fire] and having handed it over, one should offer the *arkāhuti* oblations, but one should not perform the rest of the ritual according to the regular procedure."
Regarding the departure.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should proceed with both [sets of formulas], those pertaining to the *adhvara* sacrifice and those pertaining to the fire-altar (*āgnika*).
Śālīki says that one should proceed with only those pertaining to the fire-altar.
Now, as for the rule that if one approaches water without having spread out [the sacrificial grass], [one should perform the following].

Śālīki says that one should use the *sūtra* [as prescribed]. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Wherever one comes upon water that has not been carried over, one should cause those ashes to enter it; one should not leave that [vessel] without its contents. Having taken as much [of the ash] as there is, one should re-establish it with the verse, 'Having settled in the womb by means of the ash. Then one should have the remainder deposited either in cooking-pots (*sthālī*) or in bowls (*sata*)."
"The settling upon the sacrificial ground."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should settle [the fire] by means of both the sacrificial rite and the fire-rite;
Śālīki says that one should do so by the fire-rite alone.
The scattering of the ritual materials.
The Sūtra belongs to Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should pour down both ashes and sand with the mantra, while the other two materials [the earth and the pebbles] should be poured down silently.
"In the piling of the Gārhapatya fire."

(22.4:121.17) Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct]. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "The taking up of the fire, the self-piling, the touching of the white and black [spots], the ascending, and the descending—one should perform all this ritual action according to the repeated procedure."
"One building it for the first time should pile a thousand-brick altar, consisting of five layers."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having completed these, while piling the fourth layer, one should thereafter take up [the altar] knee-high; this applies if it is to consist of five layers. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having completed these, while piling the fourth layer, one should thereafter take up [the altar] neck-high; this applies if it is to consist of a single layer."
Regarding the conjunction of the Vātsapra and the Viṣṇukrama rites.
Baudhāyana used to say: "If the Vātsapra should fall on the Upavasatha day, one should perform the worship with the Vātsapra and then proceed with the pouring together of the ashes.
But if the Viṣṇu-strides should fall on the Upavasatha day, one should stride with the Viṣṇu-strides, perform the worship with the Vātsapra, and then proceed with the pouring together."

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If the Vātsapra should coincide with the Upavasatha day, one should perform the worship with the Vātsapra and, on the following day, proceed with the mixing of the ashes.

But if the Viṣṇu-strides should coincide with the Upavasatha day, one should stride the Viṣṇu-steps, perform the worship with the Vātsapra, and on the following day, proceed with the mixing of the ashes itself."
Looking away from her, he throws drops of curd into it, saying either, "I place that pure [offering] for you," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Then, having filled it with sand and covered it over from above with curd, [he says].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should fill it with sand and place it on the northern part of the shed.
Regarding the taking up of the sling: [the rule is as follows].
"One should take it up with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
This is the worship of the Nairṛtis.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should perform the *tayādevata* and *sūdadohas* formulas;
Śālīki says that one should not perform them.
Regarding the pouring of water from a vessel: it means pouring water from a water-pot [over the head of the initiate].
"One should pour [the water] around it from left to right," says Baudhāyana;
"as may be convenient," says Śālīki.
(22.4:123.7) Regarding the worship of the *gārhapatya* fire:
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki, however, says that they should worship the Āhavanīya fire alone with this Yajus formula.
Regarding the carrying away of the *stambayajus* grass-bundle.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that the Āgnīdhra should also take [the earth] from the time of the uparavas.
The tracing out of the *catvāla* pit has been explained.
The carrying away of the fires of the worlds has been explained.
The recitation of the *sphya* and *vighana* formulas has been explained; now follows the ritual attendance (*upasthāna*).
"The untying of the black antelope skins."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
The laying down of the Vajriṇī bricks.
Śālīki says the sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should stand in front of the peg for the sacrificial post-hole, string the bow, discharge an arrow toward the east,
run after it, and place a stone upon its track.
In this same way on the south, then on the west, and likewise on the north.
"The bricks dedicated to Indra are the underlayers."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should place the Aindrī brick on the tail.
"Regarding the pouring from one vessel into another:
Baudhāyana says that one should pour while moving clockwise;
Śālīki says it should be done according to the position of the feet."
Regarding the placement of the bunch of *darbha* grass: [it is done] upon the supporting layer.
"May Vāk place thee upon the ocean"—thus either with these words or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the dūrvā-brick: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana used to say that one should place it together with *dūrvā* grass, or indeed with *dūrvā* alone;
Śālīki, however, says that this [grass] must be the *mantra-dūrvā*.
(22.5:124.10) "The plough and its yoke are made of udumbara wood."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that one should make it from the dārḍhya tree itself.
Regarding this pair of oxen and the plough: Baudhāyana says that men should take up the plough and yoke from the front, while the Adhvaryu follows from behind;
Śālīki says that one should plough after having visibly joined them together.
"One should perform the summary recitation," says Baudhāyana; "up to the *vājaśas*," says Śālīki.
(22.6:125.1) This is the consecration of the pairs of oxen.
"One should consecrate each of those [acts] individually," says Baudhāyana;
"all of them together," says Śālīki.
"The shaving with all-herbs."
"One should sow by half-verses," says Baudhāyana;
"verse by verse," says Śālīki.
"One exchanges one thing for another; one exchanges one thing for another."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should complete this direction while actually taking [the fire].
Aupamanyava says that one should transpose the Yajus formula with the Yajus.
Having placed bundles of *darbha* grass into the water for sprinkling, he sprinkles with them, either with the formula, "I sprinkle you, the fires, acceptable to the fires," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the jar-bricks.
Regarding the sūtra, it is Baudhāyana’s view that one should place these bricks only on the wings and the tail, according to Baudhāyani.
"When the quarters, each with its own mantra, are being occupied."
Baudhāyana says that one should proceed with the *tayādevatā* formula and perform the *sūdadohas* verse at the end;
Śālīki says that one should complete each individual brick as it is laid down.
(22.6:125.16) Regarding the laying down of the groups of bricks:
Baudhāyana says that one should proceed with the *tayādevatā* formulas and perform the *sūdadohas* verses at the end;
Śālīki says that one should complete each respective group of bricks.
(22.6:125.19) Regarding the touching [of the victim], there is an oblation.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should perform the *tayādevata* and *sūdadohas* verses before the touching and the offerings."
"The placing of the serpent-heads."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
And the mortar and pestle should be made of udumbara wood.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should make it from a Dārḍhya tree.
Regarding the threshing of all medicinal herbs.
"One should strike it with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the fire-pan (ukhā).
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should place only a single ukhā with the mantra, while the others are to be placed silently.
Regarding the placement of the animal heads: [the rule is as follows].
"One should place it in the middle," says Baudhāyana; "one should scatter it out from its ends and then place it," says Śālīki.
"The laying down of the Atharvaśiras," so it is said.
(22.7:126.13) Regarding the *sarvatomukha* altar: Baudhāyana says that one should place nine verses of the *Atharvaśiras* here in front of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stone.
Śālīki says that it is not the *Atharvaśiras*.
Regarding the placement of the *sarvatomukha* [fire-altar]: thus it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should lay down the Gāyatrī bricks according to the directions.
Regarding the laying down of the limbs.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
one should place the secondary bricks only when the primary members have been identified; thus says Śālīki.
"The bolster for the bull."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should place it so that its head is slightly turned back, just as a bull stands to bellow toward a cow in heat.
This concerns the laying down of the past sets of bricks.
Baudhāyana says that one should place the *āghāra* libation at the end; Śālīki says it should be done at the conclusion of the piling.
Regarding the "bestowal of the vow."
Baudhāyana says that one should offer the fast-food at midday;
Śālīki says it should be offered at the conclusion of the piling of the altar.
Regarding the laying down of the loose earth layer (*purīṣaciti*).
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should complete the layering of the loose earth on the very day before.
Two horses should stand on either side: a black one to the north and a white one to the south.
Regarding this very point, Baudhāyana says that one should have fodder brought to these two while they are standing right here;
Śālīki says that one should lead them out at each respective time.
"The placing of the Vālakhilya bricks."
Baudhāyana says that one should place the Vālakhilya bricks on top;
Śālīki says they should be placed at the sides.
"The abode of created beings," he said.
From the front of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stone, he should cause the cords to extend northward as far as the northern joint of the wing, or all around.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the *vyuṣṭi* bricks.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should lay these down facing west from the east; for the night shines forth from the east, facing west."
"Of those [bricks], he places the one containing loose earth in the middle," so it is said.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should place it either together with the loose earth or [simply] as loose earth;
Śālīki, however, says that it should consist of both the mantra and the loose earth.
Regarding the laying down of the Vairāja bricks.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"It is called the 'pillow of Yājñasenī'."
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
Regarding the laying down of the ghee-bricks: thus it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should either place them together with clarified butter or anoint them with clarified butter;
Śālīki says that these bricks should indeed be "mantra-buttered" (prepared with mantra and ghee);
Aupamanyava says that one should place lumps of clarified butter upon them here.
"The place for the depositing of the bricks."
Between the *jyotiṣmatī* bricks and the *bhūteṣṭakā* bricks, this constitutes the place for the insertion (*āvāpa*) of these bricks.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should place here the *saṃveśanayajus*, the *prabuddhayajus*, the *prayāṇayajus*, the *aparyāṇayajus*, the *sāmidhenīs*, the *āprīs*, and the sets of bricks that have already passed.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should not cause a mantra that does not pertain to bricks to become like one pertaining to bricks;
rather, one should place only those sets of bricks that have already passed here."
"The laying down [of the bricks] on the full moon day."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should place the Paurṇamāsī brick on the northern shoulder alone.
Regarding the laying down of the star-bricks: thus it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should place the *atreṣṭakā* bricks at every crossing-point and cause them to shine forth in each respective location.
Regarding the placement of the *sarvatomukha* fire.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Indeed, this [spot] becomes separated from the touching of the black [bull]; one who is about to lay down the *sarvatomukha* should touch a white horse."
"In cases of growth," so it is said.
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "On a single day, however many *vardhana* offerings may coincide, one should perform the *tayādevata* and *sūdadohas* verses at the conclusion of all of them."
Then he throws pieces of gold into the *prokṣaṇī* sprinkling waters—more than three, but not an unlimited number; it is declared that "a thousand" is [the intended number].
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
The oblation of the Śatarudrīya.
Regarding the two teachers' rule on the thread:
Gautama says that one should offer it in the very first row.
"Attendance by means of prostrations."

Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform the worship while still holding the bow; having turned from the northern direction and returned by the same way he came, standing behind [the altar] facing east, he should worship the upward-pointing [pole].

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should perform the worship after having already laid aside the bow; having turned from that very direction and returned by the same way he came, standing behind [the altar] facing east, he should worship the upward-pointing [pole].
While the water is being sprinkled around, he causes the sacrificer to recite.
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having sprinkled [water] around [the fire] each time, one should place the water-pot upon a stone, saying:
'O Stone, let hunger be yours! Let your heat reach so-and-so! and he should point toward whomever he hates."
(22.9:130.17) Regarding "drawing away": [it refers to] the act of dragging.
"One should draw it out half-verse by half-verse," says Baudhāyana; "verse by verse," says Śālīki.
The sprinkling of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stone.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should sprinkle this [altar] with the fire-altar being square.
Regarding the Vaiśvānara and Māruta [oblations], there is the question of whether they are with mantras or without mantras.
Baudhāyana says that they should be accompanied by mantras; Śālīki says they should be silent.
Aupamanyava says that only the Vaiśvānara [offering] should be accompanied by mantras, while the Māruta offerings should be silent.
This is the oblation for Ānīkavata.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should offer the Ānīkavat oblation in the Āhavanīya fire alone.
(22.9:131.8) Then he sprinkles that piled altar with the sprinkling of clarified butter.
Śālīki holds that the sūtra [is correct].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "While sprinkling it, one should follow the mantras according to direction and according to the order of the mantras."
Regarding the placing of the fuel.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should place the fuel with both [mantras], namely, the one pertaining to the *adhvara* and the one pertaining to the fire (*āgnika*).
Śālīki says it should be done with the *āgnika* mantra alone.
"The enclosing with *śākala* [wood chips] is prescribed."
Baudhāyana says that one should consign [the fire] to the Āhavanīya; Śālīki says it should be to the tail itself.
Regarding the performance of the two oblations with the *sruva* ladle.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the full-offering (pūrṇāhuti).
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
In this context, it is said: "While offering the oblation, one should meditate upon the directions with the mind."
"Either [he says], 'I am collecting fire from the quarters,' or he does so silently."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The locus of the sprinkling."
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
While spreading four [portions] upon it, he says:
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not spread [the underlayer].
Regarding the subsequent offering of the *praseka* libation.
"One should throw it into the fire," says Baudhāyana; "one should not throw it into the fire," says Śālīki.
(22.10:132.9) Regarding the cooking of the *brahmaudana* rice porridge: [the rule is as follows].
"One should cook it as at the establishment of the sacred fires," says Baudhāyana;
"in this very [manner]," says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the *brahmaudana* rice porridge.
Baudhāyana says that they should eat at the northern end of the buttocks; Śālīki says [they should eat] on both sides of the tail itself.
The oblation for those named after the wind.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should offer even to the wind here with the hollowed palms, says Śālīki;
one should offer from a vessel made of a black antelope skin, says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the throwing-in of the Śākala chips, [the view] of the Śākalas is as follows.
"One should throw it into the fire," says Baudhāyana; "one should not throw it into the fire," says Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the fire-hearths (*agnidhiṣṇiya*).
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should lay down all of them with the formulas of the Yajurveda.
"The sowing of various seeds."
Baudhāyana says that one should touch [the offering] after following it with the pouring out;
Śālīki says that one should complete each respective oblation as it stands.
(22.11:133.4) For them, he causes the call for the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*) to be raised over the rice alone; they then take up the barley.
Śālīki holds that the Sūtra [is correct].

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "From the pouring [of the grain] onwards, the ritual action accompanied by mantras should be repeated for each portion of barley; however, the call to the *haviṣkṛt* should be performed as a single, common procedure (*tantra*)."
Regarding the pouring out of the water for the consecration.
Baudhāyana says that one should pour out [the water] for the Āpyas behind the Gārhapatya fire; Śālīki says that one should pass beyond it in front;
Aupamanyava says that one may do so either in front or behind.
(22.11:133.10) He should cut off the *iḍā* from the other oblations together with the animal-cake, or from half [of them], or he should cut it from those [oblations] together with the animal-cakes.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the term "atyākramaṇa" (stepping across).
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should step across together with the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
(22.11:133.15) Regarding "consecration": [it refers to] the ritual sprinkling.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should consecrate [the sacrificer] before the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering according to what has been prescribed; here there is no black antelope skin, no two gold plates, and no *pārtha* offerings. Having merely spread out *kuśa* grass, one should consecrate him upon them."
"Liberation within yoga."
"One should yoke [the fires] day by day and release them day by day," says Baudhāyana; "One should yoke them day by day and release them at the end," says Śālīki;
"One should yoke them only at the beginning and release them at the end," says Aupamanyava.
"The performance of the sacrifice," [he said].
The rule is Baudhāyana’s;
Śālīki says that one should perform the ritual acts for this [sacrifice] according to the specific kratu itself.
Regarding the dedication of the eleven animals.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should dedicate the eleven animals to a single sacrificial post.
This is the supplementary offering for the omenta.
"One should offer oblations around each of those," says Baudhāyana;
"at the beginning and at the end," says Śālīki.
(22.12:134.14) "The smelling of the horse."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki, however, says that one should have the horse smell [the offering] only at the midday pressing.
Regarding the settling of the sacrificial animals.
Baudhāyana says that one should set down the fivefold oblation for each individual animal;
Śālīki says it should be only for the principal one.
(22.12:134.18) Regarding the removal of the heart-spikes: [the rule is as follows].
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki.
Regarding the curdled milk (*āmikṣā*), [the question is] whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
"It should be accompanied by mantras and fit for being cut off," says Baudhāyana; "it should be silent and fit for being cut off," says Śālīki;
"it should be accompanied by mantras, and one should sacrifice with it after having performed the *tantra*-transfer and the *nirūḍha* [offering]," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the performance of the oblations to the Devikās: [the rule is as follows].
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Vājapeya sacrifice.
"One should pile the fire at the Vājapeya," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not pile it," says Śālīki.
(22.13:135.10) A chariot wheel made of udumbara wood with seventeen spokes.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should make it from a *dārḍhya* tree.
"Prepare a split post made of Khadira wood, bound with leather thongs."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should also prepare here a goat-skin and a piece of gold weighing a śatamāna.
He undergoes initiation during the final days of summer, prior to the full moon of Āṣāḍhā.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should sacrifice with the Vājapeya in autumn.
The oblation of the Sāvitra formulas.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The mixing of the *surā* liquor belonging to the *vājapeya* sacrifice."
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should have [the materials] brought from wherever the *surā* might be.
He ties the loops of the bow at intervals of one cubit each, or he winds them around.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The caṣāla is made of wheat."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should also prepare [cakes] from wheat flour.
(22.13:136.9) "The fastening of the drums."
This sūtra is indeed twofold.
(22.13:136.10) "The performance of the sacrifice."
Śālīki holds that this is the sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should also enter upon the *kratú* of the *atirātra* here, and one should cause it to be completed within the same fortnight."
"He draws five *atigrāhya* cups for Indra."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki holds that all of these must be drawn with their respective *upayāma* vessels.
Regarding the taking of the cups of *surā* liquor.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that one should wipe the vessels while they are still together and then set them down; Śālīki says they should be set down after being wiped.
He stretches it out towards the north with two or three rows.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"One should approach the sacrificial post having taken six ropes," says Baudhāyana; "one should approach the sacrificial post having taken five ropes," says Śālīki;
"one should approach the sacrificial post having taken four ropes," says Aupamanyava.

(22.14:137.5) One should take up only a single cord and proceed toward the sacrificial post, says Aupamanyavīputra. One should fasten [the animal] to the very cord used for the Agniṣomīya sacrifice, says Āñjīgavi.
(22.14:137.8) [This concerns] the dedication of the animals belonging to the Vājapeya sacrifice.
Having consecrated the animals of the set of eleven, one should then consecrate those belonging to the Vājapeya, says Baudhāyana;
one should consecrate only those belonging to the Vājapeya and not those of the set of eleven, says Śālīki.
The introductory rite for the animals dedicated to Prajāpati.
Baudhāyana says that one should dedicate them one by one; Śālīki says that one should dedicate them all together.
(22.14:137.13) This is the supplementary oblation for the omenta.
"One should offer oblations for each of those [verses]," says Baudhāyana;
"at the beginning and at the end," says Śālīki.
(22.14:137.15) [The ritual] for the removal of the heart-spikes.
Baudhāyana says that one should remove them one by one; Śālīki says that one should remove them all together.
(22.14:137.17) "The yoking of the chariots."

Śālīki says that one should use the Sūtra [as prescribed]. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first employ that mantra which is used for the simultaneous throwing down [of the yokes], and then one should silently throw down the horses."
(22.14:137.20) "The arrival at the limit."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having turned clockwise, they should go to this goal; then they should turn back from there by moving away from the center. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having turned away from the center, they should go to this goal; then they should turn clockwise from there."
Then he causes the sacrificer to put on a garment of silk cloth.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should cause the sacrificer to put on both of these garments.
"Having resorted to a basis," so it is said.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
It takes ten eons for one to ascend it.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should descend with these very same mantras.
At this point, he places a stool for him from the time of the descent.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki, however, says that one should descend from this [chariot] with both a goat-skin and a hundred-measure weight of gold.
Then they carry him to the Sadas on this very seat, or he goes there himself.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the *atigrāhya* cups.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
Regarding the consumption of the portions belonging to Prajāpati.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
"In the third from the anus."
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that the *upayaṣṭṛ* should offer two additional oblations (*upayaja*) for each of the two [sets], with the third being the *guda*.
Śālīki says they should be offered one after another.
Aupamanyava says that having thrown all of them into the fire together, he should consecrate them with all the formulas.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Rājasūya sacrifice.
"One should pile the fire-altar at the Rājasūya," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not pile it," says Śālīki.
"Baudhāyana says that one should pour [the grains] out again, grind them, and then have them brought;
Śālīki says that they should remain exactly as they were poured out."
(22.16:139.15) Regarding the mantra or non-mantra of the Nairṛta [offering]:
Baudhāyana says that [the sacrificer] should be accompanied by the mantra; Śālīki says it should be done silently.
(22.16:139.17) "Regarding the carrying of a single firebrand."
"One should carry [the fire] from the *anvāhāryapacana*," says Baudhāyana;
"from the village fire," says Śālīki.
"The oblation for Nairṛta."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s:
one should offer it after enclosing it with two loose blades of grass, says Śālīki.
Regarding the giving of the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
"One should offer [the oblation] day after day," says Baudhāyana;
"both at the beginning and at the end," says Śālīki.
Regarding the pouring of water from a vessel: [it is done] by pouring it near [the head].
"One should pour it out while moving clockwise," says Baudhāyana;
"as may be convenient," says Śālīki.
(22.16:140.5) "Svāhā! Homage to him who has done this! Thus.
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki, however, says that one should carry the *svāhākāra* through to the very end here as well.
Regarding the application of the *saṃtanī* [oblations] in succession.

Baudhāyana used to say: "On whatever day one should sacrifice with an *iṣṭi* or with an animal sacrifice, on that very day one should employ the *saṃtanī* [oblations]. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Indeed, these two are seen to serve the purpose of the daily *āśrāvaṇa* call; therefore, on whatever day one should sacrifice with an *iṣṭi* or with an animal sacrifice, one should not employ the *saṃtanī* on that day."
The performance of the Cāturmāsya sacrifices follows in succession.

Baudhāyana used to say: "On whichever day one performs the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, on that very day one should also perform the Saṃtanī. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "These two [offerings] are indeed seen to serve the purpose of the *āśrāvaṇa* call day after day;
therefore, on whichever day one performs the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, on that day one should not perform the Saṃtanī."
The performance of the Pañcedhmīya has been explained.
Then, with the upaveṣa, he sweeps together the embers.
Śālīki prescribes the Sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having silently gathered the embers together, one should then offer oblations over them with the *sruva*-ladle using five [mantras], beginning with: ‘To Agni, the slayer of demons, svāhā!
At this point, one should give away a chariot drawn by a *praṣṭi* horse."
(22.17:141.1) There is an oblation of *apāmārga* groats.
Śālīki says that one should recite the *sūtra* [as given].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer the groats of *apāmārga* for him with the entire mantra;
one should then throw the *sruva*-ladle after it silently."
He should rise silently.
(22.17:141.4) Regarding the performance of the offerings to the Devikās: |||
The rule is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should perform the offerings in succession for each Soma sacrifice. Āñjīgavi says that one should not sacrifice with the Devikā oblations.
"Relinquishing [the fires] by means of the sacred fires."
"One should conclude with the unceasing [fires]," says Baudhāyana;
"having consigned them into the two kindling woods," says Śālīki.
"The pouring together of the milk."
Baudhāyana says that one should pour [the water] into a leather bag or a wooden trough; Śālīki says it should be poured into a new water-jar.
"In those cases where [the work] was done by oneself."
Śālīki says that one should use *sūtra* grass.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should bind the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) from *kuśa* grass crushed by the hooves of cattle, and the fuel-wood (*idhma*) from wood that has fallen of its own accord. Whatever is the form of the altar (*vedi*), that itself shall be the altar."
Having placed either a leather bag or a hollow gourd on the chariot, he should drive around;
whatever fresh butter might spill there, that shall serve as the clarified butter (ājya).
(22.17:141.16) "The offering of the oblation to Mitra and Bṛhaspati."
Baudhāyana says that there should be four handfuls for each [of the two].
Śālīki says that there should be four handfuls separately for each.
"On a red hide."
The sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says it may even be one that has not been mounted.
Regarding the purchase of the Soma, Baudhāyana says that the regular [cows] should be included in the hundred;
Śālīki says that these very [cows] should constitute the hundredth.
Regarding the drawing of the *vasatīvarī* waters.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that one should also take the Sarasvatī waters as the Vasatīvarī waters here.
"The animal for Indra-Agni is to be seized as an additional offering after the one for Agni."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki maintains that the *savanīya* offering should indeed be dedicated to Indra and Agni.
(22.18:142.11) Regarding the making of bowls: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana says that one should have the vessels made according to their specific distinctions;
Śālīki says that these should be exactly as prescribed in the archetype.
(22.18:142.13) The supplementary oblation for the Sarasvatī offerings.
Śālīki says that one should offer the oblation with the *sūktam*.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "With those two *ṛc*s with which one offers over the flowing waters, one should offer at each *graha*;
then one should offer the *sārasvatī* offerings silently."
This concerns the drawing of the cups for the consecration rites.
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should draw the cups for the consecration before the Sadas.
Regarding the gift of a bow.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the potsherds for the cake on twenty-one potsherds dedicated to the Maruts: [the procedure is as follows].
Baudhāyana says that after laying down the bricks belonging to the iṣṭi, one should lay them down in groups;
Śālīki says they should be laid down only in groups.
(22.18:143.4) "Regarding the *āmikṣā*: [is it] with a mantra or without a mantra?"
"It should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana;
"it should be silent," says Śālīki.
"The place of a eunuch," [it is said].
Baudhāyana says that one should stand within the altar; Śālīki says that one should stand outside the altar.
(22.19:143.8) Regarding the fashioning of jewels: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana says that it should be made of udumbara wood and covered with an iron [ring] of udumbara;
Śālīki says it should be made of udumbara wood alone.
Upon that chariot-stand, together with the charioteer, he places the chariot.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that there should be only one charioteer for those who establish the fires.
(22.19:143.12) Regarding the handing over of the wooden sword (sphya).
Śālīki holds that there is a scriptural rule [to this effect].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should hand over [the vessel] to the sacrificer alone with the mantra; the others should hand it over silently."
Regarding the "manufacture of dice."
"They should be made of gold," says Baudhāyana; "of silver," says Śālīki;
"of ivory," says Aupamanyava.
"They are made of vibhītaka wood," says Aupamanyavīputra.
(22.19:143.18) Then, having cut off five dice, he hands them over to him.
Śālīki holds that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Whatever part of it might not have been performed, one should supply that there as well, [reciting] 'This king has come toward the quarters.'"
(22.19:144.3) Now, at the Viṣuvat [day], he offers an oblation upon a bunch of darbha grass.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that [the sacrificer] should go to wherever there may be a clump of darbha grass; Śālīki says he should go to that very place where the clump of darbha grass is.
Regarding the carrying away of the fires.
"One should carry the fires continuously," says Baudhāyana;
"having consigned them into the two kindling woods," says Śālīki.
(22.20:144.8) "Regarding the preparation of the altar."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that the sacrificial altar should be successively larger than the preceding one.
Then, having brought him from the bathing place and purified him, he leads forth the one wearing a lotus-fiber girdle.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should have both kinds of *puṇḍarīka* lotuses made—both those of gold and those grown in water; Śālīki, however, says they should be only those grown in water.
They set aside for him this remnant of the oblation as his portion of the vow.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should not place the remnants of the oblation here as a portion for the vow-food.
Regarding the purchase of Soma, Baudhāyana says that the regular [offerings] should be performed;
Śālīki says that only these [specific offerings] should be performed.
(22.20:145.1) Regarding the oblations for the *aupasadā* rites, there is the question of whether they are accompanied by mantras or are mantra-less.
Baudhāyana says that they should be accompanied by mantras; Śālīki says they should be silent.
"For the animal dedicated to Agni, a hornless goat dedicated to Prajāpati is to be offered as an additional victim."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki maintains that the *savanīya* animal sacrifice should belong exclusively to Prajāpati.
"The Hotṛ priest is a descendant of Bhṛgu."
Baudhāyana says that one should choose a Bhārgava as the Hotṛ from the very beginning;
Śālīki says that the Hotṛ should be a Bhārgava only at the Daśapeya sacrifice.
"A hundred Brahmins drink," they say.
Baudhāyana says that the sacrificer should be the one hundred and first;
Śālīki says that the sacrificer alone should be the hundredth.
Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
"Baudhāyana says that one should give these very same sacrificial fees as prescribed for a Brāhmaṇa;
Śālīki says that this [set] is the face of the thousand."
"In their risings," [it is said].
"They should go [with the fires] as far as the *āvabhṛtha*," says Baudhāyana;
"as far as the *apsuṣoma*," says Śālīki;
"as far as the *dhruva*," says Aupamanyava.
Having sacrificed each oblation, he pours clarified butter over the offering to Bṛhaspati.
Having sacrificed to the one belonging to Bṛhaspati, one should pour the clarified butter over the offering for Bṛhaspati; thus says Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that this applies only to the other oblations, but not to the one for Bṛhaspati.
One calls for the *āśrāvaṇa* loudly for the offering to Āditya, and in a whisper for that to the Maruts.

Baudhāyana says that from the *āśrāvaṇa* of the Āditya offering onwards, it is whispered (*upāṃśu*), while the rest is loud (*uccais*). Śālīki says that from the *āśrāvaṇa* of the Māruta offering onwards, it is whispered, while the rest is loud. Aupamanyava says that the Āditya offering is entirely loud, and the Māruta offering is entirely whispered.
"Among the Sātyadūtas."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should simply say: "So-and-so has sent this to you."
"The two-night sacrifice," [he said].
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that on the day of sacrifice, the preceding day is the first [rite] and the following day is the second.
(22.21:146.11) Regarding the performance of the oblations to the Devikās:
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the ritual procedure for the bricks.
Baudhāyana used to say that there should be fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should have the *vārtraghna* formulas, and the deities should be announced loudly.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that there should be seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should have the *vṛdhanvant* formulas, and the deities should be announced in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
"The performance [of the ritual] is for the sake of the sacrificer."
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the duties of the sacrificer (*yājamāna*) in their entirety according to the path of the *iṣṭi* sacrifice;
Śālīki says that one should perform the duties of the sacrificer as far as the occasion permits.
"One who, being a regular performer of the New and Full Moon sacrifices, should omit either the new moon day or the full moon day, shall offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pathikṛt."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having offered the *pāthikṛt* cake, one should subsequently offer a *vaiśvānara* cake on twelve potsherds; then one should perform the expiation for the transgression. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having offered the *pāthikṛt* cake, one should subsequently offer the *vaiśvānara* cake on twelve potsherds as part of the same ritual procedure (*samānatantra*), and one should not perform the expiation for the transgression separately.
Aupamanyava says: "One should perform the expiation for the transgression together with either one of the two offerings."
Regarding this, Añjīgavi used to say: "The sacrifice of one whose ritual procedure (*tantra*), once extended, is extended by another ritual procedure, is indeed torn asunder.

One should therefore perform that very unshakable cake on eight potsherds for Agni as the *pāthikṛt* offering on either the full moon or the new moon day; one should not perform a compensatory sacrifice (*pratiyajet*) for what has already passed."
"One who, having established the sacred fires, should act as if contrary to his vows, should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vratapati. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana says that this has been stated as beginning from the very time of the fire-laying;
Śālīki says it is when the fires have been both formally established and fully kindled.
"One whose dwelling is beset by demons should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, the slayer of demons. Thus [it is said].
Having offered the Agnihotra, one should conclude the Iṣṭi, says Baudhāyana;
when the Iṣṭi has been concluded, one should offer the Agnihotra, says Śālīki.
"One practicing exorcism should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni accompanied by Rudra. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana used to say that the officiating priests should proceed wearing red turbans and red garments;
Śālīki, however, says that this is already expressed by the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses themselves.
"One whose cattle or men have died, or who is afraid, should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Surabhimat. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana used to say that they should throw fragrant substances into the *prokṣaṇī* waters and that the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) should perform their duties while possessing fragrance;
Śālīki, however, says that this is already expressed by the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses themselves.
"One whose desire does not come to pass should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana used to say: "If the desire for which [the offering] is prescribed there should not be fulfilled when they perform that [offering], then one should act in this manner.
Śālīki says: "This very [offering] should be the one for all desires.
Aupamanyava says: "It may be for each individual desire."
"One whose fire, having been taken out, should go out before the Agnihotra has been offered, should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Jyotiṣmat. Thus [it is said].
Śālīki holds that the *sūtra* [is authoritative].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should recite these mantras: "the churning," "the further churning," and "the kindling."
"One should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara when a son is born. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana used to say that when the ten-day period has passed, one should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara and have the child lick the remnants of the oblation.
Śālīki says that this should be done as soon as [the child] is born, and that one should not have the child lick the remnants of the oblation.
Aupamanyava says it should be done at the next full-moon or new-moon festival.
"The two oblations were inverted."
Baudhāyana says that the Mārutas should receive the first mantra-rite;
Śālīki says [it should be] from the portioning out (avadāna); Aupamanyava says [it should be] from the offering (pradāna).
Aupamanyavīputra says [the rule applies] from the *cātuṣprāśya* onwards.
"One should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara after having gone to his dwelling place. Thus [it is said].
(23.2:149.12) "The place where he intends to go shall be the sacrificial site.
Having gone there, he should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara," says Baudhāyana.
"In his own established fire-places," says Śālīki.
"With that same rope by which one might drive away the best cow," so it is said.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should simply say: "This person here has sent this to you."
"One should bind balbaja grass to the fuel-bundle. Thus [it is said].
The rule is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that even grasses of the *balbaja* species may be tied together here as sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
"One practicing exorcism should offer a cake on eleven potsherds dedicated to Agni and Viṣṇu. Thus [it is said].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says it is only after one has recognized that the person is practicing sorcery against him.
"The clarified butter belongs to Sarasvatī."
Baudhāyana says that this clarified butter should be poured out with a mantra; Śālīki says it should be done silently;
Aupamanyava says that one should take it from the *dhruvā* ladle at each respective time.
"In the *Adhvarakalpā*," so it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should perform the first ritual procedure ending with the *iḍā*; likewise the second; and one should carry forward the remainder together with the third.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should let the remnants of the first ritual procedure remain until the [oblations] have been led forward;
likewise for the second, and likewise for the third."
"One should carry forward the remainder together with the third [portion]," says Aupamanyava; "the full-vessel rite and the Viṣṇu-strides [should follow]."

"For one who should desire the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*), for him he should offer this *caru* oblation to Soma and Rudra on the full moon day of the month of Tiṣya. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana says that one should offer [the oblation] on the day of the fast (upavasatha);
Śālīki says it should be on the day of sacrifice (yajaniya).
"The clarified butter is for sprinkling; they purify themselves with clarified butter."
Baudhāyana says that one should throw the water-pot into the ladle containing the clarified butter (*ājya*).
Śālīki says that one should perform both the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*) and the purification (*mārjana*) with clarified butter, while performing everything else with water.
Aupamanyava says that whatever must be done with water, all of that should be done with clarified butter.
(23.2:151.7) "If one should fear, 'I shall become afflicted with skin disease,' he should offer a sacrificial pap (caru) to Soma and Pūṣan. Thus it is said.
Baudhāyana says that one should offer [the oblation] when the forms have been recognized;
Śālīki says that one should do so even before, while still apprehensive.
"In the halves," it is said.
Baudhāyana says that when the sacrifice has been completed, one should add fuel to half [of the fires]. Śālīki says that they should remain lying there right where they are.
"The two oblations were inverted."
Baudhāyana says that the Mārutas should first receive the mantra-rite;
Śālīki says [it should be] from the portioning out; Aupamanyava says [it should be] from the offering.
"Aupamanyavīputra says [it should be done] after the fourfold tasting."
"The Hotṛ performs the offering with the two verses addressed to the Maruts."
Baudhāyana used to say that the Hotṛ should invoke the Maruts from the very beginning, while the Adhvaryu should do so during the recitation;
Śālīki, however, says that this is already expressed by the *yājyā* and *puro’nuvākyā* verses themselves.
"One desiring prosperity should offer a caru-oblation to the Ādityas who are accompanied by the word *bhuvat*."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "All [the rites] should have their footprints; all should have the Sāvitrī; and all should have the sacrificial grass and fuel together."
(23.3:151.21) Regarding the removal of the dust from the footprints.
Śālīki says that one should [use] the sūtra [as stated].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having removed the dust from the footprints with the entire mantra, one should pour it out in the northern section;
then, one should lead it silently across the chest."
"There are one hundred gold *kṛṣṇala*s," they say.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that these [cups] should indeed be "near-a-hundred" (upaśata), and one should also exclude them.
"He cuts off four *kṛṣṇala* berries at a time for each portion, in order to obtain the fourfold cutting. Thus it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Those portions that have already been cut out, one should simply offer them. As for those intended for consumption, they should remain held apart. Then, the others they should divide into equal shares."

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Those portions which have been cut off, one should indeed offer them. But those which are intended for consumption, they should remain held apart. Then, having poured the other portions into the *prāśitraharaṇa* vessel, one should hand it over to the Brahman."
"For one who may be seized by *pāpayakṣman* (evil consumption), he should offer this *āditya-caru* on the new moon day. Thus [it is said].
Baudhāyana says that one should offer [the oblation] on the day of the Upavasatha;
Śālīki says it should be on the day of sacrifice.
(23.3:153.1) [The rule applies] to the enclosing sticks of the Sāṃgrahaṇī sacrifice.

Baudhāyana says that one should enclose [the fire] with the implements used for the iṣṭi sacrifice and then enclose it with those used for the puroḍāśa sacrifice; Śālīki says that one should do so only with the implements used for the iṣṭi sacrifice.
The offering of oblations.
Śālīki holds that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer these oblations with vessels made of Udumbara wood; having offered them, one should throw those very vessels right here into the fire."
Regarding the inspection of the clarified butter: [the rule is as follows].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"That which was new became fresh butter (*navanīta*). Śālīki says that one should purify the clarified butter (*ājya*) with these very [verses] after it has been inspected.
"For as many horses as he may receive, so many four-potsherd offerings to Varuṇa should he prepare, with one additional."
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should accept a single [gift] with the Vaiśvānara [offering];
likewise two;
but having accepted a group, one should perform [the rite] with Varuṇa offerings, exceeding by one when there are many."
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should accept a single gift from Vaiśvānara, but not two;
having accepted a group [of gifts], one should perform the rite, but not for two or for many—[offering] the Vāruṇa oblations with one additional cake."
Regarding the curdled milk (*āmikṣā*), there is the question of whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
"It should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana;
"it should be silent," says Śālīki.
He sweeps it again; having swept it, he cuts off the portions.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should collect [the portions] together with these very same mantras and then cut off [the portions].
He offers a sacrificial cake on thirty-three potsherds.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki, however, says that this should be only when the sacrificial cake is doubtful.
The supplementary oblation is performed with a stalk of *varṣāhū* grass.
The rule of Baudhāyana is that [one should go] where there is a clump of *varṣāhū* grass; Śālīki says that one should go to whichever such clump may be found.
(23.4:154.9) Regarding the shaking out of the black antelope skin.
Baudhāyana says that one should shake out the black antelope skin while standing within the altar;
Śālīki says [one should do so] outside the altar.
"The performance of the Kārīrī [offering] for one who effects immediate rain."
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"In the case of contact, there shall be the performance of penance."
The Sūtra belongs to the two teachers.
Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "That which is indeed the Āhavanīya fire is from that very source that this [Gārhapatya] is drawn forth;
the Anvāhāryapacana has the village as its source."
In each such case, there is no expiation,
for the contact with fire for a futile purpose is indeed praised.
Thus, indeed, these sacrifices have been explained.
"One offers while stepping forward."
"To what extent, indeed, has this been stated?"
"There are five fore-offerings," says Baudhāyana;
"those which take place before the shed," says Śālīki.
If the portion of the animal victim should be lost, one should take a substitute portion from the clarified butter.

Baudhāyana used to say: "If a portion of the animal victim should be lost—whether it be one or two—one should perform an offering with clarified butter as a substitute, and having performed that, one should sacrifice again.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If a portion of the animal victim should be lost—whether it be one or two—one should perform an offering with clarified butter as a substitute; having performed that, one should consider the matter settled.
But if more than that [is lost], then one should act in this manner [as Baudhāyana prescribed]."

Baudhāyana says that wherever there may be a navigable river or a stream flowing between two mountains, it is a place where the *saṃsava* (the simultaneous hearing of the sound of the *śastras*) does not occur. Śālīki says that wherever sounds do not mingle, it is a place where the *saṃsava* does not occur.
Aupamanyava says that wherever one might pass through [such a space], it is a place where the *saṃsava* does not occur.
Aupamanyavīputra says that the *saṃsava* occurs there between two neighboring countries.
Āñjīgavi says that the *Chāgaleya Brāhmaṇa* states: "There is no *saṃsava* between two who do not hate each other."
The oblation of the Abhibhūtis.
Baudhāyana says that after performing the *ādhvara* oblations, one should perform the *sāttvāyaṇika* oblations; Śālīki says that one should perform only the *sāttvāyaṇika* oblations.
(23.5:156.6) "When they have broken out and set forth."
Śālīki says that one should use the *sūtra* [as prescribed].
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "With those two verses with which one would offer into the *pūtabhṛt* and *ādhavanīya* vessels, one should offer at each *graha*;
then one should pour out the residue silently."
Regarding the permanent taking up [of the vessel], one recites the verse addressed to Viṣṇu.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki, however, maintains that this [offering] must be performed using only the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya).
Having responded to each *uktha* with the formula, he says: "O reciter of the *uktha*," at each pressing (*savana*). Or [he may say this] at every pressing.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the drawing of the Pṛṣṭhya cups.
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Whenever these days might coincide, one should indeed take the Pṛṣṭhya cups there;
for these [days] are seen to belong to the year itself."
Aupamanyava says that one should take them at the end of the year itself.
Regarding the consumption of the Pṛṣṭhya cups.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should consume them both with the consumption formula recited at each pressing and with the regular formula;
Śālīki, however, says it should be with the regular formula alone.
"For the strengthening of the stalks."
"One should pull them out one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki.
"Shaking [the grains]," he said.
"One should shake [the grass] crosswise," says Baudhāyana;
"in the manner of a fan," says Śālīki;
"one should stir [it]," says Aupamanyava.
"The oblation of the portion."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "With those two verses with which one should touch [the water], with those two one should offer it;
then one should touch [the water] silently."
Regarding the drawing of the *pṛśni* cups: [the rule is as follows].
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"Therefore, one should burn the undergrowth."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one may even burn down the thicket here with a cake alone.
"The bull grows old among the cows."
Śālīki holds that this is the rule of the Sūtra.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Even if one should immolate another animal outside the ritual procedure (*tantra*), one should perform these same rites for it—namely, for the two introductory offerings, for the omentum, and for the deities."
(23.6:158.1) "The oblation of fat from the embryo is performed with eight-footed verses."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: “One should not offer the fat-oblation of the embryo,” says Śālīki.
“One should neither offer the fat-oblation of the embryo, nor the iḍā, nor the sviṣṭakṛt,” says Aupamanyava.
(23.7:158.4) The introductory rite for the Ajavaśā cow.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should dedicate it with a verse addressed to Vāyu.
Regarding this, the elder Kātyāyana used to say: "Just as at the initial dedication one pushes forward the act of dedication, so too should the subsequent mantras be pushed forward."
When, after she has been seized, a cloud appears.
Baudhāyana used to say: "If there are clouds that are not black at the end of the day, one should indeed complete the sacrifice;
but if they should be black, then one should act in this manner.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If they should not obscure the sun, one should indeed complete the sacrifice."
If they should conceal him, he should act in this manner; Gautama maintains that there is no suspension of the rite until [the victim] has been seized.
(23.7:158.13) "In the victories," [he says].
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"In the *abhyātāna* [offerings]," so it is said.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana.

Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should offer these as spoon-oblations—the Abhyātānas, the Jayas, and the Rāṣṭrabhṛts—and thus the New and Full Moon sacrifices would be attended by the Abhyātānas, the Jayas, and the Rāṣṭrabhṛts."
"On the *śamyā* and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*s)," [it is said].
Baudhāyana says that one should make the enclosing-sticks of Śamyā out of Śamyā wood;
Śālīki says that these should be of the same kind as those used in the archetype sacrifice.
One offers the Rāṣṭrabhṛt oblations twice with the utterance of svāhā.
"One should offer the oblations with distinct pauses," says Baudhāyana;
"two spoonfuls at a time," says Śālīki.
"One offers on the gaming board; one offers at the front of the chariot; one offers on the pole of the chariot."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that these [vessels] should belong to the fires themselves.
"The sacrificial fuel consists of wood from the Nyagrodha, Udumbara, Aśvattha, and Plakṣa trees."
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: one should anoint these fuel-sticks separately and place them on the fire separately; thus says Śālīki.
"Whatever is harsh in speech, with that he utters the vaṣaṭ-call."
The Sūtra is that of Śālīki.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should offer curd-mixture mixed with alkaline salt together with an Arka leaf,
and one should utter the *vaṣaṭ* call as either "jahi" or "kaḍ."
(23.7:160.1) "Procreation," he says.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should impel [the horse] with both, namely with the verses addressed to Vasiṣṭha and with the verse addressed to Savitṛ; Śālīki says it should be done with the verse addressed to Savitṛ alone.
"In cases where [the rules] have been transgressed."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"In the *atimokṣas*," it is said.
The former ritual procedure is that of Śālīki; the latter is that of Baudhāyana.
"The grasping of the Prāṇagrahas."
The Sūtra is Baudhāyana’s: "These have been seen as occurring within the year;
one should take them within the year," says Śālīki.
(23.8:160.9) "Having milked her, one should give [the milk] to a Brahmin whose food one would not otherwise eat. Thus it is said.
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "If he should sit down before the formal inquiry [into the sacrifice], then he should act in this manner."
"If the Gārhapatya fire should go out while the Āhavanīya has not yet gone out," so it is said.
The Sūtra [is] that of Śālīki.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: having poured this entire fire into a vessel, having carried it around to the south of the sacrificial ground, having removed the ashes from the site of the Gārhapatya fire, having smeared it with a lump of cow-dung, having piled it up and added fuel, and having drawn out the flaming Āhavanīya fire, one should remove the ashes from the site of the Āhavanīya, smear it with a lump of cow-dung, pile it up and add fuel; then, when the Āhavanīya is provided with fuel-sticks, one should offer six spoonfuls [of oblations], [reciting]: "Awake, O Agni... "You... [and so forth].
"O Agni, you are far-extending; may the mind, the light, enjoy [the offering]; stretching out the thread; up that one; the bright one."
"In the case of Soma sacrifices where there is an excess," so it is said.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
When the *dhruva* ladle has been displaced, there is the performance of an expiation (*prāyaścitta*).

Baudhāyana used to say: "If, before the final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), the Sāman-singers and the Bahvṛcas should obtain [the opportunity], they should repeat the Stotras and Śastras; having done that, one should sacrifice again. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If, before the final purificatory bath, the Sāman-singers and the Bahvṛcas should obtain [the opportunity], they should repeat the Stotras and Śastras; having done that, one should consider the rite as already accomplished."
Regarding the phrase "the grasping of days."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that they should draw the cups beginning with the one for Mitra and Varuṇa on whichever day immediately follows.
(23.8:161.12) Regarding the performance of an expiation when the sacrificial post has sprouted.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should perform the expiation when the sacrificial post has grown over while the ritual procedure is still in progress.
"If one's Soma should run out, he should split a piece of gold into two parts; he should shake one part onto the *ṛjīṣa* and offer the other as a libation. Thus it is said.
The rule is Baudhāyana’s: from this point forward, the principal cups should be offered and refilled while containing gold. Śālīki says they should be offered and refilled without gold.
"In the case of the Ādārasoma sacrifices," so it is said.
The rule is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that they may also cause another [Soma] to be brought by means of an Ādārasoma.
Regarding the blessings.
Baudhāyana says that the benedictions should follow [the formulas];
Śālīki says that these very [formulas] themselves should constitute the benedictions.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the twelve-day sacrifice.
"One should pile the fire-altar during the twelve-day sacrifice," says Baudhāyana;
"one should not pile it," says Śālīki.
"The additional cups" (atigrāhya).
Baudhāyana used to say that the householder alone should consign [the fires] into the two kindling woods;
"this constitutes the form of the *atigrāhya* cup," he said.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that they should consign them separately into their respective kindling woods; having churned the fire for the first one, the householder, they should release the blazing fires even while they are still blazing.
"This is the form of the *atigrāhya* cup."
(23.9:162.11) "The pouring together."

Baudhāyana used to say that those intending to pour the fires together should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni accompanied by the Brahman, to Agni accompanied by the Kṣatra, and to Agni the bearer of the Kṣatra.
Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that this sacrifice is indeed for the purpose of joining the fires; therefore, one should offer it at the very place where one intends to pile the fire-altar.
Aupamanyava says that one should follow the animal-cake offering dedicated to Prajāpati.
"Pavana" means wind.

Baudhāyana says that they should purify them one by one and then draw them up one by one; Śālīki says that they should purify them all at once and then draw them up one by one; Aupamanyava says that they should purify them all at once and then draw them all up together.
Regarding the selection of the ancestral lineage (*ārṣeyavaraṇa*).

Baudhāyana used to say: "If there are any who are of the same *gotra* and not separated [by another lineage], even if they belong to different *gotras*, their selection should be considered as the selection of a single *ṛṣi*-lineage. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Whether they are separated or not separated, if they are of the same *gotra*, their selection should be considered as the selection of a single *ṛṣi*-lineage."
"Milk for the vow! he says.
Baudhāyana says that they should milk together and divide the portions equally; Śālīki says that each of them should have a separate cow for the vow-milk.
Regarding the rule that "on the sixth day of sitting, they pile up the *uttaravedi*," the *sūtra* of the two Teachers also provides the injunction that it may be done on the eleventh day.
(23.9:164.3) Regarding the taking up of the *vasatīvarī* waters: [the rule is as follows].
Śālīki says that one should follow the Sūtra.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "If the pitcher should have a residue remaining, one should pour it out silently;
